title: Uskottava politiikka perustuu arvoihin, ei ”gallupdemokratiaan”
content:
Yhteinen käsitys on koetuksella maailmalla ja Suomessa, totesi valtiotieteiden tohtori Arja Alho TSL:n Yhteinen todellisuutemme – keskustelutilaisuudessa Porissa.

Syyskuisen torstain tilaisuudessa mietittiin Alhon alustamana, millainen on kansalaisyhteiskunta, joka on aina demokratian pohja.

Demokratiaan kuuluu, että kaikki pidetään mukana ja kaikki oppivat. Ihmiset ovat yhdenvertaisia ja heillä on yhdenvertainen pääsy tiedon lähteille.

Poliittinen toiminta on uskottavaa silloin, kun se lähtee arvoista ja ymmärryksestä, ei ”gallupdemokratiasta.”

Median muutos on Alhon mukaan suuri. Lehdistössä on vähemmän vaihtoehtoja ja somen algoritmit rakentuvat markkinaehtoisesti. Ne myös voivat johtaa hyvin haasteellisiin sisältöihin.

– Jos jokin haastaa yhteistä todellisuutta, se on joukko, johon kuuluvat esimerkiksi Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg ja Bill Gates. Noin 3000 miljardööriä hallitsee miltei 8,3 miljardin ihmisen kohtaloita, Alho muistutti.

Tarvitaan lisää vuorovaikutteista keskustelua. Vaalit ovat demokratian kuorrutus, jos pohjalla ei ole kansalaisyhteiskuntaa ja sivistystä. Tärkeistä asioista hiljaa oleminen ei vie asioita eteenpäin. Erimielistä, mutta hyvähenkistä keskustelua tarvitaan.

title: US: Deportations to Haiti Endanger Lives
content:
(Washington, DC) – Since ending Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haiti in late July 2026, US authorities have deported hundreds of Haitians back to their country, where they face threats to their lives and safety and receive little to no support, Human Rights Watch said today. The US Senate should urgently pass House-approved legislation that would reinstate TPS for Haitians.

According to Haiti’s National Office for Migration (Office National de la Migration), more than 450 people have been deported from the United States to Haiti since July. Many had lived in the United States for years and were separated from US citizen family members, while others said they had pending asylum claims in the US. Haitian authorities lack the funding, staff, and policy frameworks to safely receive and assist deportees, Haitian government officials told Human Rights Watch.

“The United States is returning people, some with pending asylum claims, to a country that doesn’t have the capacity to protect them from violence, let alone help them find food and shelter,” said Nathalye Cotrino, senior Americas researcher at Human Rights Watch. “The US government should immediately halt these removals.”

title: Vihapuhetta seksityöntekijöistä – Iiris Elena Rusin näyttely ”Myös meidän sydämet voivat särkyä” avautuu Valokuvataiteen museossa
content:
Näyttely sai kipinänsä Me Naiset -lehdessä helmikuussa 2021 julkaistusta haastattelusta, joka keskittyi Rusiin seksityöntekijänä ja kuvataiteilijana. Haastattelua jaettiin sosiaalisessa mediassa ja keskustelupalstoilla, jotka täyttyivät Rusin ulkonäköä, haluttavuutta ja moraalista toimintaa arvostelevista kommenteista. Julkaisun jälkeen Rusia lähestyi julkisella paikalla nuori mies, joka huusi tälle "Maksa veroja, huora!" ja jatkoi matkaansa hymyillen.

”Nettikirjoittelu ei synny ja elä tyhjiössä, vaan heijastaa ympäröivää yhteiskunnallista ilmapiiriä”, Rusi sanoo.

Näyttelyä varten Rusi haastatteli eri-ikäisiä ihmisiä, jotka tekevät vapaaehtoisesti ja itsenäisesti seksityötä Suomessa. Seksityöntekijöiden joukko on monenkirjava, eikä toteuta tiettyä kaavaa tai edusta tiettyä ihmistyyppiä. Seksin myyminen ja ostaminen ei ole Suomessa laitonta, mutta Suomen lainsäädäntö ei tunne termejä seksityö, seksityöntekijä tai vastikkeellinen seksi. Tämän lisäksi seksityöhön liittyy edelleen voimakas stigma.

title: Protestoimalla vaikutat, sanotaan ilmastoahdistusta poteville nuorille – Hanna Höijeriä se turhauttaa, ja siksi hän kuvaa dokumenttielokuvaa Afrikan ilmastosankareista
content:
”Fuck the politicians: jos he eivät kuuntele, niin ei sitten. Lähdetään itse tekemään tätä hommaa.” 

Se on viesti, jonka opiskelija, ilmastoaktivisti ja elokuvantekijä Hanna Höijer, 22, haluaa sukupolvelleen välittää. 

Hän on kyllästynyt siihen, että nuorille tarjotaan lääkkeeksi ilmastoahdistukseen lähes pelkästään protestointia, vaatimusten esittämistä päättäjille tai somessa toimimista. Periaatteessa se on hyvä asia, mutta samalla herkästi myös vähätellään nuorten omia kykyjä ja jätetään heidät muiden armoille, hän sanoo. 

Höijer näkee, että ihmiset jaetaan julkisessa keskustelussa ilmastonmuutoksen uhreihin ja ratkaisijoihin. Uhreja ovat nuoret, ratkaisijoita taas yleensä ”keski-ikäiset valkoiset eurooppalaiset miehet puvuissa.” 

”Tämä jaottelu häiritsee minua. Joo, nuoret ovat uhreja, mutta se ei tarkoita, etteivätkö nuoret voisi olla myös ratkaisijoita.” 

Siksi hän tekee kollegoineen parhaillaan dokumenttielokuvaa Not Done Yet, joka tuo parrasvaloihin ilmastonmuutokseen konkreettisia ratkaisuja Afrikassa kehittävät nuoret.

title: Pitkän uran tehnyt talotekniikkavaikuttaja Ilkka Salo: Tekniikan on palveltava ihmisiä ja ympäristöä
content:
Talotekniikka on muuttunut perusteellisesti niiden vuosikymmenten aikana, jotka diplomi-insinööri Ilkka Salo on viettänyt alan parissa. Putkiasentajaharjoittelijana 1980-luvulla alkanut ura kulki energia-analyyseistä ja puhdastilatekniikasta ABB:n tuotekehitykseen ja lopulta yli 20 vuoden mittaiseksi uraksi talotekniikka-alan järjestöjohtajana. Taltekan eli Talotekninen teollisuus ja kauppa ry:n toimitusjohtajana Salo toimi yhdistyksen perustamisesta vuodesta 2018 kevääseen 2026 saakka.

Lämmöllä-lehden laajassa henkilöhaastattelussa Salo nostaa esiin yhden ajatuksen, joka on kulkenut mukana läpi hänen uransa: talotekniikka ei ole ensisijaisesti laitteita, putkia, kanavia tai energiankulutusta. Sen tehtävänä on luoda ihmisille terveelliset, turvalliset ja miellyttävät olosuhteet.

– Tällä alalla tehdään konkreettisia ratkaisuja, ja sisäympäristön merkitys on valtava. Opiskeluaikoina kaikkea ei tietenkään vielä täysin sisäistänyt, mutta työn merkityksellisyys ja konkreettinen asioihin vaikuttaminen vetivät puoleensa, talotekniikkavaikuttaja Ilkka Salo kertoo.

title: Whiplashed middle powers seek new alliances as Trump rages on world stage
content:
While world leaders prepare for annual UN gathering, shifts in the global order continue in the face of a disruptive American president

In the event of a midterms election battering, it is possible that a deflated Donald Trump, constrained by a Democrat-controlled Congress, will gradually have to face up to the indignity of irrelevance.

While continuing to sign off Truth Social posts with his usual, “Thank you for your attention to this matter”, no one will actually be paying much attention. His meandering press conferences will no longer be carried live by TV networks. The Republican party will move on to the question of his successor. Trump could announce he had changed the name of the Champs-Élysées to Sunset Boulevard and even Google Maps will stifle a yawn. He would become that most pitied of political animals, the lame duck.

title: Kiusaaminen alkaa kauan ennen kuin se näyttää kiusaamiselta, sanoo tutkija
content:
Uudet tutkimustulokset osoittavat, että lasten ja nuorten keskinäiseen kiusaamiseen herätään liian myöhään. Kun asia tunnistetaan, ryhmässä on voinut olla pitkään käynnissä ilmiöitä, jotka ovat luoneet pohjan ulossulkemiselle, häirinnälle ja väkivallalle. Aikuisilla onkin keskeinen rooli varhaisessa tunnistamisessa.

"Kiusaaminen ei synny tyhjästä. Sitä edeltävät usein pienet, mutta merkitykselliset tilanteet, joissa lapset ja nuoret alkavat arvottaa, vertailla ja sulkea toisiaan ulkopuolelle. Juuri näihin hetkiin pitäisi kiinnittää nykyistä enemmän huomiota", Oulun yliopiston uuden oppituolin, nuorisotutkimuksen, professori Tuija Huuki kertoo tiedotteessa.

Tutkimus haastaa myös yleisen käsityksen siitä, että kiusaaminen johtuisi ensisijaisesti tietyistä "kiusaajista" tai "pahoista lapsista". Tulokset viittaavat siihen, että tavalliset lapset ja nuoret voivat tietyissä olosuhteissa alkaa vahingoittaa toisiaan.

Riski kasvaa erityisesti silloin, kun lasten ja nuorten väliset suhteet jäävät ilman aikuisen ohjausta.

title: Miten meillä menee? VM kertoo talousennusteensa
content:
Valtiovarainministeriö esittelee maanantaina uuden arvionsa Suomen talouden lähivuosien näkymistä.

Luvassa on vuosien 2026-2028 taloudellista kehitystä koskeva ennuste ja vuoteen 2030 ulottuva keskipitkän ajan kehitysarvio.

Suomen talous on viime aikoina ollut jälleen kasvamaan päin. Samalla kapuloita talouskasvun rattaisiin heittää sota Iranissa.

Iranin sota vaikutti kesällä olevan lähellä ratkeamista, mutta sittemmin sotiminen on jatkunut ja erityisesti polttoaineen hinta on jatkanut nousuaan, kun öljy ei kulje Hormuzinsalmen läpi totuttuun tapaan.

Erityisesti dieselin hinta on noussut viime viikkoina niin Suomessa kuin maailmallakin. Dieselin korkea hinta vaikuttaa usein suoraan myös lähes kaikkien muiden tuotteiden hintoihin, sillä kuljetusala pyörii pääasiassa dieselin voimalla.

VIIME VIIKOLLA muun muassa Etla ja Labore korjasivat aiempia talousennusteitaan ylöspäin, mutta nekin olivat varsin varovaisia arvioissaan työllisyystilanteen korjaantumisesta.

Syyskuun alussa käydyn budjettiriihen jälkeen pääministeri Petteri Orpo (kok.) kuitenkin hehkutti, kuinka suomalaisilla on pitkästä aikaa syytä luottaa parempaan huomiseen.

title: UN: Commit to Human Rights, Justice for Grave Crimes
content:
World leaders at the annual meeting of the United Nations General Assembly in New York City from September 22-28, 2026, should commit to defending human rights, Human Rights Watch said. They should counter attempts to undermine accountability for grave international crimes and the work of the UN and other vital international institutions. 

Dozens of leaders and foreign ministers from the UN’s 193 member countries will attend the General Assembly’s general debate. Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is scheduled to deliver the first speech on September 22, followed by US President Donald Trump. Others speaking on the first day include the leaders of Türkiye, France, the United Kingdom, and Japan.

“The UN and other international organizations created to protect human rights are under attack from countries that had pledged to defend them,” said Louis Charbonneau, UN director at Human Rights Watch. “All UN member countries should condemn attempts by the United States, Russia, China, and others to dismantle the international human rights system and destroy avenues for accountability for abuses.”

title: POROKYLÄN LEIPOMO SELVITTI LEIVÄN KOTIKÄYTÖN YMPÄRISTÖVAIKUTUKSET – KULUTTAJIEN TAVAT VAIKUTTAVAT SELVÄSTI PÄÄSTÖIHIN
content:
Porokylän Leipomo tilasi Karelia-ammattikorkeakoulun opinnäytetyönä toteutetun tutkimuksen, jossa selvitettiin leivän kotikäytön eli säilytyksen, voileipien valmistuksen ja hävikin ympäristövaikutuksia. Tutkimuksen teki Evelina Meski osana Sustainability Management -koulutusohjelman ylempää AMK-tutkintoa. Tulokset osoittavat, että kotikäytön vaiheen kokonaisvaikutukset ovat suhteellisen pieniä, mutta kuluttajien käyttäytymisellä on niihin selvä vaikutus.

Tutkimuksessa tarkasteltiin Porokylän Leipomon kolmea päätuoteryhmää: perinteistä ruislimppua, palaleipää ja gluteenitonta leipää. Kuluttajien säilytys-, valmistus- ja hävikkitietoja kerättiin kyselytutkimuksella, johon vastasi yhteensä 232 henkilöä. Kerättyä aineistoa käytettiin elinkaariarvioinnin (LCA) lähtötietoina, ja laskenta toteutettiin SimaPro-ohjelmistolla Ecoinvent-tietokantaa hyödyntäen.

title: Ääntenlaskenta onnistui: Putinin puolue voittaa Venäjän vaalit
content:
Venäjän valtapuolue Yhtenäinen Venäjä on voittamassa maan duuman vaalit. Asiasta kertoo Venäjän valtiollinen uutistoimisto Tass viitaten keskusvaalilautakunnan tietoihin.

Kun runsaat neljännes äänistä oli laskematta, Yhtenäinen Venäjä oli saamassa lähes 58 prosenttia äänistä. Kremlin hyväksymä oppositio eli kommunistit olivat saamassa noin 14 prosenttia ja liberaalidemokraatit lähes 9 prosenttia äänistä. Käytännössä nämäkin puolueet tukevat Venäjän nykyjohtoa.

Jos ja kun Yhtenäinen Venäjä tulee saamaan parlamenttiin kahden kolmasosan enemmistön, se voi vapaasti tehdä Vladimir Putinin haluamia muutoksia perustuslakiin. Näin yksinvaltiaan toimille saadaan näennäinen parlamentin siunaus.

Venäjän vaaleja pidetään vilpillisinä, kuten aiempiakin Venäjän vaaleja tällä vuosituhannella. Kaikki Ukraina-sotaa vastustavat puolueet menettivät vaalikelpoisuutensa jo kesällä, ja sodanvastustajiksi epäiltyjä henkilöehdokkaita on eri puolilla maata joko vangittu tai muuten poistettu ehdokaslistoilta.

Vaalit olivat ensimmäiset sen jälkeen, kun Venäjä aloitti laajamittaisen hyökkäyssodan Ukrainassa vuonna 2022.

title: AfD eteni taas osavaltiovaaleissa – liittokansleri Merzin ahdinko syvenee
content:
Saksassa radikaalioikeistolainen ja maahanmuuttovastainen Vaihtoehto Saksalle -puolue (AfD) on voittanut sunnuntaiset Mecklenburg-Etu-Pommerin osavaltiovaalit. Liittokansleri Friedrich Merzin puolue kärsi murskatappion.

Vaalien lopputuloksesta kertovat muun muassa Tageschau ja ZDF.

Alustavien lukujen mukaan AfD keräsi osavaltiossa yli 38 prosenttia äänistä. Toiseksi tullut sosiaalidemokraattinen SPD jäi vajaan kolmen prosentin päähän.

Liittokansleri Merzin kristillisdemokraattinen CDU jäi puolestaan alle viiden prosentin äänikynnyksen. Tällä tuloksella puolue putoaa ensimmäistä kertaa ulos osavaltion parlamentista.

Merz kuvaili ovensuukyselyiden jälkeen Mecklenburg-Etu-Pommerin tulosta katastrofiksi. Hän on kuitenkin vakuuttanut jatkavansa uudistuksiaan takaiskuista huolimatta.

Todennäköisemmin osavaltion johdossa jatkaa jonkinlainen SPD:n johtama koalitio, sillä muut puolueet vasemmistopopulistista BSW:tä lukuun ottamatta eivät suostu AfD:n kanssa yhteistyöhön. Venäjä-mielinen BSW jäi kuitenkin niin ikään alle äänikynnyksen.

Osavaltioparlamenttiin ylsivät myös vasemmistopuolue Linke ja vihreät.

title: More Programs Aren’t Enough: Why EduWiki Needs Stronger Infrastructure
content:
When people think about Wikimedia education work, they often think first about events: edit-a-thons, campaigns, classroom programs, contests, workshops, and training sessions. But over time, one lesson keeps becoming clearer: education work does not scale through activities alone. It scales through infrastructure.

That realization has become increasingly important for the EduWiki Hub as conversations continue around sustainability, coordination, visibility, and long-term support for Wikimedia education communities.

The Wikipedia & Education User Group is the Wikimedia Foundation’s only recognized global affiliate focused entirely on education-related Wikimedia initiatives. Its Theory of Change was designed around a central challenge: how do we help education communities grow sustainably while improving onboarding, coordination, and impact across the movement?

The answer has never been simply “run more programs.” The research behind the Theory of Change identified deeper structural needs: clearer coordination, stronger support systems, better knowledge sharing, and more reliable technical maintenance for the tools organizers depend on every day.

title: How two elections reshaped the India–Bangladesh border
content:
Push-in attempts by BSF stretch across Bangladesh’s land border, hitting all four edges of the map

Originally published on Global Voices

India–Bangladesh Friendship Gate at the Tamabil-Dawki border in northeast Bangladesh. Image via Wikipedia by Ankan. CC BY-SA 4.0.

This report features interviews and infographics by Amatullah Sumaya, Aronee Ayub, Nusaiba Nawaz, Sampoorna Ganguly, and Sayeeda Nowshin for the Data Journalism Course at the University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh.

A 55-year-old physically challenged stranger appeared on the Bangladesh side of the India-Bangladesh border in Chapainawabganj in June 2026. By the time Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) reached him, a crowd had gathered around him.

He could not hold a pen — not because he did not know how to write, but because he had no fingers with which to hold it.

“The matter came to our attention after Shreejib Kumar Singh was found on the Bangladesh side of the border in the Chapainawabganj area,” the officer-in-charge of Gomastapur Police Station told Global Voices in a WhatsApp interview in August, recounting how the incident was reported to police.

title: Digital Tribulations 25: Building Technological Sovereignty from Below, The Experience of Argentine Cooperativism – Interview with Cecilia Muñoz from Código Libre
content:
The introduction of Digital Tribulations, a series of intellectual interviews on the developments of digital sovereignty in Latin America, can be read here and the entire series can be found here.

During the month I spent in Buenos Aires, the last city I visited before finally flying back to Europe, I managed to get a firsthand look at its famous cooperativist scene, which extends to platforms. By “famous” I of course mean a niche that has accompanied platform studies since the sharing economy: platform cooperativism. I first came across it through the pioneering work of Trebor Scholz, and I became more familiar with it thanks to the prolific scholarship of my Brazilian friend Rafael Grohmann. He was the one who gave me Cecilia’s contact, along with the phone number of a fellow Italian, Stefano Tortorici, who is writing his PhD on platform cooperativism. As two Italian researchers in our semi-nomadic phase, I bonded with Stefano and ended up hanging out with his numerous artistic housemates, who shared a house not far from the gentrified Palermo neighborhood.

title: Nepal could show the world how to recover sustainably from a major disaster
content:
With chances of further sensational hydropower tunnel rescues dimming, the devastating ice-rock avalanche in August at the Nepal-Tibet border and catastrophic floods downstream are no longer making global headlines.

But now is the time to pay careful attention to community-centred lessons from past disasters as complex planning decisions are made about recovery and reconstruction that will shape long-term outcomes.

Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority recently released a Rapid Disaster Needs Assessment (RDNA) highlighting many of the challenges facing disaster-affected Nepalis, including the approximately 33,000 who have lost their homes.

As Nepal prepares long-term recovery and risk-reduction strategies, we offer insights from our collaborative research about post-disaster reconstruction and displacement following Nepal’s 2015 earthquake, as well as ongoing mountain hazards, to highlight areas of concern for the country’s affected communities.

title: Najmeh Amini from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad: “I Have Been Sentenced to Death”
content:
According to HRANA, one of those arrested during last year’s January protests, has reported that she has been sentenced to death.

In an audio message from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, Ms. Amini stated that the judiciary issued her death sentence on September 16, 2026.

The prisoner has called on the United Nations, lawyers, activists, and human rights organizations to review her case so that she may exercise her right to a fair trial.

HRANA is unable to independently verify Najmeh Amini’s statements.

A court hearing to address the charges against Ms. Amini was held in August of this year at the Mashhad Revolutionary Court. She was tried on charges of “assembly and collusion against national security” and “insulting sacred beliefs and the Imams.”

On January 31, 2026, Najmeh Amini was arrested by security forces at Ferdowsi Shopping Center in Mashhad during the January protests. She was subsequently transferred to Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

Najmeh Amini, 23, is an accounting student and a resident of Mashhad.

title: Disappearance of 2 Journalists in Djibouti Raises Concerns for Their Safety
content:
The Committee to Protect Journalists said Sunday that it is “deeply concerned” by reports that South African investigative journalist Micah Reddy and local fixer Kooki Mahmoud have gone missing in Djibouti, and urged authorities “to immediately clarify their whereabouts and ensure their safety.”

Contact with Reddy, the African coordinator for the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ), and Mahmoud, a Djibouti-based journalist, was lost Saturday at approximately 1 p.m. local time, said an ICIJ statement. The statement, issued Sunday, said ICIJ is gravely concerned for their safety and authorities in Djibouti have not so far responded to its requests for information.

“We are calling on the government of Djibouti to: Immediately clarify Reddy and Mahmoud's whereabouts and confirm their well-being; Launch a prompt, transparent investigation into their disappearance; Keep their families, colleagues and employers fully and promptly informed,” the ICIJ statement said.

title: Global Poll: People Still Want the UN—But Want It to Deliver
content:
Ahead of the UN General Assembly’s high-level debate, a 20-country survey finds strong support for international cooperation despite widespread anxiety about wars and the future.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 20 September 2026 (IDN) — The United Nations may be struggling with wars it cannot stop, divisions among the major powers and growing doubts about the international order. But a new global poll suggests that people are not ready to give up on either the UN or international cooperation.

They do, however, expect more.

A survey released by the United Nations Foundation on 17 September found that 57 per cent of respondents were worried about the future, while nearly nine in ten believed that even the world’s most powerful countries need the international system rather than trying to confront today’s problems on their own.

Only 13 per cent regarded the United Nations as outdated and no longer necessary.

But 52 per cent said the organisation remains necessary, even as it struggles to deliver results.

title: EU budget needs taxes governments aren’t already raising, Costa says
content:
DUBLIN — Governments will be more likely to back new EU taxes for the bloc’s next seven-year budget if they raise money that national governments are not already collecting, European Council President António Costa said.

In an interview with POLITICO, Costa set out for the first time what he gathered from leaders during his tour of 25 capitals on one of the thorniest issues in the talks: how to build support towards new EU levies — known as “own resources” — that would generate fresh revenue to the budget.

The answer will help determine whether EU governments can agree on a budget by the end of the year — before 2027’s elections in France, Italy, Spain and Poland threaten to derail the talks — without either cutting spending on new priorities or asking national governments to pay more.

“If we don’t create new own resources, we need to ask [for] more money from the member states,” Costa said. “We know that we need to keep the national contributions at a reasonable limit. For this, we need to have a credible basket of new own resources.”

title: WikiGotong-Royong Malaysia Day 2026: Contributing Knowledge, Documenting Heritage
content:
Malaysia Day is more than just a date commemorating the formation of the country. It is also an opportunity to reflect on the diverse histories, cultures, languages and communities that make up Malaysia. For Wikimedia Malaysia, this spirit is expressed through WikiGotong-Royong Malaysia Day 2026, a digital editing campaign (edit-a-thon) that brings together volunteers to enrich and document knowledge about Malaysian history, heritage, culture, local languages, and figures involved in the formation of Malaysia focused on Wikipedia Project.

You may refer the event page on meta-wiki (click here)

The concept of gotong-royong, which is deeply rooted in Malaysian society, is brought into the digital space. While traditional gotong-royong involves communities coming together and working collectively, WikiGotong-Royong invites contributors to share their time, knowledge and skills to build free knowledge resources. Each edit may seem small, but when carried out collectively, these contributions can create something much greater for the benefit of the public.

Scam emails are increasingly using psychological tricks, such as using near-identical URLs like miсrosoft.com

You’ve read the email carefully and it looks legitimate. The link it asks you to click on has none of the usual red flags: there are no weird numbers or extra parts to the URL. You feel safe to proceed.

But if you had looked slightly closer you may have noticed something slightly wrong with one of the characters. Just as in the headline of this piece where instead of “a” we used the Cyrillic “α”.

It just goes to show that the split-second decision you make when clicking a link is often the most vulnerable part of the whole security chain.”

title: From the streets to the ballot box: What Hungary can teach Serbia
content:
Orbán’s machine seemed invincible — until a grassroots movement cracked the psychological trap of fear

Originally published on Global Voices

Péter Magyar's speech at the convening of the National Assembly in Budapest, Hungary, on May 9, 2026. Photo by Elekes Andor via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0).

This article by Tjaša Feher was first published in Serbian on Istinomer.rs on September 2, 2026. An edited version is republished here under a content-sharing agreement between Global Voices and the Center for Research, Transparency and Accountability (CRTA).  

As Serbia gears up for what many already describe as a historic election scheduled for October 18, the challenge is not simply whether an entrenched government can be defeated, but whether almost two years of student-led mobilisation can translate into electoral power.

The political crisis that followed the November 2024 Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse has produced something Serbia has not seen for years: sustained civic mobilisation, new networks of trust and participation by large numbers of people outside conventional opposition structures.

title: Trump declares victory in Greenland, but the deal exposes a deeper crisis of trust
content:
US President Donald Trump is already presenting the new security agreement between the United States, Denmark and Greenland as a personal triumph.

By his telling, Washington has secured permanent control over Greenland’s security and the power to prevent adversaries from establishing military bases or making sensitive investments there.

The Prime Minister’s Office of Denmark describes a different bargain: stronger Arctic security that preserves the Kingdom of Denmark’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as Greenlanders’ right to self-determination.

Yet the political bargain is already visible. Trump gets the spectacle of power – or as a US correspondent for Danish newspaper Politiken said, “he was allowed to take a victory lap on social media”. Denmark and Greenland keep nominal sovereignty. NATO avoids an immediate rupture. Each party can declare success.

That is the optimistic reading. The more troubling one is that the agreement rewards months of coercion against an ally. It normalises a sphere-of-influence politics in which smaller states remain legally sovereign but face pressure to accept strategic subordination.
snippet: US President Donald Trump is already presenting the new security agreement between the United States, Denmark and Greenland as a personal triumph.
creator: Shannon Brincat, Senior Lecturer in Politics and International Relations, University of the Sunshine Coast

title: Wiki for Minorities Welcomes Burkina Faso: Documenting Underrepresented Communities Through Free Knowledge
content:
Wiki for Minorities continues to grow across Sub-Saharan Africa, and Burkina Faso has now become an important part of this expanding movement for diversity, inclusion, and representation in the Wikimedia ecosystem. In recent years, the Wiki for Minorities Burkina Faso initiative brought together Wikimedia contributors to address the digital underrepresentation of minority and marginalized communities across the country. The initiative was designed to document, preserve, and make more visible the histories, cultures, languages, experiences, and contributions of communities that remain poorly represented online.

The campaign placed particular emphasis on people with albinism, people who are blind or visually impaired, people with disabilities, minority linguistic and cultural communities, and other groups whose stories are often missing from online knowledge resources.

title: In a world of wars and climate crisis, a new leader could save the UN. But would Trump allow it? | Steve Bloomfield
content:
As the organisation meets this week, it remains the best hope for restoring order. But it relies on goodwill from the US president – and that is lacking

If all goes to plan, at some stage in the coming weeks 15 diplomats will emerge from a small sound-proofed room deep in the bowels of the United Nations headquarters in New York and announce the organisation’s next secretary-general.

The person they choose will face a combination of challenges unlike any that their predecessors have had to deal with. Two of the security council’s permanent members, the US and Russia, are engaged in wars of choice that have no end in sight. A UN commission of inquiry has accused Israel of committing genocide in Gaza, but the UN has effectively been reduced to the role of bystander, pushed out by Donald Trump’s Board of Peace. The climate crisis is creating a cascade of new humanitarian disasters, while every day now seems to bring a new security threat caused by the unregulated rise of AI.

Steve Bloomfield is the former international editor of the Observer and a previous winner of the Orwell prize

The majority of the world’s languages are primarily spoken, not written. So, the knowledge of the speaker communities is oral, yet Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects require written citations.

The OpenSpeaks Archives is developing a process for Wikimedians to cite oral knowledge from Indigenous and other low-resourced language communities, including nearly 20 language communities from India, Nepal, and Sri Lanka. This process includes audio-visual documentation, creating technological and educational resources, and community capacity building.

title: Celebrating Wikipedia 25 in Odisha: Outreach, Education, and Lessons in Community Building
content:
Twenty-five years of Wikipedia is not just a milestone for the global Wikimedia movement; it is a celebration of every language community that keeps free knowledge alive. In Odisha, India, the Odia Wikimedians User Group marked this silver jubilee through a dynamic series of activities blending public festivals, institutional partnerships, community gatherings, and digital contributions.

From lively cultural gatherings to lecture halls and community studios, here is the story of how we celebrated Wikipedia 25–along with what worked, what we learned, and where we are heading next.

One of our core goals was to make Wikipedia visible beyond typical digital spaces by taking it directly to people in their everyday community settings.

title: The Knowledge Commons in the Age of AI: Keynote speech at WikiConference India 2026
content:
Written version of the opening keynote delivered at WikiConference India 2026 (WCI 26) by Tanveer Hasan, Open Knowledge Initiatives, India.

I want to begin by acknowledging who is in this room. We are the people who build, maintain, and govern the most remarkable knowledge infrastructure humanity has ever created. We do this work not for profit or acclaim but because of our belief in the principle of free knowledge for everyone.

Keynotes are either information-heavy or seen as inspirational talks. I am sorry to disappoint you: this one is neither. What this is, is a collaborative discussion that I am presenting on behalf of all the organisers, the programme team and my team members. I am the voice of the talk, but the thinking is truly shared and collaborative. My goal is not to inspire you. You are already inspired, and that is why the scholarship team had such a difficult job in making its decisions. My intention is to share some data, to offer a framework for thinking about our challenges, and to ask some difficult questions that I believe we, as a community, must answer together.

title: “Our Dear Friend Umar”: How We Uncovered That a Russian Oligarch Bankrolled Donald Trump Jr.’s Wedding
content:
My colleagues and I had been digging for days. We’d heard a rumor that a Russian oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin named Umar Kremlev had attended Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding this past May in the Bahamas. But to confirm that, we needed visual proof. 

First, we scoured everything the Trumps had released from the event, held on a pair of private islands. On social media and in the pages of tabloids such as Page Six and Hello! magazine, official photos from the weekend showed an intimate chapel ceremony alongside lavish beach parties. Several photos depicted guests, including Jared Kushner and Eric Trump, and we scanned them all for signs of Kremlev. Still, nothing had turned up yet.

We then turned to Kremlev’s social media profiles on the off chance that he’d posted about the wedding. Incredibly, on Telegram, Kremlev had posted videos over the same weekend as Trump Jr.’s wedding that appeared to be from someplace tropical. In one, a single detail caught our attention: As Kremlev speaks in Russian to the camera, the frame gives a partial view of an outdoor patio setting. It wasn’t palm trees or crystal water we noticed, but the wicker furniture.

title: ‘Supermountains’ Buried Under Antarctica Fueled Explosion of Life, Scientists Discover
content:
Welcome back to the Abstract! These are the studies this week that ate well, moved mountains, grew brains, and saved medieval texts.

First, scientists set out to understand why Venus doesn’t have a moon and discover even more unnerving stuff about this delightfully nightmarish planet. Then: a hidden range of primordial supermountains, a literal brain-space, and evidence of Tudor-era subterfuge.

As always, for more of my work, check out my book First Contact: The Story of Our Obsession with Aliens, or subscribe to my personal newsletter the BeX Files. 

Kane, Stephen R. et al. “Tidal Demise: The Evolution and Fate of a Hypothetical Venus Moon.” The Astrophysical Journal.

Venus is a bizarro world with a year that is shorter than its day, a surface shaped by diabolical heat and pressure, and skies soaked in sulfuric acid. Frankly, this planet is metal enough as it is, but scientists have now suggested that Venus is also a moon-eater.

title: Pakistan: Rights Lawyers Rearrested after Bail
content:
(New York) – Pakistani authorities on September 17, 2026, rearrested human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha soon after the Supreme Court granted them bail, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities should immediately release the two and drop the criminal charges against them, which appear aimed to punish peaceful expression and human rights advocacy.

The authorities had originally charged and convicted Mazari and Chattha, a married couple, for social media posts in support of local activists and criticizing the military. The Supreme Court on September 17 granted bail and ordered their release pending the Islamabad High Court’s final decision on their appeals. Hours later, the police rearrested Mazari and Chattha on anti-terrorism charges related to a separate, older case from March 2025 concerning their participation in a protest the authorities allege was illegal.

title: Africa’s Public-Sector Reforms Need Leaders, Not Only Technical Expertise
content:
The African Capacity Building Foundation and the Gates Foundation are expanding a programme designed to help officials turn sound policies into lasting institutional change.

By Jeffrey Moyo

HARARE, Zimbabwe | 19 September 2026 (IDN) — African governments must invest more seriously in leadership development if ambitious public-sector reforms are to produce lasting results, according to the African Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF) and the Gates Foundation.

The two organisations made the case during a 3 September webinar, “Leading Public Sector Transformation in Africa: Leadership Lessons from the LEAPS Programme”. The discussion examined how stronger leadership could help governments overcome resistance to reform, improve public financial management and turn policy initiatives into measurable institutional gains.

Mamadou Biteye, ACBF’s Executive Secretary, said public-sector reform in Africa was rarely held back by a shortage of good ideas.

“More often, the real challenge is our ability to lead change by bringing people together, building trust, overcoming resistance, and sustaining momentum,” he said.

title: ‘A place of silence, contemplation, and beauty can also become a form of resistance,’ in conversation with Catalan artist Jaume Amigó
content:
‘[P]ainters cannot escape the state the world is currently in. In my work, I try to seek out another reality …’

Originally published on Global Voices

Jaume Amigó, ‘Papers d’aigua I,’ 2023. Acrylic on paper, 290 x 420 cm (114.2 × 165.4 in). Photo courtesy of the artist.

For Jaume Amigó, painting can be a form of resistance, not by reproducing the violence and disorder of the present, but by creating an alternative space within it. At a moment saturated with immediate and often brutal images, the Catalan artist turns toward silence, contemplation, beauty and the rhythms of nature. “Painting is also a way of taking a position,” he says, through “the creation of another possible space” that, by contrast, “can also become a form of resistance.”

Born in Barcelona in 1963, Amigó studied engraving and printmaking at the Llotja School of Art and Design. Painting remains central to his practice, but he has also worked in sculpture, ceramics, engraving, installation and scenography. Based in l’Alzina de Ribelles, in Catalonia’s La Noguera region, he has exhibited widely in Spain and abroad, including in Japan, Morocco, the Netherlands and Switzerland.

title: Eduskunta pyörii kirjoittamattomien sääntöjen varassa – pitäisikö niistä tehdä virallisia?
content:
Kuka saa kyselytunnilla puheenvuoron, kuinka kauan hallitusta hiillostetaan ja milloin keskustelu katkaistaan? Moni eduskunnan sääntö perustuu perinteisiin – ja puhemiesten mielenliikkeisiin.

Eduskunnan työtavoista vain runko on laissa. Loput ovat kirjoittamattomia sääntöjä ja perinnettä, jota uudet edustajat eivät välttämättä tunne ja jota puhemiehet tulkitsevat kukin omalla tavallaan.

Silti sekä entinen puhemies Matti Vanhanen (kesk.) että eduskunnan entinen pääsihteeri Seppo Tiitinen suhtautuvat penseästi ajatukseen tarkemmista pykälistä: sääntöjä ei pelasta kirjaaminen, vaan valvonta ja keskustelu – ja niissä avainasemassa on puhemies.

Kun eduskunnan puhemies torstaisin avaa televisioidun kyselytunnin, hän nojaa yllättävän ohueen säädöspohjaan.

Perustuslaki ja eduskunnan työjärjestys määrittelevät vain raamit: työjärjestyksen 25 pykälän mukaan puhemies antaa harkintansa mukaan edustajien ja ministerien käyttää puheenvuoroja, ja kun hän katsoo keskustelun riittävän, hän julistaa sen päättyneeksi.

Sellaiset asiat kuten, kuka kysyy ensin, kuinka kauan yhtä aihetta käsitellään ja milloin hallituspuolue pääsee väliin, ovat perinteen ja puhemiehen harkinnan varassa.

title: Looking Toward Korea from the Ruins of Nagoya Castle: A Report on the Japan-Korea Edit-a-thon in Karatsu
content:
Early September 2026, twelve contributors—including five from South Korea—arrived in Karatsu by train from Hakata for the Japan-Korea Edit-a-thon in Karatsu. It was my first time setting foot in Saga Prefecture.

First, I took a photograph of the monument in the station plaza honoring individuals who made significant contributions to the development of railways in Saga Prefecture. The monument features relief portraits of four figures, one of whom was Kotaro Oshima. Oshima was a businessman from Karatsu who dedicated himself to local development by launching various enterprises—spanning not only railways but also banking and electric power companies. I learned about him while preparing for this edit-a-thon; having long held an interest in Meiji-era entrepreneurs, I had already drafted an article about him in advance. On the day of the event, we visited the former Karatsu Bank building—where he had served as president—and then moved to Oshima’s former residence, the venue for the afternoon’s edit-a-thon, where I published the article on Kotaro Oshima.

title: Russia’s Rigged Elections Still Serve a Purpose
content:
The outcome of Russia’s parliamentary elections is predetermined. Yet the Kremlin cares about much more than the figures announced once the ballots are (mis)counted.

Vladimir Putin’s regime can of course falsify almost any result. Independent election monitoring has been largely destroyed, voting has been extended over three days, and electronic ballots are difficult to verify. But an entirely fictional election would cease to perform its most important function. It would tell the Kremlin nothing about the discipline of its officials, the resilience of regional elites, or the state’s ability to mobilize the population.

Russian elections are therefore more than a falsified vote count. They are a nationwide examination of the Putin system. Citizens play a secondary role. The real examinees are governors, bureaucrats, directors of state institutions, and party functionaries.

From September 18 to 20, Russians elect a new State Duma. At the same time, more than 2,200 regional and municipal elections will take place across the country, distributing approximately 20,700 elected offices and legislative seats.

title: How Poland “planned to occupy Czech lands” – coordinated information operation exposed
content:
Facebook posts called on people to gather for a protest in the Czech border town of Třinec on Saturday, 29th of August. The protest never took place. The Třinec municipal authorities had already announced that no public event had been registered, while the Czech Republic’s largest trade union, KOVO, which represents metalworking and industrial workers and whose logo was used in the protest advertising materials, denied any connection with the action. Moreover, Polish and Czech media had already exposed the disinformation campaign, which involved fake social media profiles, fabricated media outlets, forged documents and even an unauthorised publication of an article on the website of a public broadcaster.

At the beginning of August, disinformation began circulating claiming that Poland planned to take over more than 600 hectares of Czech territory. According to an analysis by the Czech news portal Seznam Zprávy, several social media accounts in the Czech Republic circulated a document purportedly sent by the Polish government to the Czech authorities. It allegedly demanded that land with a total area of 638.44 hectares be handed over to Poland.

title: Moscow cries fraud abroad while fixing the vote at home
content:
Moscow routinely portrays elections in democratic countries as fraudulent and controlled from abroad. Yet Russia’s own parliamentary election offers no genuine political choice: the Kremlin controls the field and has eliminated even the possibility of voting against the war in Ukraine. As the war’s effects reach deeper into everyday life, growing public dissatisfaction is being kept out of the ballot box.

When post-Soviet states turn away from Russia, as Armenia or Moldova have done, Kremlin officials and aligned outlets usually blame Western interference. Yet Moscow has itself tries to influence elections through foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI), often alongside financial support for pro-Russian groups. Moldovan authorities say Russian agents spent about €200 million – nearly 1% of Moldova’s GDP – on vote-buying and disinformation during the country’s 2024 presidential election and EU referendum. Investigators later found that the sanctioned Russian organisation Evrazia had used similar tactics ahead of Armenia’s 2026 election. Moscow nevertheless portrayed EU assistance intended to counter such threats as election interference.

title: Judge Denies Efforts to End Oversight of Maricopa County Sheriff’s Office as Racial Profiling of Latinos Persists
content:
A federal judge has denied efforts to remove oversight of the Maricopa County Sheriff’s Office, saying the agency continues to show racial disparities in traffic arrests of Latinos — and that there is not enough evidence that efforts to improve would stick without legal monitoring.

In his 72-page ruling issued Sept. 10, U.S. District Judge G. Murray Snow stressed Sheriff Jerry Sheridan’s role in the department’s racial profiling since the start of the case more than a decade ago, including fighting court-ordered reforms and stymieing investigations. Sheridan was the No. 2 under former Sheriff Joe Arpaio when the county was found out of compliance with federal law.

“Then Chief Deputy, now Sheriff, Sheridan in particular was found to have abused his authority over MCSO’s internal affairs process by obstructing and manipulating misconduct investigations and disciplinary proceedings — including those involving himself — to shield deputies and Command Staff from accountability and undermine the enforcement of remedies designed to address the constitutional violations against the Plaintiff class,” the judge wrote in an opinion that mentions Sheridan 30 times.

title: Sweden’s 2026 election: Social Democrats lost the battle but won the war?
content:
In last week’s parliamentary elections in Sweden, the Swedish Social Democratic Party undoubtedly became the largest party, with the support of 28 per cent of voters and a strong chance of leading the next government by replacing the incumbent right-wing one. Yet, within Swedish Social Democracy, a sense of dissatisfaction prevails. How did this come about?

In a fragmented parliament with eight parties, 28 per cent of the popular vote is not a disaster – especially not from a European perspective. When conservative Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson steps down after four years, it will be the first time since 1994 that a Swedish government has lost power after only a single term.

Yet the 2-point drop to 28 per cent remains historically weak for the Social Democrats. Above all, the contrast with the preceding term is striking. For periods, the party polled between 35 and 37 per cent, and as recently as August, the centre-left opposition bloc held a lead of around ten percentage points. When the results came in, however, the election was decided by a razor-thin margin.

title: Samtal om Själö hospital – kvinnoöden på 1800-talet
content:
Tidpunkt: 26.10 klockan 18.00-19.00
Plats: Finlandsinstitutet
Adress: Snickarbacken 4, Stockholm
Språk: svenska
Inträde: Gratis, men anmäl dig gärna här gärna här

Berättelsen om Själös kvinnoöden fortsätter att fascinera den finländska befolkningen och är igen aktuell i och med den nya finländska långfilmen Berätta för alla. På Själö, en ö i Åbolands skärgård, har ett av Finlands äldsta sjukhus fungerat i över 350 år. Men det var på 1800-talet som sjukhuset mer eller mindre förvandlades till ett sjukhus för enbart kvinnor. Kvinnor som beskrevs som obotligt sjuka men som i hög grad bestod av individer som samhället helt enkelt inte ville veta av. Och de allra flesta kvinnor som kom till Själö blev kvar resten av livet.

I samband med premiären av Berätta för alla ordnar vi ett samtal om Själös kvinnoöden och kanske ställer vi oss frågan, hade också jag hamnat där? För hur ser den samhälleliga blicken på kvinnor egentligen ut idag och vad är det med Själö som fortsätter att beröra?

I samtalet deltar bland annat författaren Johanna Holmström som skrivit boken Själarnas ö och skådespelaren Marketta Tikkanen från den högaktuella filmen Berätta för alla.

title: Keskustelu Seilin sairaalasta – Suomalaisten naisten kohtalo 1800-luvulla
content:
Aika: 26.10 kello 18.00-19.00
Paikka: Finlandsinstitutet
Osoite: Snickarbacken 4, Stockholm
Kieli: Ruotsi
Sisäänpääsy: Imainen mutta ilmoittaudu mielellään täällä

Tarina Seilin saaren naisten kohtalosta kiehtoo yhä suomalaisia, ja on nyt noussut jälleen pinnalle uuden elokuvan Kerro kaikille myötä. Turun saaristossa sijaitsevalla Seilin saarella sijaitsee yksi Suomen vanhimmista sairaaloista, joka on toiminut jo yli 350 vuotta. Mutta vasta 1800-luvulla sairaala muuttui käytännössä vain naisille tarkoitetuksi laitokseksi. Naiset, joita kuvailtiin parantumattomiksi yksilöiksi, olivat suurin osa vain ihmisiä joista yhteiskunta ei halunnut tietää. Monet näistä naisista jäivät Seilin saarelle loppuelämäkseen.

Kerro kaikille elokuvan yhteydessä järjestämme keskustelun Seilin naisten kohtalosta, kysyen ehkä myös itseltämme, olisinko minäkin jäänyt saarelle? Millainen on yhteiskunnan suhtautuminen naisiin nykyään, ja mikä Seilin saaressa vielä tänäkin päivänä koskettaa?

Keskusteluun osallistuvat muun muassa kirjailija Johanna Holmström, joka on kirjoittanut kirjan Sielujen saari, sekä näyttelijä Marketta Tikkanen, joka näyttelee elokuvassa Kerro kaikille.

title: How Togolese people are reinventing political protest amid civil society crackdown
content:
All Togolese people are being affected by the country’s economic and political crisis

Originally published on Global Voices

Protest against Faure Gnassingbé in Belgium in October 2017. Since the 2025 Gen Z protests, the Togolese state has cracked down on protesters and civil society. Image via Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 2.0 

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

In Togo, demonstrations and opportunities for civil disobedience are drying up as the government cracks down on civil society and tightens restrictions on freedom of expression amid an ongoing political crisis. However, this does not spell the end of protest, as citizens find other avenues to make their voices heard.

As in-person gatherings have become difficult to organize or too risky for citizens, online protest has become an increasingly common form of political dissent in Togo.

title: What Shall We Do About South Africa?
content:
By Azu Ishiekwene

The writer is the Editor-In-Chief of LEADERSHIP and the author of the new book Writing for Media and Monetising It.

ABUJA, Nigeria | 18 September 2026 (IDN) — If South Africa needed any serious signal that the mobs roaming the streets of its cities and townships in search of immigrants were a disgrace, the FIFA World Cup in June 2026 provided a large screen.

But the country is not looking. Or is looking but cannot see.

In the last three years, according to Xenowatch, about 50 people have been killed in xenophobic-related incidents in South Africa. That’s not counting the displaced and wounded or the hundreds forcibly repatriated, and those whose businesses have been destroyed.

Between June 2026 and now, there have been eight verified deaths linked to xenophobic attacks on Africans. Two of them, Bishop Taiwo Michael Fakunle and James Uchechukwu Nwankwo, were Nigerians. The Ghanaian News Agency reported that two Ghanaians were killed between July and August.

What will it take to end this madness, which has set one of Africa’s most promising countries against the rest of the continent?

title: OKM: selvitys esittää tekijänoikeusjärjestöille lakisääteistä asiavaltuutta
content:
Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriön julkaisema selvitys ehdottaa, että tekijänoikeusjärjestöjen asiavaltuudesta säädetään lailla. Muutos helpottaa teosten luvattomaan käyttöön puuttumista erityisesti silloin, kun käyttö koskee suurta määrää teoksia.

Taiteilijan voi olla vaikea valvoa, miten hänen teoksiaan käytetään. Tekijänoikeusjärjestöillä on oikeuksien hallinnointiin valtuutuksia, mutta ne eivät voi lähtökohtaisesti viedä omissa nimissään tekijänoikeuden loukkauksia oikeuteen, jollei yksinoikeuksia ole siirretty järjestöille. Asia nousi esiin korkeimman oikeuden (KKO 2024:53) ratkaisussa, jossa KKO katsoi, ettei Kopiostolla ollut asiavaltuutta eli oikeutta esittää omissa nimissään vaatimuksia tekijänoikeuden loukkausta koskevassa jutussa.

OKM:n tilauksesta asiantuntijaselvityksen tehnyt emeritusprofessori Niklas Bruun esittää, että asiavaltuudesta säädetään lailla. Bruunin mukaan tekijänoikeusjärjestöillä on välitön intressi valvoa oikeuksia, sillä ne hallinnoivat tekijänoikeuksia ja lähioikeuksia kollektiivisesti, oikeudenhaltijoiden yhteiseen lukuun.

title: Purkutaiteen 10-vuotisnäyttely käsittelee epämukavia aiheita mutta tarjoaa myös rauhoittumisen paikkoja
content:
Ai tätä trendisanalla ”immersiivinen taide” tarkoitetaan! Sen hoksaa, kun vaeltaa Arabian 135-korttelin käytävillä, entisissä studioissa ja luokkahuoneissa.

Keväällä avatussa Purkutaide-kollektiivin 10-vuotisnäyttelyssä Tämän haluan sanoa on esillä 55 tilataideteosta, joiden luomaan maailmaan voisi helposta upota koko päiväksi.

Kollektiivi uskoo moniaistillisuuteen ja kokemuksellisuuteen ja pyrkii siihen, että kaikki tuntevat olonsa tervetulleiksi. Sekä taideharrastajat että vähemmän kokeneet kävijät voivatkin löytää teosten kuva-, väri-, ääni- ja tekstimaailmasta uusia tapoja hahmottaa todellisuutta ja erilaisia yhteiskunnallisia ilmiöitä.

Asia on painavaa. Omiin huoneisiinsa erotellut teokset käsittelevät muun muassa pikamuotia, ekologista kriisiä, tuotantoeläinten asemaa, sukupuolta, mielenterveysongelmia ja muistisairautta.

Keskeinen teema on useammassakin teoksessa toistuva lähisuhdeväkivalta. Elina Holleyn, Miia Naparin ja Haydn Douet Lukiesin Varjolinnunlaulu avaa katsojan eteen huoneen, joka näyttää ensin tavalliselta asunnolta. Lähempi tarkastelu paljastaa vääristyneen, ahdistavan kulissin.

title: Eskarilaisten vanhemmat kutsutaan kirjastoon
content:
Miten lasten lukuinto syntyy? Samalla tavalla kuin miten he muutenkin elämää oppivat. Aikuisten esimerkin kautta.

Tämän ovat oivaltaneet Oriveden kirjastoammattilaiset, kirjastonhoitajat Mia Moilanen ja Ilkka Kaita-aho sekä varhaiskasvatuksen opettaja Tanja Riihimäki, jotka aloittivat pari vuotta sitten kirjaston vanhempainillat esikoululaisten perheille.

Syksyn alkaessa esikoulun aloittaneet ja heidän vanhempansa kutsutaan kirjastoon seikkailemaan ja saamaan tietoa siitä, mitä kaikkea kirjasto perheille tarjoaa.

Myös perheiden muut lapset ovat tervetulleita iltaan, sillä tarkoitus on herättää koko perheen yhteinen kiinnostus kirjojen maailmaan. Näin kirjaston avulla täydennetään neuvolasta alkanutta lukemisen pariin kannustamista.

Vanhempainillan aikana kirjasto on varattu pelkästään eskareiden perheille. Ensimmäisellä kerralla mukana oli sata osallistujaa, eli lähes kaikki pienen paikkakunnan esikoululaiset perheenjäsenineen.

title: What might Canada’s EU ‘associate membership’ look like, and is it even a possibility?
content:
In a speech to the European Parliament, Canadian prime minister Mark Carney declared that “Europe and Canada are stronger together”. He also backed an offer made by the president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, one day earlier for Canada to become the first “associate member” of the bloc.

“Canada welcomes this ambition,” he said. “An alliance for the future is a unique, positive approach that we will define together.” But what might associate membership look like, how significant is von der Leyen’s offer in the history of the EU’s relations with external states, and how likely is it to come into being?

Canada already has a preferential trade deal with the EU in the form of the 2016 Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (Ceta). This type of free-trade agreement is typical of the sort of legal instrument used by the EU to manage relations with its main international partners.

But one way in which the EU could upgrade Ottawa’s relations with Brussels would be to look to the template of the “association agreements” the EU uses to bring neighbouring countries into closer alignment with its policies and programmes.

title: Russia’s parliamentary elections will not be a referendum on the Ukraine war – or anything, really
content:
Russia is not a democracy. However, Russia does have elections – many of them, in fact.

From September 18-20, Russian voters will elect their national parliamentary representatives (to the Russian State Duma), as well as 11 governors, deputies to 39 regional assemblies, and deputies to other lower-level representative bodies.

The elections will be the first parliamentary elections since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. However, this will not be a barometer of public opinion about the war, the state of the Russian economy, or, well, anything.

Russians have many reasons to be disenchanted with President Vladimir Putin’s regime. The war is now in its fifth year, with an estimated 1.4 million battlefield casualties (including 450,000 deaths). Some 30,000 Russian soldiers are either being killed or injured a month. Ukraine is also increasingly bringing the war home to Russians with frequent drone attacks.

Yet, these elections will be carefully stage-managed to guarantee a favourable result – and a continued strong mandate – for Putin’s party.
snippet: Russia is not a democracy. However, Russia does have elections – many of them, in fact.
creator: Alasdair McCallum, Sessional Tutor, Constitutional Law, Monash University

title: Wikipedistiksi kurssin kautta?
content: Pitkän linjan wikipedistinä olen vuosien ajan yrittänyt houkutella tuttuja ja tuntemattomia Wikipedian muokkaajiksi, sillä Wikipediaa hienompaa yhteistyöprojektia on vaikea löytää. Usein olen kuitenkin saanut samansuuntaisia vastauksia. Yksi ei välttämättä tiedä, että kuka tahansa voi muokata. Toinen arvelee, ettei pysty tarjoamaan Wikipedialle mitään lisäarvoa. Kolmas on ehkä kiinnostunut, mutta ei tiedä mistä aloittaa. Vuosien varrella olen ollut monessa muokkaustapahtumassa opettamassa vasta-alkajille Wikipedian saloja. Jo päivän tai muutaman tunnin aikana on saatu ahaa-elämyksiä ja onnistumisen riemua, kun ensimmäinen ikioma Wikipedia-artikkeli on julkaistu kaikkien nähtäville. title: Wiki Loves Monuments: workshop & skrivstuga
content:
I september arrangerar vi den svenska grenen av Wiki Loves Monuments – en internationell fototävling där du bidrar till fri kunskap genom att fotografera det skyddade kulturarvet. Vi ordnar tävlingen i samarbete med Arbetslivsmuseernas samarbetsråd, vilket vi är väldigt glada över.

För att delta i tävlingen måste varje bild föreställa någon av Sveriges fornminnen, byggnadsminnen, K-märkta skepp/fritidsbåtar, kulturreservat eller arbetslivsmuseer. Bilderna släpps fria för hela världen att använda under Creative Commons-licens. Tack vare fokuset på just det skyddade kulturarvet byggs det upp en värdefull bildsamling som kan användas av exempelvis kulturarvsinstitutioner, journalister och forskare som vill synliggöra det skyddade kulturarvet.

Olidans kraftverk vid Göta älv i Trollhättan, Sverige Fotograf: Simiha, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

  • Leta fram ett foto du tagit på det skyddade kulturarvet – eller gå ut och ta nya bilder.
  • Skapa ett konto på Wikimedia Commons (tar cirka 30 sekunder), om du inte redan har ett.
  • Ladda upp bilden via kartan eller uppladdningsverktyget. Du kan ladda upp hur många bilder du vill till och med 30 september.

title: Janne Riiheläinen: Venäjä mittaa mielellään meidänkin kansalaistahtoamme
content:
Vieraiden valtioiden kuten Venäjän pahantekijät toivovat, ettemme olisi niin tunnollisia ja kunnollisia kuin nyt – koska sen jälkeen ne pystyisivät helpommin murentamaan yhteiskuntaamme.

Avaimenperässäni roikkui pitkään sellainen kolikosta käyvä
metallinpalanen, jolla sai vapautettua marketin sisäänkulun luona odottavat ostoskärryt mukaansa kauppaan.

Alun perin kolikoilla toimineen lukitussysteemin tarkoituksena oli varmistaa, että ihmiset palauttaisivat kärryt paikalleen käytön jälkeen, eivätkä jättäisi niitä pitkin parkkipaikkoja.

Jossain vaiheessa joku muutti mielensä ja kaupassa kärryjen luo ilmestyi lappu, jossa pyydettiin jättämään kärryt lukitsematta. Eikä niitä ole ainakaan omien havaintojen perusteella yhtään sen enempää levällään kuin ennenkään.

Tämä on Suomi. Tämä on sellaisten ihmisten maa, jossa suuri enemmistö hoitaa asioita kunnollisesti ja tunnollisesti.

Ostoskärryjen palauttaminen paikalleen nousee siitä samasta suhtautumisesta, jonka takia seisomme odottamassa tyhjän kadun äärellä punaisissa valoissa ja olemme valmiit puolustamaan maatamme, vaikka tulos olisi epävarma.

title: "We Are the 99%": 15 Years Later, Occupy Wall Street's Impact Is Still Being Felt
content:
Fifteen years ago this week, thousands of activists marched on the Financial District in New York City. They formed the Occupy Wall Street encampment in Zuccotti Park, launching a movement focused on economic inequality that spread across the nation and globe under the slogan, “We are the 99%.” Protesters would go on to sleep in Zuccotti Park for nearly two months before police raided the encampment.

“Occupy Wall Street changed the public’s common sense about class and class struggle and inequality in this country,” says Yotam Marom, who helped organize the Occupy protests in New York City. “It’s hard to see how you get a Bernie Sanders 2016 run without the public shifting its relationship to that story.”

Marom says Occupy participants were inspired by mass protests happening around the world at that time, including the Arab Spring and the anti-austerity movement in Spain known as the Indignados.

Still, “We got it wrong on a lot of things. We had a ton of internal conflict that really jeopardized the project,” he says.

Marom’s new book is For Louder Days: Reaching Beyond a Politics of Powerlessness.

title: What does a stronger Europe actually require? Demos Helsinki’s comments on the State of the Union.
content:
President von der Leyen highlighted in her State of the Union speech on 16 September a Europe that must become more capable of acting on its own terms: stronger in defence, more secure in energy, more competitive in technology, and more resilient in the face of climate and social pressures.

However, strengthening Europe is not only a question of ambition. It raises difficult questions about dependencies, governance and what we actually mean by resilience. Drawing on research from three EU-funded projects, we look at some of the tensions behind the speech: what technological sovereignty requires in practice, how climate resilience depends on institutions that can work across policy silos, and why Europe’s strength cannot be measured solely through current economic indicators. 

“Europe will need its own capabilities”

“Europe will need its own capabilities”

“We need to stay in the race” 

“We need to stay in the race” 

President von der Leyen made technological capacity a clear part of Europe’s push for greater strategic autonomy. But strengthening technological autonomy is considerably more difficult in practice than the political ambitions might suggest.

title: EFF Statement on California Governor's Executive Order on AI
content:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom's executive order is an opportunity for a needed, thoughtful conversation about artificial intelligence and its potential harms. Everyday Californians are feeling real anxiety about the risks of artificial intelligence, and as an organization that works to ensure technology empowers people, EFF welcomes this order as a way for the state of California to lead a much-needed dialogue that addresses these concerns. 

Nonetheless, the most immediate and current concerns with this technology are not about sci-fi scenarios concerning rogue super-intelligence. They are happening right now through biased algorithmic decision-making for employment or government benefits, AI-powered surveillance systems such as Flock cameras, and artificially inflated personalized pricing. People want state and federal leaders to act, and we urge Gov. Newsom to develop thoughtful policies to address those concerns. Today’s EO is a good start.

title: New Case Filed Against Political Prisoner Mostafa Tajzadeh
content:
According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, a new case has been filed against Mostafa Tajzadeh while he is in prison.

Fakhrossadat Mohtashamipour, Tajzadeh’s wife, stated that after his furlough was approved and the administrative procedures were completed, the process of sending him on furlough was halted at the final stage. Follow-up inquiries revealed that a new case had been opened against him on the charge of “propaganda against the regime,” with bail set at 500 million tomans.

According to his wife, the case dates back to August of this year and must be resolved by the branch handling the case.

Mostafa Tajzadeh was arrested by security forces on July 8, 2022, and subsequently transferred to Evin Prison.

Tajzadeh has faced several judicial cases in recent years.

title: Datakeskuksenkin voi rakentaa puusta – puurakentamisesta, sivuvirroista ja hiilidioksidin hyödyntämisestä kasvua itäiseen Suomeen
content:
Puurakentaminen, metsätalouden sivuvirtojen hyödyntäminen ja talteen otetun hiilidioksidin jalostaminen voivat synnyttää Itä-Suomeen uutta yritystoimintaa ja korkeamman jalostusarvon tuotteita. Näitä mahdollisuuksia kehitetään Itäisen Suomen metsäbiotalouden uudet avaukset -kasvuohjelmassa, joka kokoaa yhteen kuusi maakuntaa, tutkimus- ja koulutusorganisaatioita sekä yrityksiä.

Kasvuohjelma koostuu kolmesta hankkeesta, joissa kehitetään metsätalouden sivuvirtojen käyttöä, teollista puurakentamista sekä hiilidioksidin talteenottoon ja hyödyntämiseen perustuvia ratkaisuja. Toiminta kattaa Etelä-Karjalan, Etelä-Savon, Kainuun, Kymenlaakson, Pohjois-Karjalan ja Pohjois-Savon.

Hankekokonaisuus on saanut valtioneuvostolta 2,5 miljoonan euron rahoituksen. Hankkeiden tulokset ovat hyödynnettävissä koko toiminta-alueella.

Kasvuohjelmaa koordinoiva Pohjois-Karjalan maakuntaliitto kokosi hankkeiden vetäjät ja yritysyhteistyökumppanit paneelikeskusteluun arvioimaan, millaisia mahdollisuuksia hankkeet avaavat uuden liiketoiminnan, investointien ja työpaikkojen synnylle Itä-Suomessa.

title: Johtajan nimissä tuleva kiireellinen maksupyyntö voi olla huijaus
content:
Traficomin Kyberturvallisuuskeskukselle ilmoitetaan säännöllisesti huijauksista, joissa rikollinen esiintyy organisaation johtajana ja yrittää saada työntekijän siirtämään rahaa.

Liikenne- ja viestintävirasto Traficomin Kyberturvallisuuskeskukselle on raportoitu tapauksia, joissa huijari esittää olevansa esimerkiksi pääjohtaja, kunnanjohtaja, arkkipiispa, rehtori, pormestari tai pääsihteeri.

Huijarit selvittävät etukäteen organisaation johtoa ja työntekijöiden tehtäviä. Johtajan nimiin väärennetyllä viestillä rikollinen yrittää saada työntekijää tekemään maksun tai hankinnan. Valejohtaja voi pyytää työntekijää hankkimaan lahjakortteja liikelahjoiksi tai maksamaan laskun ilman tavanomaisia tarkastuskäytäntöjä. Usein verukkeena on, että johtaja on kokouksessa eikä voi vastata puheluihin, mutta asia pitää hoitaa kiireesti ja kyselemättä.

title: British-Turkish novelist and storyteller Elif Shafak wins Helena Vaz da Silva European Award 2026
content:
Press release English – Portuguese

The acclaimed British-Turkish author Elif Shafak is the winner of the Helena Vaz da Silva European Award for Raising Public Awareness on Cultural Heritage 2026. This European recognition pays tribute to Elif Shafak’s exceptional ability to bring Europe’s rich and diverse cultural heritage to life through her captivating storytelling, while responding to the challenges of our time with a powerful call for defending democracy, promoting solidarity, embracing cosmopolitanism and celebrating cultural diversity.

Elif Shafak – Photo credit: Ferhat Elik

The Helena Vaz da Silva European Award was established in 2013 by the Centro Nacional de Cultura (Portugal) in collaboration with Europa Nostra and the Portuguese Press Club, and has the support of the Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sports and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Portugal, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation and Tourism of Portugal.

The award ceremony will take place on 5 November at the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon, Portugal.

title: Nordic Perspectives on Education: A Two-Book Launch
content:
The books  (Brill) and (Stockholm University Press) present current knowledge on the research and practice of moral and citizenship education and of gifted education in the Nordic countries: Denmark, Iceland, Finland, Norway and Sweden. The Nordic countries share a common social and cultural history, together with a commitment to human rights and to the principles of non-discrimination, social justice, respect for life, human dignity and cultural diversity.

How are these values realised in the Nordic model of education and in the policy of “one school for all”? What kind of research and practice is needed in these fields today? And how can Nordic co-operation advance research and teaching across the Nordic countries?

Professor Kirsi Tirri (University of Helsinki) presents Nordic Perspectives on Moral and Citizenship Education, and Professor Valerie Margrain (Karlstad University) presents Nordic Perspectives on Gifted Education. A panel discussion follows the presentations, and the event closes with questions from the audience.

title: Venezuela: Reform Needed for Rights Progress
content:
(Washington, DC) – Venezuela needs to take urgent measures and carry out institutional reforms to protect people’s basic rights, Human Rights Watch said today, following its first official visit to the country since 2008. 

Human Rights Watch visited Caracas this week and met with interim President Delcy Rodríguez, other government officials, human rights groups, members of the opposition, journalists, relatives of political prisoners, foreign diplomats, and others. Staff also visited Petare, a low-income neighborhood on the outskirts of Caracas. During its previous high-level visit, in 2008, Venezuelan authorities detained Human Rights Watch staff after they released a report and expelled them from the country.

“Interim President Delcy Rodríguez has overseen a pause to the most overt forms of repression in Venezuela,” said Federico Borello, deputy executive director at Human Rights Watch. “But in this fragile political moment, these gains will only become sustainable with robust institutional reforms and the release of all political prisoners.”

title: Living Heritage Journeys: training on intangible cultural heritage in Kraków
content:
On 14 September 2026, Muzeum Krakowa hosted the training “Cultural Heritage Is More Than Monuments. Intangible Cultural Heritage in Practice – Safeguarding, Cooperation and New Challenges”, devoted to the specific characteristics of working with intangible cultural heritage and its role in museums, cultural institutions, public administration and the tourism sector. The training was led by Hanna Schreiber, our Chairholder.

Taking the 2003 UNESCO Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage as its starting point, the training focused on living practices, knowledge, skills and traditions sustained by communities and transmitted from generation to generation. Participants explored differences between working with tangible and intangible cultural heritage, as well as challenges related to relationships with heritage bearers, participation, documentation, interpretation and the presentation of living heritage. The programme combined lectures with workshop activities.

title: Bosnia Seizes 1.1 Tons of Synthetic Drugs Worth Up to €33 Million
content:
Authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina have seized nearly 1.1 metric tonnes of dangerous synthetic cathinones with a potential street value of up to 33 million euros ($37.82 million), and arrested two suspects, marking the largest synthetic drug bust in the history of the nation of roughly 3.5 million people, the State Border Service announced.

The seized substance—an extremely dangerous stimulant used as a substitute for cocaine and ecstasy—carries a wholesale market value of 5 million euros ($5.73 million), but its street value skyrockets when broken down into individual grams sold at 20 to 30 euros ($23 to $34.50) each across the region, according to the Border Police. In addition to the massive drug cache, officers confiscated a firearm, mobile phones, corporate documentation, official stamps, and specialized full-face respirator masks with advanced air-filtration systems used to protect operators during chemical synthesis and drug "cooking." The Border Police noted that investigators have not yet established the origin or final destination of the shipment, as the investigation remains ongoing.

title: Rage Against the Machines: From the Luddites to the AI Data Center Backlash
content: One often-repeated anecdote about Milton Friedman has the famous economist visiting a canal under construction in nineteen-sixties China. Noticing the sheer number of human laborers digging away with shovels, he asked the official in charge why they weren’t getting the work done faster with excavators and other modern machines. The bureaucrat explained to him that doing it by hand created more jobs. Friedman’s reply: “If it’s jobs you want, you should give those men spoons instead.” Whether or not this exchange ever actually happened, it illustrates a conflict that’s arisen more than once in the history of civilization, possibly since the dawn of industrialization — and at least since the heyday of the Luddites.

title: California’s Newsom signs executive order to explore new AI rules, consider ‘kill switch’
content:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order on Friday to speed up two AI laws he recently signed and explore proposals like requiring that AI companies develop a “kill switch” for their most advanced models.

The order comes after the Democrat told POLITICO this week he was mulling his options to take further action on AI safety, including a possible special legislative session to address recent safety concerns set off by AI researchers’ warnings that the technology could pose an existential risk to humanity and prominent autonomous hacking incidents.

Newsom said his executive action was also driven by federal inaction, after President Donald Trump responded to the warnings by dismissing them as a “hoax” and saying the only guardrails AI needs are his presidency. On Friday, Newsom urged Trump and Congress to adopt California’s AI framework or use the state’s existing regulations as a floor for federal rules.

“The federal government’s abject failure to create any form of meaningful AI oversight or accountability should alarm every American, especially when AI CEOs themselves are begging for regulation,” Newsom said in his press release.

title: Digitizing Tunisia’s Documentary Heritage: From the National Archives to Future GLAM Collaboration
content:
Tunis, Tunisia — A one-month Wikipedian in Residence project at the National Documentation Center of Tunisia has resulted in the digitization of more than 3,000 historical documents, opening new opportunities for the preservation, dissemination, and reuse of Tunisia’s documentary heritage through Wikimedia projects.

The residency was carried out by three Wikipedians in Residence from Wikimedia Tunisia: Mounir Touzri, Houssem Eddin Boubakri, and Naim Garboussi. The team worked in collaboration with the National Documentation Center’s Sub-department of National Archives to identify, digitize, organize, and prepare historical materials for wider public access.

A major part of the project focused on the digitization of magazines published between 1955 and 1983, together with other historical documents related to Tunisia’s history.

The main subjects represented in the digitized collection include sport, art, and cinema, as well as other aspects of Tunisia’s cultural and historical development. The materials contain photographs, articles, reports, and other documentary sources that can provide valuable information about different periods of Tunisian history.

title: Russia’s Election Campaign Puts Governors on the Hook
content:
In the upcoming Russian parliamentary elections from September 18-20, governors will be the top candidate in 45 of the ruling United Russia party’s 57 regional rosters (80%).

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin, who is also considered the governor of the Russian capital, ranks second on the five-candidate federal party roster. Adding other governors running in second place brings the total number of such officials featured at the top of United Russia’s regional and federal rosters to 55. Since 2016, the number of governors heading the party’s rosters has risen sharply: from 19 in that year, to 49 in 2021 and now 55.

This growing reliance is telling. Regional leaders are not merely electoral “coattails” or “locomotives”; they also bear personal responsibility for results in their regions. Voting for United Russia can thus increasingly be seen as a referendum on governors’ approval, shifting accountability for the party’s performance onto their shoulders, and potentially becoming a major pain in their necks. For the party, it’s a useful corrective since it both keeps political elites in step and devolves any electoral uncertainty onto other officials.

title: Tennessee Lawmakers Demand Answers on Safety in State Youth Prisons
content:
Four Democratic Tennessee state lawmakers sent a letter to the Department of Children’s Services demanding answers about safety and oversight in the state’s juvenile justice facilities.

The letter cites a recent WPLN and ProPublica investigation that found that juvenile justice facilities run by Tennessee businessman Jason Crews repeatedly failed to report abuse of children and other serious incidents to the state as required. The reporting involved interviews with dozens of former staff and youth, along with a review of emergency call logs, company records and state documents. Crews and his company Wayne Halfway House run all three of the state’s highest-security youth prisons. 

“The allegations that serious physical and sexual abuse, dangerous restraints, injuries, and other critical incidents have gone unreported by WHH demand an urgent, transparent, and independently verifiable response from the Department of Children’s Services,” lawmakers wrote.
