title: A State of the Union bereft of coherence and clarity
content:
The State of the Union is a very special exercise for the president of the European Commission. Its main purpose is to show that the Commission has a clear vision to tackle the numerous challenges and perils the Union is facing, and that, despite the complex environment, there is an experienced pilot at the helm. Indeed, this year’s statement takes place at an exceptionally difficult time, as President Ursula von der Leyen has said from the outset. Her description and diagnosis of the geopolitical and internal challenges and transformation are accurate enough. But what about her answers and political solutions?

Von der Leyen likes to use a certain degree of pathos to appeal to emotions. That is why she invites some special guests to materialise these emotions. One may doubt if pathos is the best way to respond to people’s fears and expectations and to gain trust.

title: Seilin sairaala – Suomalaisten naisten kohtalo 1800-luvulla
content:
Aika: 26.10 kello 18.00-19.00
Paikka: Finlandsinstitutet
Osoite: Snickarbacken 4, Stockholm
Kieli: Ruotsi
Sisäänpääsy: Imainen mutta ilmoittaudu mielellään täällä

Tarina Seilin saaren naisten kohtalosta kiehtoo yhä suomalaisia, ja on nyt noussut jälleen pinnalle uuden elokuvan Kerro kaikille myötä. Turun saaristossa sijaitsevalla Seilin saarella sijaitsee yksi Suomen vanhimmista sairaaloista, joka on toiminut jo yli 350 vuotta. Mutta vasta 1800-luvulla sairaala muuttui käytännössä vain naisille tarkoitetuksi laitokseksi. Naiset, joita kuvailtiin parantumattomiksi yksilöiksi, olivat suurin osa vain ihmisiä joista yhteiskunta ei halunnut tietää. Monet näistä naisista jäivät Seilin saarelle loppuelämäkseen.

Kerro kaikille elokuvan yhteydessä järjestämme keskustelun Seilin naisten kohtalosta, kysyen ehkä myös itseltämme, olisinko minäkin jäänyt saarelle? Millainen on yhteiskunnan suhtautuminen naisiin nykyään, ja mikä Seilin saaressa vielä tänäkin päivänä koskettaa?

Keskusteluun osallistuvat muun muassa kirjailija Johanna Holmström, joka on kirjoittanut kirjan Sielujen saari, sekä näyttelijä Marketta Tikkanen, joka näyttelee elokuvassa Kerro kaikille.

title: Ecuador detains former minister José Serrano after U.S. deportation
content:
Serrano’s return puts Ecuador’s justice system and rule of law under renewed scrutiny

Originally published on Global Voices

Screenshot taken from the YouTube video “José Serrano enters the El Encuentro prison after being deported from the United States,” by TVC Noticias; fair use.

Following the U.S. immigration system’s refusal to grant political asylum to former Interior Minister José Serrano Salgado, his deportation to Ecuador was carried out under the strictest security measures.

Serrano faces several investigations opened by the Attorney General’s Office of Ecuador, related to his tenure as a government official under former President Rafael Correa, as well as his alleged participation as the mastermind behind the assassination of journalist and former presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio. In the latter case, at the request of the Prosecutor’s Office, the judges ordered both pretrial detention and for him to be transferred to the El Encuentro prison (officially called the Santa Elena No. 1 Detention Center), located in the coastal province of Santa Elena.

title: How Spain’s socialist-led government fumbled the Ceuta crisis, and put itself on the back foot
content:
The crisis in Ceuta has put Pedro Sánchez’s government on the defensive, just as Spain’s political actors return from the summer break. Weeks after the crisis began, the situation remains unresolved. Of the estimated 80,000 migrants who entered Ceuta in late July, 5,482 remain.

Fierce debate has raged over the government’s handling of the crisis, with protests across the country, a deepening culture war, and violent attacks on migrants in Ceuta – some allegedly carried out by Spanish soldiers.

Within Spain, the crisis has barely left the headlines for the last seven weeks. While a permanent solution has yet to emerge, one thing is clear: the government has missed a vital chance to frame the issue of migration on its own terms.

This year’s mass regularisation saw Sánchez taking the initiative. In doing so, he cast himself – and by extension Spain – as a champion of human rights, one who pushes back against Europe’s prevailing anti-migrant sentiment, placing the economy and inclusion at the centre of the debate.

title: The International Olympic Committee wants mental health screening in elite sports. Here’s why
content:
Elite athletes are exposed to a range of sport-specific factors that can heighten their vulnerability to mental ill-health. These include injury, overtraining, burnout, performance-related pressures, intense public scrutiny and social media abuse.

Despite these risks, athletes are often perceived as models of psychological resilience, able to withstand the inherent tension of competing at the highest levels. The mythology of the “mentally tough” or bullet-proof athlete often obscures the reality of elite sport’s mental toll.

This is why the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is encouraging elite level sports around the world to develop stronger mental health protocols for athletes.

I was one of a global network of academics who helped develop the IOC’s recently updated expert consensus statement on mental health in elite sport.

With an emphasis on better early intervention, a key element is mental health screening. This is where athletes complete brief, structured questions to identify possible signs of mental health difficulties that may warrant further assessment.

title: Suomen ensimmäiset F-35A-hävittäjät saapuivat Rovaniemelle – yksi jäi matkasta
content:
Suomen ensimmäiset omat F-35A-hävittäjät saapuivat perjantaina maahan, kun kaksi uudenkarheaa monitoimihävittäjää laskeutui Rovaniemen lentokentälle Hornet-hävittäjien saattamina.

Koneet lennettiin Suomeen perjantaina Portugalin Azoreilta. Määränpäänä oli Lapin lennoston tukikohta Rovaniemellä, jossa sijaitsee Ilmavoimien ensimmäinen F-35-tukikohta.

Odotetun kolmen uuden hävittäjän sijasta perille saapui perjantaina vain kaksi konetta. Paikallisen lentoharrastajan Azoreilla aiemmin päivällä julkaisemalla videolla näkyi, että vain viisi kuudesta siirtolennolla olleesta F-35A-hävittäjästä nousi ilmaan Terceiran lentokentältä.

SUOMEEN saapuneiden hävittäjien lisäksi Lajesista lähti kolme Belgiaan suunnannutta F-35A-hävittäjää, jotka lensivät Lajesiin suomalaishävittäjien kanssa. Suomen ja Belgian hävittäjiä saattamaan lähti yhteensä kaksi KC-135 Stratotanker -ilmatankkauskonetta.

Ilmavoimat ei perjantaina kommentoinut STT:lle kolmannen koneen matkasta jäämisen syytä senkään jälkeen, kun koneet olivat jo laskeutuneet. Pääesikunnan viestinnästä kerrottiin illalla, että asiaa kommentoidaan, kun se on ajankohtaista.

title: Behind the Blog: Eating the Internet
content:
This is Behind the Blog, where we share our behind-the-scenes thoughts about how a few of our top stories of the week came together. This week, we discuss just doing it, machines that eat the internet, and an eavesdropping watch.

EMANUEL: It is a foundational, defining feature of 404 Media, but I sometimes forget that when I’m having trouble with a story, I need to just do it. 

This is most of all true when it comes to reporting. I spent a couple of weeks looking into AI generated music on Spotify appearing under the names of real artists. It’s an issue I and many other publications have reported on in the past, but whenever I look into it I am shocked by how prevalent the issue is. If you talk to any musician or spend some time clicking around music platforms yourself, you’re going to quickly find hundreds of examples of this abuse of the digital music distribution system.

title: Pakistan: Re-arrest of Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha is a terrible injustice
content:
Reacting to the re-arrest of human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha just hours after they had been granted bail by the Supreme Court yesterday, Babu Ram Pant, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for South Asia, said:

“Imaan and Hadi’s re-arrest dispels any pretence that the charges against them are anything other than a politically motivated attempt to punish them for their human rights work. Their case demonstrates once again the authorities’ willingness to weaponize the legal system against critical voices.

“These latest charges, brought against them for simply attending a peaceful protest, are not only absurd but an insult to their lifelong commitment to human rights.

title: "Hope Is the Thing with Feathers": Rhiannon Giddens on New Album, AI, Ed Sheeran, Macklemore & Trump
content:
“If we don’t connect those dots between the struggles, we’re never going to get anywhere,” says Pulitzer Prize- and Grammy-winning multi-instrumentalist Rhiannon Giddens. “That’s what music is for. … We have to make music with people from different backgrounds because then we have that conversation.”

Giddens has had a wide-spanning career, including her time with the Carolina Chocolate Drops, an old-time Black string band, and her work as a musical consultant on Ryan Coogler’s landmark film Sinners. She won a Pulitzer Prize for music in 2023 for her opera Omar about Omar ibn Said, a Muslim scholar in Africa who was sold into slavery in the 1800s. title: How to Limit What Apple’s New Siri AI Can Access in iOS 27
content:
Apple’s new operating system is here, and along with it comes a new version of Siri, dubbed with two very familiar letters: AI. As the name suggests, this Siri power-up resembles an AI chatbot more than the often derided voice assistant you might be used to. It has even evolved from a blob you invoke with a verbal command or a button press to a whole app. This update comes with a slew of privacy complications, but you can take some control over what this new Siri can access and use. 

There’s no denying that the new version of Siri is far more powerful than it used to be, and arguably more useful at surfacing details on your phone. But that comes at the cost of deeper access. Once enabled, Siri and Spotlight are combined, unifying the interface. Where you may have once just pulled down on the screen to search for an app or contact, you’re now also invoking Siri. 

Spotlight and Siri are now visually one and the same.

title: ‘A map is never neutral’: meet the cartographers who took on centuries of western bias
content:
Equal Earth projection, adopted by the UN last week, provides an alternative to 16th-century Mercator display

Three cartographers have spoken of their astonishment at the UN’s near-universal adoption of a map they created to more accurately show the sizes of Africa and Europe, even though they have received a few complaints from some disgruntled diplomats.

The creators of the Equal Earth projection aimed to provide an alternative to the dominant 16th-century Mercator display, which critics have long faulted for giving the impression that northern hemisphere nations are larger than they are – and therefore subtly reinforcing perceptions of where global strength lies.

title: Anna Maria Fjordbøge discussed ethnographic findings on digitalisation and judicial independence
content:
In her presentation, “Blurring boundaries? Negotiating digitalization, efficiency efforts and tripartition of power at the Danish courts” Fjordbøge discussed the ongoing digitalisation of the Danish courts and the penal chain.

The presentation drew on findings from a year-long ethnographic fieldwork project examining how digitalisation and efforts to improve the efficiency of court processes are discussed and implemented in the Danish judiciary. Particular attention was paid to debates concerning the constitutionality of recent digitalisation initiatives, as well as to interactions between administrative and managerial professionals and legal professionals.

A central theme of the presentation was judicial independence. Fjordbøge approached independence as an essentially contested concept within the Danish judiciary and legal policy: different groups of actors may attach different meanings to what judicial independence entails and how it should be protected in practice.

title: Oversight Reports Echo HRW Findings on US Immigration Abuses
content:
On September 11, the US Department of Homeland Security’s Office of Inspector General published reports outlining findings from visits to Krome North Service Processing Center and the now-shuttered “Alligator Alcatraz,” immigration detention facilities in Florida. The oversight body found that the facilities failed to comply with DHS standards, including for medical care, environmental health and safety, and—in the case of Krome—use of force.

One of the most disturbing findings at Alligator Alcatraz was the use of “small metal enclosures”—essentially cages—to hold detainees for up to two hours, which the inspector general said “does not align with standards for humane treatment.” The report states that in at least one case, this may have been used as a “disciplinary tool.”

The inspector general said that confining people in cages “presents significant risks to detainee health and well-being.”

While Alligator Alcatraz officially closed on June 25, there are more than 200 active immigration detention facilities throughout the United States. Human Rights Watch has found cruel, inhuman, and degrading treatment at several of these facilities, including Krome.

title: Iraq Sentences Former Electricity Director General to Seven Years for illicit enrichment
content:
An Iraqi anti-corruption court has sentenced the former director general of a state electricity distribution firm to seven years in prison for illicit enrichment, ordering him to forfeit nearly $20 million in restitution and fines as part of a sweeping crackdown on graft in the country’s power sector.

The official, Alaa Samir Rashid Shukr Al-Jubouri, who headed the state-owned General Company of Electricity Distribution (Middle Region), was convicted by Iraq’s Central Criminal Court for Combating Corruption. According to the country’s Integrity Commission, Rashid amassed unexplained wealth exceeding 5.5 billion Iraqi dinars (about $4.2 million) along with an additional $5.5 million in U.S. currency.

The court ordered Rashid to return the illicit gains and levied an equivalent fine, bringing his total financial liability to approximately $19.4 million. Judges also upheld a freeze on his movable and immovable assets, paving the way for seizure.

title: Friends with benefits: EU associate membership explained
content:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen surprised Brussels, and the world, during her 2026 State of the Union address by suggesting she wants to see Canada as an associate member of the EU.

European Parliament President Roberta Metsola, a Maltese member of von der Leyen’s center-right party, jumped on the idea. She suggested that Australia and New Zealand — which, like Malta and Canada, are Commonwealth countries — could also be candidates for the yet-to-be-defined category of EU associate membership.

While potentially attractive, the idea is neither simple nor well understood outside of EU policy circles. For now, it’s a political slogan only.

The closest existing model is the European Economic Area, in which Norway, Iceland and tiny Liechtenstein participate, as a way of accessing Europe’s single market and regulatory space.

Here, POLITICO explains why it’s so hard to get close to EU membership, and what rights and obligations would flow from any country pursuing such a deep set of ties:

Ursula von der Leyen’s proposal is best understood as an invitation to design a new arrangement for deeper relations between the EU and its trusted partners.

title: The Big Day Looms for Putin’s Election Fixers
content:
Sergei Kiriyenko became head of the Kremlin’s political bloc after the 2016 State Duma elections. His predecessor, Vyacheslav Volodin, lost his position partly because turnout in those elections fell below 50%, a show of popular apathy too notable to ignore.

Volodin had not wanted to overheat the system. But he worked hard to construct a network of sham public organizations around Putin, each offering unconditional support for the president and his policies. The All-Russia People’s Front was the clearest example.

Under Volodin’s model, a dependent or loyal electorate was expected to turn out on election day. This ensured predictability while also providing a measure of legitimacy. Protest-minded citizens, meanwhile, were expected to stay away from the polls and then draw the obvious conclusion: the authorities had won thanks to the votes of the loyal electorate.

title: Your AI doomsday questions answered: ‘Why aren’t these companies being held to account?’
content:
After a week of alarming warnings about artificial intelligence’s potential to destroy the world as we know it, our technology reporters answered your questions on the reality of the AI threat

IcommentthereforeIam asks: Given our senses, emotions, memory and moods, is it ever going to be accepted that humanly conscious AI is fantasy?

Dan: This is a serious question that has even rattled Richard Dawkins, the evolutionary biologist. He may not believe that God is real but he does believe that AI is conscious - or at least the chatbot he was using, which he called Claudia. “You may not know you are conscious, but you bloody well are,” he wrote.

And he’s not the first. In 2022 Google fired an engineer who went public with his belief that a company-developed AI had feelings. At the more troubling end of this belief, there are countless examples of people becoming overly attached to, and influenced by, AI chatbots – including cases of psychosis.

title: “A Clear Watering Down”: Drug Transparency Bill Stripped of Critical Provisions Ahead of Senate Vote
content:
Landmark legislation designed to alert consumers to where their drugs were made is headed for a full Senate vote, but safety experts say the transparency bill has been stripped of two of its most critical provisions.

The Clear Labels Act was introduced earlier this year by Sens. Rick Scott, R-Fla., and Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., after lawmakers and drug safety experts called for more transparency in the industry. Last year, a ProPublica investigation revealed that the U.S. kept importing generic drugs from foreign factories after inspectors had identified quality and safety lapses at the sites, including leaks, mold and contaminated water.

Medications made at these facilities were linked to thousands of reported adverse reactions in patients.

The bill aims to allow doctors and patients to see on the label exactly where a medication was made — details that had largely been withheld until now, even from Congress. Current generic drug labels often include only the location of the packager or distributor, which can be thousands of miles away from the actual manufacturer.

title: How a traditional Nordic way of eating could help you live longer
content:
We live in Denmark, which consistently ranks as one of the world’s healthiest countries. The modern Danish diet, however, may not be quite so world-leading – with many Danes consuming high levels of sugar, salt and convenience food.

Yet, go back a few generations and science is increasingly showing that many of the staple foods of our grandparents’ generation.

Think homemade rye bread, herring, root vegetables and berries – can significantly reduce your risk of chronic disease and help you live longer.

Often described as the Mediterranean diet of the north, the Nordic diet is a predominantly plant-based diet rooted in traditional Nordic foods.

Health Gap / Sundhedskløften is a collaborative series from The Conversation UK and Denmark’s Videnskab.dk exploring what the two countries can learn from each other when it comes to health and wellbeing.

From cycling and alcohol to inequality, healthcare and everyday habits, the series looks beyond hospitals and medical treatment to explore how culture, politics and society shape the way people live – and how healthy they are.

content:
Ahead of planned demonstrations marking one year since mass anti-corruption protests took place in the Philippines on 21 September 2025, Ritz Lee Santos III, Executive Director of Amnesty International Philippines, said:

“As people prepare to take to the streets once more to demand accountability for corruption, Philippine authorities must ensure the right to peaceful assembly is protected and refrain from using excessive force. The authorities must not repeat the mistakes of last year’s violent response to peaceful protest.

“One year on, protesters arrested during the 2025 demonstrations continue to face charges, while authorities have failed to thoroughly, independently and impartially investigate allegations of police violence.

title: Secure Messaging and AI Remain In Conflict Despite the Promise of TEEs
content:
Secure messaging platforms, like Signal, WhatsApp, and recently, encrypted RCS, operate on a straightforward assumption: the content at each end of a conversation is private to the participants in the conversation. End-to-end encryption helps provide the mathematical guarantees that the companies who operate these messaging platforms cannot access the contents of messages. But there’s no way to guarantee what happens once the message arrives on a phone. As more devices and services introduce more artificial intelligence (AI) features into messaging apps, that line begins to blur. 

When AI features are computed entirely on device, it’s less concerning. Yet sometimes the computing requirements are heavy enough that the computation has to be done on a company server. Tech companies tell us they have a solution for this: trusted execution environments (TEEs). But do server-side TEEs really solve the problem?

TEEs exist to serve many different functions, ranging from digital rights management (DRM) content protections to securely storing information in your phone's mobile wallet, but for our purposes, we’ll be focusing on how tech companies use them for their AI tools.

For the second year in a row, the administration has barred the Palestinian delegation from US travel for the forum

title: Türkiye: LGBT Rights Crackdown Strikes at Rule of Law
content:
(Istanbul, September 18, 2026) – The Turkish government’s major crackdown on groups and activists defending the rights of lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) people threatens the rule of law and fundamental rights in Türkiye, Human Rights Watch said today. 

On September 12-14, 2026, coordinated police raids targeted seven groups defending the rights of LGBT people and two supporting people living with HIV, as well as bars and nightclubs in Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, Aydın, and Mersin. Police arrested at least 112 people, with 82 still detained under court order. At least 24 of them are LGBT activists, founders or executives of the targeted groups, and one is a journalist.  

“This crackdown is a blatant attempt to criminalize and marginalize LGBT people and silence the groups that stand up for their rights,” said Benjamin Ward, deputy Europe and Central Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The Turkish government should immediately release LGBT activists and others arrested without credible evidence of criminal wrongdoing and end its campaign against LGBT groups.”

title: Georgia Court Sentences Ex-Security Chief to 13 Years in Prison in Corruption Case
content:
The former head of the State Security Service of Georgia was found guilty this week of accepting more than $2 million in bribes and sentenced to 13 years in prison, as a corruption crackdown continues against former senior officials from the ruling Georgian Dream party. 

Grigol Liluashvili, who headed the security service from 2019 until 2025, was arrested last December following raids on his home and those of two other former ruling party elites.

Tbilisi City Court Judge Nino Tarashvili on Wednesday found Liluashvili guilty of “accepting bribes on an especially large scale,” said the Prosecutor's Office of Georgia’s press release announcing the verdict. 

Liluashvili’s lawyer Lana Tsertsvadze reacted outside the courtroom, telling reporters it was an “unjust verdict” that she would appeal.

“The defense and Mr. Grigol Liluashvili anticipated an acquittal because there was not a single piece of evidence in the case to prove his guilt,” Tsertsvadze said in a video interview. “Mr. Grigol Liluashvili will seek to establish his innocence through legal avenues. This unfounded, unlawful, and unjust decision will be challenged in the Court of Appeals.”
snippet: The former head of the State Security Service of Georgia was found guilty this week of accepting more than $2 million in bribes and sentenced to 13 years in prison, as a corruption crackdown continues

title: Kremlin Vote-Fakers Crush the Liberals
content:
With Russia’s parliamentary elections now imminent, the registration and subsequent hurried removal of the liberal Yabloko’s federal list from the State Duma ballot stand out as the campaign’s most consequential event — both for democratic opposition inside and outside of the country and the Kremlin itself.

The crackdown on the only party openly calling for peace began months before the election, targeting its most prominent figures, and has continued throughout the campaign, which ends with voting from September 18-20. A recent poll by a small, independent research group with access to voters inside Russia suggests Yabloko could have won 20-25% of the vote had it remained on the ballot, challenging the Communist Party (KPRF) for second place behind United Russia.

The authorities have long had ample scope to “adjust” the ruling party’s result by transferring votes between tallies. In 2024, manipulation inflated Putin’s total by 22–25 million votes in the 2024 presidential vote, adding roughly a third to his actual vote count.

title: Why ProPublica Is Leaning Into Sports Investigations
content:
If you have seen the headlines of the major investigation we recently published, “The Dominican Baseball Factory,” you may have wondered: Why is ProPublica, with its serious-sounding mission of accountability and its focus on abuses of power, reporting on baseball?

The answer would be: Exactly.

Baseball fans have long marveled at how the Dominican Republic, a tiny island nation with a population akin to Ohio, has produced so many brilliant players — roughly 10% of the major league. Major League Baseball and the owners of its 30 teams have regularly harvested bumper crops of sluggers to build their rosters and their fanbase, including most recently the Toronto Blue Jays’ Vladimir Guerrero Jr., the New York Mets’ Juan Soto and the San Diego Padres’ Fernando Tatis Jr., whose playing contracts total more than $1.6 billion.  

Learn more about this story on ProPublica’s podcast “Paper Trail.”

But as with many such tales of extraordinary success, the origin story is much darker.

title: ”Ne syövät taloutemme aamupalaksi” – Kansanedustaja kehottaa nostamaan katseen taskulaskimesta
content:
Kansanedustaja Saara Hyrkön (vihr.) mukaan EU:n taloussääntöjen puolustuspoikkeamaa tulisi jatkaa myös vuoden 2028 jälkeen. Energiapoikkeaman Hyrkkö laajentaisi koskemaan ympäristöturvallisuutta.

Tiedotteessaan Hyrkkö patistaa hallitusta aktiivisiin toimiin EU:ssa. Hän toteaa seuranneensa viime kuukausien talouskeskustelua turhautuneena.

Kokoomusjohtoinen hallitus on tehnyt alijäämäisen budjetin ja toisaalla ehdotellut uusia veronalennuksia. Samaan aikaan liike nyt on ilmoittanut irtaantuvansa velkajarrusovusta. Vihreiden linja julkisen talouden vahvistamisesta ei Hyrkön mukaan ole muuttunut.

– Vihreät on alusta asti ollut kriittinen velkajarrua ja etenkin sen jyrkkää soveltamista kohtaan. Samaan aikaan näemme edelleen arvon laajapohjaisella yhteistyöllä ja tarpeen vahvistaa julkista taloutta, Hyrkkö sanoo.

KESKUSTELU velkajarrusta meni Hyrkön mukaan alunperin väärille raiteille, kun velkajarrusta alettiin puhua pakkopaitana. Hän uskoo, että tämä mielikuva yhdistettynä hallituksen vastuuttomaan talouspolitiikkaan on syönyt suomalaisten luottamusta politiikan kykyyn ratkoa isoja ongelmia.

title: EFF to Lawmakers: Ground AI Cybersecurity Rules in Best Practices
content:
With doomsday AI scenarios dominating the news, lawmakers are rightly concerned about reports concerning security breaches at major US AI labs, such as the OpenAI–Hugging Face incident and the many others reported in its aftermath. As they consider potentially regulating frontier AI, they should focus any new legislation on the immediate, demonstrated risks from those incidents. 

Post-incident reports show that the Hugging Face incident could have been mitigated or prevented by following longstanding cybersecurity best practices, like stronger sandboxing and monitoring. Any new legislation should focus on closing gaps in existing law to prevent AI companies from taking unreasonable risks with the public's security.

title: Georgia: Critics Jailed for Online Speech
content:
(Berlin, September 18, 2026) – Georgian authorities are using vague administrative offenses to jail or heavily fine people for online speech, deepening the government’s crackdown on freedom of expression, Human Rights Watch said today.

Since June 2026, a new Ministry of Internal Affairs unit has monitored social media and referred hundreds of posts to courts to be tried for speech-related charges, such as insult or profanity. In July, courts sentenced a journalist and an activist to 14 and 25 days of detention, respectively, for online statements deemed insulting, and in September, authorities opened proceedings against a blogger over a Facebook comment deemed profane. 

“Statements can be crude or disrespectful, but that does not justify jailing people for what they say about public officials,” said Hugh Williamson, Europe and Central Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Detention or substantial fines for nonviolent expression under vague rules, combined with monitoring social media, pose a serious threat to free expression in Georgia.”

title: How to Defeat Russia’s Shadow War
content:
Europe’s response to Russia’s increasingly ferocious attacks on Ukraine and a widening shadow war campaign against European NATO has been familiar: strategic restraint.

That strategy is increasingly outdated. Something new is needed.

Hybrid warfare operates in the space between strategic necessity and military constraint. Both Putin and his entourage are faced with a stalling front line, an unfolding fiscal crisis, and Ukrainian strikes reaching ever further into Russian soil that, in autocratic regime logic, demand an aggressive response, not the negotiating table. Putin must escalate, driven by the realities of regime survival, whether Europe shows restraint or not.

Jonathan Powell, the UK’s national security adviser, who helped negotiate the Good Friday Agreement in Northern Ireland nearly three decades ago, argued on September 13 that the Kremlin’s escalating reaction to Western pressure was “a sign of success” and that Europe should not “take its foot off the gas”.

While the shadow campaign against Europe does not prove Russia is buckling, it does reveal that it is willing to up the ante.

– Sen lupaan, että tässä kirjassa on paljon sellaista, josta et ole taatusti kuullut aikaisemmin. Minulle on elämän aikana sattunut monenmoista, kaikenlaisia kommelluksia, muutama läheltä piti -tilanne niin yksityiselämässä kuin politiikassa.

KIRJASSA katsotaan myös tulevaisuuteen, vuoteen 2035, jolloin Lindtmanin tytär täyttää 18 vuotta.

– Minkälaisen maan ja maailman me jätämme hänen ikäpolvelleen. Se on asia, joka sytyttää minut joka aamu.

Lindtman lupaa kirjassaan paljastaa myös kirjan nimen taustan.

content:

Temat för seminariet är duodji som näring och hur duodjis ställning som näring kan stärkas. Under dagen diskuteras möjligheterna att ha duodji som inkomstkälla och erfarenheter och synpunkter på hur förutsättningarna för duodji kan utvecklas delas. title: EU leaders visited Arktikum as a part of the European Arctic Summit held in Rovaniemi
content:
17.09.2026

  • Share on FaceBook
  • Share on LinkedIn

    • The European Arctic Summit was held in Rovaniemi 13-14 September 2026, where EU leaders gathered to address issues related to the Arctic region.

    The geopolitical significance of the Arctic continues to grow rapidly, and the aim of the European Arctic Summit held in Rovaniemi was to strengthen the EU’s common strategic approach to the region. Arktikum served as a meeting venue for the summit, where the EU leaders also got to visit the Arctic Opposites science exhibition by the Arctic Centre with the executive producer Nicolas Gunslay.

    In addition, EU politicians discussed with local representatives about current Arctic questions such as the impacts of climate change and the perspectives of the Sámi People’s, the EU’s only Indigenous People, to the changing state of the region. The Rector of the University of Lapland Antti Syväjärvi and the President of the Sámi Parliament of Finland Pirita Näkkäläjärvi took part in these discussions held in Arktikum. The President Näkkälärvi emphasized to European heads of state that sustainable Arctic security can’t be achieved without the people of the Arctic and vibrant Indigenous peoples.

title: Pragmatic principles for more rights-respecting age assurance architectures
content:
This is the second part of a two-part series in which we explore approaches to protecting children online while safeguarding privacy, security and the open web. Part one covers our concerns regarding age gates, and suggests alternative policy proposals that address the root causes of online harms. Part two explores better ways to build age assurance architectures that respect users’ rights and autonomy.

Across the world, legislation to introduce age gates and social media bans is proliferating. Many governments are still considering age restrictions a straight-forward and cost-effective tool to achieve their child safety goals. However, evidence is mounting that age assurance mandates pose risks to users’ privacy, security, free expression and access to  information, threaten the open web and competition, and undermine policymakers’ goals: enabling young people to have safe and trustworthy experiences online, while enabling the digital economy to grow.

title: Das sind die Top 10 Wikipedia-Artikel im August
content:
Im August 2026 wurden folgende Artikel in der deutschsprachigen Wikipedia besonders häufig aufgerufen:

Hayden Panettiere war eine US-amerikanische Schauspielerin und Sängerin. Besonders bekannt war sie für ihre Rolle als Cheerleaderin Claire Bennet in der Fernsehserie Heroes und als Juliette Barnes in der Serie Nashville. Schon als Kleinkind übernahm Panettiere kurze Rollen in TV- und Werbespots, später sprach sie offen über ihre Probleme mit Alkoholabhängigkeit und Depressionen.

Sie wurde nur 36 Jahre alt, die Umstände ihres Todes sind aktuell noch nicht abschließend geklärt. Ihr Wikipedia-Artikel wurde im August ganze 1.364.992-mal aufgerufen.

Am 12. August kam es vorwiegend über Grönland, Island, Spanien und dem Nordpolarmeer zu einer totalen Sonnenfinsternis. Ihren Höhepunkt erreichte sie westlich von Island im Atlantik, wo die Phase der totalen Verfinsterung ganze zwei Minuten und 18 Sekunden anhielt. In der spanischen Stadt Palma dauerte sie dagegen nur noch etwa eine Minute und 30 Sekunden.

title: New Resources from FADGI on Content Authenticity and Provenance for AI-impacted Content
content:
Today’s guest post is from Kate Murray of the Digital Collections Management & Services Division and leader of the FADGI Audiovisual Working Group.

The FADGI (Federal Agencies Digital Guidelines Initiative) AudioVisual Working Group is pleased to announce two new resources now open for public comment: TCR4CAP: Tiered Community Recommendations for Content Authenticity and Provenance, with a focus on LAM collections content impacted by artificial intelligence and the supporting technical assessment report, Content Authenticity and Provenance for Audiovisual Collections: An Environmental Review (also called CAP Environmental Review). Both work in tandem to assist cultural heritage institutions with decisions about documenting content authenticity and provenance (CAP), especially for content impacted by artificial intelligence (AI) in the stewardship lifecycle.

title: Europe heard Draghi. Now it has to act
content:
The report by Mario Draghi, The Future of European Competitiveness, published on 9 September 2024, was intended as a response to the widening gap between the European economy and its US and Chinese competitors.

The former president of the European Central Bank pointed to low productivity, insufficient investment in new technologies, high energy prices, fragmentation of the single market and difficulties in financing European companies.

Draghi called for a deeper single market, simpler regulation, better access to finance and the mobilisation of additional public and private investment. He estimated that the EU needed around €750–800 billion in additional investment every year — equivalent to 4.4–4.7% of EU GDP — to finance the transition and restore economic dynamism.

Two years later, the core of Draghi’s diagnosis has been broadly accepted in Brussels. The implementation of his prescriptions, however, tells a much less impressive story.

title: Meta ordered to remove UK deepfakes as oversight board criticises ‘inadequate’ safeguards
content:
Facebook told it was wrong in leaving up AI-generated videos of a Labour councillor and Muslim campaigner, amid calls to curb fakes

Meta’s “supreme court” has ordered the tech company to take down deepfake videos of a UK politician and a young Muslim woman from Facebook and do more to tackle AI-generated fake imagery.

A fake video showing a Labour party councillor in Scotland making inflammatory comments about refugees should not have been left up by Facebook, the board said. It also ruled that an AI-generated video of a Muslim campaign volunteer should have been removed after it falsely depicted her offering health advice while carrying out absurd exercises or eating junk food.

title: Oregon Lawmakers Seek to Open Up Affordable Housing Records Following ProPublica’s Reporting
content:
Two Oregon lawmakers want to end an unusual exemption in the state’s records law that has kept the public from learning how hundreds of millions of dollars in taxpayer money is spent on subsidized housing — and the effort has already landed key industry support.

Rep. Pam Marsh, chair of Oregon’s House Committee on Housing and Homelessness, told ProPublica that she plans to introduce legislation next year to eliminate a law that shields key details of state spending on low-income housing.

The southern Oregon Democrat said she didn’t realize the documents were being kept secret until reading about it in a ProPublica story. She said previous leaders of her committee told her they were also unaware.

“I think this is an issue that will have very broad interest,” Marsh said.

State Sen. Khanh Pham, a Portland Democrat and chair of the Senate Committee on Housing and Development, said she also wants the Legislature to tackle the issue in its next session.

title: “Eluteelt, Eva Lille. Kultuurisilla ehitaja” Jupiteris
content:
Sirp 35 aastat tagasi: 10.5.1991 Eval on juubel.

Legendaarne kultuurisilla ehitaja ja tugisammas Eva Lille tähistas tänavu 85. sünnipäeva. Soome Instituudil Eestis täitus 35. tegevusaasta. Instituudi sünnile ja algusaegade tegevusele andis ka Eva hiiglasliku panuse. Üle kuuekümne aasta Soome-Eesti sillal tegutsenud Eva unikaalne intervjuu on nüüd vaatamiseks Jupiteris.

1941. aastal sündinud Eva Lille on tuntud eesti kirjanduse soome keelde tõlkijana ning olulise eestvedajana Soome ja Eesti vaheliste sidemete avanemisel. Ta hakkas tooma eesti kultuuri suletud nõukogude ühiskonna varjudest soomlaste teadvusse ja aitas ühtlasi rajada alust sidemete sõlmimisele nende kahe maa vahel. Ta oli üks neist, kes asutasid Helsingi Tuglas-seura, mille büroo muutus 1991. aasta Moskva ebaõnnestunud riigipöördekatse ajal ”Eesti esimeseks välisministeeriumiks”.

title: Street art in Russia is dead and the country is full of monumental war art
content:
Abroad, artistic themes inevitably part with protest

Originally published on Global Voices

“War is now” street art by Philippenzo. Photo by Daria Dergacheva, used with permission.

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

Editor’s note: This article is  based on a presentation and interview with Russian street artist Slava PTRK , originally from Yekaterinburg, Russia, who currently lives abroad, in exile. Through the artists’ narrative, Global Voices traces how street artists in Russia — starting with protests in 2022 — were either pushed out of the country, or prosecuted and sent to jail. How has immigration changed protest art? What work are those abroad still able to do? Are others who remained in Russia now either silent or working for the state? What remains are small acts of protest.

The Heritage Management Organization (HERITΛGE) se complace en anunciar los 10 proyectos seleccionados para recibir apoyo a través de HerMaP México, su principal iniciativa para fortalecer la gestión del patrimonio cultural en la región fronteriza del norte de México.

Los proyectos seleccionados representan a Baja California, Sonora, Chihuahua, Coahuila, Nuevo León y Tamaulipas, garantizando así la representación de los seis estados que conforman el ámbito geográfico de HerMaP México en esta primera convocatoria de apoyos.

Los proyectos fueron seleccionados entre 115 solicitudes recibidas a través de una convocatoria abierta lanzada a principios de 2026, reflejando tanto la extraordinaria riqueza del patrimonio cultural de la región como el compromiso de las comunidades, profesionales e instituciones que trabajan para salvaguardarlo.

title: Embodied Freedom and Mutual Recognition: A Fichtean Foundation for Healthcare Ethics
content:
By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 17 September 2026 (IDN) — Beauchamp and Childress’ principlist framework has shaped biomedical ethics for more than four decades, providing clinicians and policymakers with a vocabulary centered on autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence, and justice. Its influence is undeniable: the four principles have become the default language of ethics committees, medical school curricula, and institutional policy.

Yet principlism’s strength—its broad flexibility and intuitive appeal—is also its deepest weakness. Designed as a “mid-level” approach that avoids metaphysical or theoretical commitments, principlism cannot provide a foundational account of healthcare ethics. Its principles lack justification beyond a shifting and often contested “common morality”; it offers no ontology of the human person; it cannot adjudicate conflicts among its own norms; and it reduces autonomy to little more than procedural respect for patient choice. Such limitations have long been acknowledged yet rarely addressed at their philosophical root.

title: IJ4EU Impact Award 2026 winners announced
content:
Two investigations into deadly “forever chemicals” are among the three winners of the 2026 IJ4EU Impact Awards, alongside a cross-border exposé showing how doctors sanctioned for malpractice are able to continue working after being banned elsewhere.

The winning teams of journalists each received €5,000 at the annual awards presented by the Investigative Journalism for Europe (IJ4EU) fund, which supports cross-border public-interest journalism in Europe.

In alphabetical order, the three equal winners are:

  • Bad Practice, by a consortium of 50 media outlets led by OCCRP, VG and The Times.
  • Factories on the Run: Inside the Global Trade that Moves PFAS Downstream, by Gianluca Liva, Marta Frigerio, Anna Violato, Filippo Tommasoli, Thomas Goorden and Varrun Sukhraj.
  • The Forever Lobbying Project, by a consortium of European media partners coordinated by Le Monde.

    • The jury also singled out Killing for the Photo, by Barbara Matejčić in collaboration with Natalija Jovanović and Ruben Brugnera, for special recognition.

    The winners were announced on September 17 in Budapest at IJ4EU’s annual UNCOVERED Conference, hosted this year by Goethe-Institut Hungary.

title: Vallan maantiede: Ovatko Yhdysvaltojen terveysdiilit syöttö Kiinan lapaan?
content:
Vuosi sitten Yhdysvaltojen hallinto julkaisi uuden strategian globaalin terveyden edistämiseksi. Strategiapaperin otsikkoon oli liitetty tuttu iskulause ”Amerikka ensin”. Samassa yhteydessä strategian toimeenpano siirrettiin terveysministeriöstä ulkoministeriöön.

Pian strategian julkistamisen jälkeen Trumpin hallinto lähestyi Afrikan maita. Se halusi nyt neuvotella kahdenvälisiä diilejä – aiesopimuksia, jotka mahdollistaisivat terveysavun jatkamisen, mutta entistä tiukemmilla ehdoilla.

Yhdysvalloille ei riittänyt pelkästään se, että jatkossa kehitysapuvarojen käyttöä syynättäisiin tarkemmin. Avun vastineeksi se halusi suoran pääsyn afrikkalaisten terveysdataan ja patogeeninäytteisiin, jopa mineraaleihin.

Mutta mikä on hinta sille, jos globaalia terveysapua ohjaavat ensisijaisesti Yhdysvaltojen intressit? Intressit, jotka ovat yhä useammin kaupallisia, tai ulko- ja turvallisuuspoliittisia.

Ja mitä riskejä sisältyy siihen, että Yhdysvallat vetäytyy monenkeskisestä yhteistyöstä, ja rakentaa rinnalle omia järjestelmiään, joissa sen edut menevät yhteisen terveysturvallisuuden edelle?

Huomataanko uusi pandemia ajoissa?

Vallan maantiede -podi julkaistaan yhteistyössä Maailman Kuvalehden kanssa.

title: Esittävän taiteen tukirakenteiden kehitysprosessi on käynnistynyt
content:
Joukko esittävän taiteen järjestöjä ja muita alan tukirakenteita on käynnistänyt keväällä 2026 yhteisen kehitystyön kohti tulevaisuuskestävää esittävän taiteen ekosysteemiä ja vaikuttavampaa yhteistoimintaa.

Järjestöt tunnistavat siiloutumisen ja ovat huolissaan siitä, miten jatkuvasti heikentyneet voimavarat riittävät tehtävien ja tarkoituksen toteuttamiseen. Kehitystyön ytimessä onkin kysymys, millaiset tukirakenteet palvelevat esittävää taidetta ja sen uudistumista sekä taiteentekijöiden moninaisen toimijakentän tarpeita pitkällä tähtäimellä – rakenteellisesti kestävällä tavalla.

Kehitysprosessi mahdollistaa keskenään erilaisten toimijoiden säännöllisen yhteen tulemisen ja yhteisen ajattelun. Työssä yhtä aikaa kerätään ja jäsennetään tietoa sekä kokeillaan ja kehitetään syntyviä ideoita käytännössä.

Esittävän taiteen järjestö- ja tukirakenteita edustavat yhteisöt osallistuvat kehitystyöhön kukin omista lähtökohdistaan ja tarpeistaan käsin. Prosessi on sen osallistujayhteisöille mahdollisuus vahvistaa yhteyttä kollegoihin ja luoda suhteita muihin toimijoihin samalla kun ymmärrys esittävän taiteen kentän tilannekuvasta ja omasta toiminnasta osana kokonaisuutta tarkentuu.

title: Houthi advance boosts Iran’s leverage over the US and Saudi Arabia – but may cost rebel group its legitimacy back in Yemen
content:
It took just a few days for Houthi forces to seize most of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, including the shores of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial Red Sea maritime choke point.

The offensive started on Sept. 3, 2026, with a push to cut the strategically important road linking the city of Taiz to the port of Mokha. By Sept. 11, Mokha, the town of Dhubab and the island of Mayyun, in the mouth of the strait, were under Houthi control.

The Yemeni rebel group seized some 2,100 square miles of territory, forcing more than 100,000 people to flee, according to the U.N., with many making the risky journey to nearby Djibouti by boats.

It is the largest shift in the front lines of Yemen’s civil war since a U.N.-brokered truce froze them in April 2022.

Most of the coverage has interpreted the offensive as a new lever for Iran – a key ally of the Houthis – in its ongoing war with the United States, or a fresh threat to Saudi Arabia and global shipping.

title: EU:n laajentumiskomissaari Marta Kos vierailee Helsingissä

Tapaamisissa keskustellaan Euroopan unionin laajentumispolitiikan kokonaisuudesta sekä Ukrainan, Moldovan ja Länsi-Balkanin maiden EU-jäsenyyspoluista. Suomi tukee EU:n naapuruston eurooppalaista integraatiota ja niiden demokratia- ja oikeusvaltiokehitystä, joiden merkitys korostuu nykyisessä haastavassa geopoliittisessa tilanteessa.

title: Erdogan muutti mielensä, hakee jatkokautta Turkin johdossa
content:
Turkin presidentti Recep Tayyip Erdogan aikoo hakea jatkokautta presidentinvaaleissa, jotka järjestetään todennäköisesti vuoden 2028 huhtikuussa, kertoo hänen avustajansa turkkilaismedian mukaan.

Vielä vuonna 2023 edellisvaalien aikaan Erdogan sanoi, että alkava viisivuotiskausi jäisi hänen viimeisekseen. Erdogan (s. 1954) on ollut Turkin presidenttinä vuodesta 2014 alkaen.

Normaaliaikataulun mukaan seuraavat vaalit järjestettäisiin toukokuussa, mutta maan parlamentin odotetaan aikaistavan niitä järjestettäväksi 16. huhtikuuta.

Uutistoimisto AFP:n ja uutissivusto al-Monitorin mukaan päätös sallisi Erdoganin hakea jatkokautta.

Hallitus väitti aiemmin, ettei vaalien aikaistaminen ollut sen suunnitelmissa.

title: ‘Doom Loop’: OpenAI and Microsoft Admits LLMs Are Destroying the Web and Built on Theft
content:
Executives working on AI at Microsoft and OpenAI admitted what its critics have been saying all along: Large language models are predatory pieces of technology that have been built on what a Microsoft executive called “an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions,” and the “largest theft of labor in human history.” An internal Microsoft document said generative AI products have created a “doom loop” that is killing “the entire web.” 

Those statements and a series of other mask-off moments feature heavily in an unredacted court filing that was unsealed Thursday in the behemoth New York Times vs OpenAI copyright lawsuit that has been winding its way through the court system for years. In a filing asking for summary judgment (basically, a filing with the court asking it to rule), lawyers for the New York Times laid out a series of admissions made by Microsoft and OpenAI executives in documents and depositions that until now had remained either sealed or redacted at the request of Microsoft and OpenAI.

title: Ignore human rights risks, face the consequences: Telenor under investigation for crimes against humanity in Myanmar
content:
Update: On September 17, 2026, Asker and Bærum District Court in Norway allowed a lawsuit against Telenor to proceed. The case was filed by the Justice & Accountability Initiative on behalf of people’s whose data was shared by Telenor with the Myanmar military.

On September 15, 2026, Norwegian authorities announced an investigation into Telenor for suspected crimes against humanity and sanctions violations in Myanmar following the 2021 military coup. For years, Access Now and civil society have raised the alarm over Telenor’s hasty and irresponsible departure from Myanmar and the potential human rights abuses should Telenor sell its Myanmar enterprise to the military-linked M1 Group.

The decision to file charges against Telenor follows a police complaint filed by Justice for Myanmar and ICJ Norway last year. Earlier this year, the Swedish human rights group Justice and Accountability Initiative (JAI), with the support of various Myanmar civil society organizations and EU-based groups, also filed a class-action lawsuit against Telenor.

title: US State Department must reverse decision to ban Palestine delegation from attending UNGA session in New York
content:
Responding to the US State Department’s announcement in a statement yesterday that it has, for the second consecutive year, barred the high-level delegation of the State of Palestine, including Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas, from attending the UN General Assembly in New York, Amnesty International’s Senior Director for Research, Policy, Advocacy and Campaigns, Erika Guevara Rosas said: 

“The decision by the US State Department to deny visas to a high-level delegation of the State of Palestine to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly must be reversed. The State Department’s statement makes it obvious: this decision is designed to punish the State of Palestine for pursuing international justice and accountability at international institutions, including through the International Criminal Court (ICC) and International Court of Justice (ICJ). This measure is part of a relentless campaign of reprisals against the very notion of international justice.

title: GoodBrother: not every brother is big
content:
On World Patient Safety Day, 17 September, we often think about preventing medical errors, infections or other risks in healthcare. But for older people living independently, safety can also mean knowing that help will arrive when something goes wrong, without giving up privacy, dignity or control.

This is where smart technology could make a difference. But it also raises an uncomfortable question: how much monitoring is too much?

The COST Action GoodBrother explored how cameras, microphones and artificial intelligence could support older people while respecting their fundamental right to privacy.

Imagine living alone in your eighties. A small camera could detect if you fall. A microphone could recognise signs of trouble and alert a carer. Smart technologies like these have enormous potential to help older people to live independently for longer.

But there is a problem. As soon as cameras and microphones enter the home, many people start to worry. Who can access the recordings? Who owns the data? Could helpful technology start to feel more like surveillance?

title: Humanitarian Archive Emergency Coalition: Get Involved Remotely!
content:
The DRP has been pleased to be part of a growing coalition concerned about the future of humanitarian archives amid challenges to foreign aid funding. 

In response to these concerns, a Steering Committee from around the world was convened by researchers at the University of Manchester’s Humanitarian and Conflict Response Institute and launched as the Humanitarian Archive Emergency Coalition. In addition to creating a Registry to document at-risk archives, the HAE has created a Digital Archiving Toolkit, a Landscape Report, and more. 

They’ve also been running five in-person regional workshops around the world to gather feedback from practitioners, archivists, researchers, and custodians. They will be conducting several online workshops at the end of the month and welcome more participation. Join one of three online workshops (2 hours each) based on your preferred language and time zone:

  • French – Wednesday 30 September, 16:00 CET (14:00 UTC / 10:00 Port-au-Prince)

title: "Call It Evil": Philosopher Susan Neiman on Why Moral Clarity Matters in the Trump Era
content:
We speak with moral philosopher Susan Neiman, author of the new book Call It Evil: Understanding the Trump Era. Neiman argues that evil — far from being an outdated religious concept — is a vital way to understand how injustice works in the world. The Trump administration’s abusive policies have been aided by a general reluctance to call them out as evil, part of how people are “brainwashed … by the idea that morality is for losers, suckers, fools,” she says.

“People worry that it’s polarizing, that it’s demonizing, and by that worry, we leave the strongest weapons we have in the language in the hands of people who are least responsible in using them,” says Neiman.

title: The next frontier for circularity is governance
content: Resource extraction has tripled since 1970, and on current trends, it could rise by a further sixty per cent by 2060 against 2020 levels. This will exacerbate the planetary crisis and drive economic risk, including price volatility and supply chain disruption. Linear waste, materials extracted, used once and discarded, costs the global economy €25.4 trillion a year, close to a third of global GDP. While circularity was expected to counter this trajectory, the Circle Economy’s Circularity Gap Report puts the world’s circularity rate at 6.9 per cent, the lowest figure the metric has recorded since its introduction in 2018.

title: California’s “Addictive Feeds” Law Violates Teens’ First Amendment Rights
content:
A California law that prohibits teens from receiving recommended social media content from other social media users violates their First Amendment rights, EFF argued this week.

The case, Meta v. Bonta, challenges SB 976, which requires that teen social media users get their parents’ permission before seeing other users’ recommended speech on their social media feeds. The legal challenge to SB 976 has largely centered on how the law violates social media services’ First Amendment rights to curate user-generated content and present it as they see fit.

But the friend-of-of the-court brief EFF filed along with the Center for Democracy & Technology and the Wikimedia Foundation shows that the law violates teen users’ First Amendment rights, too.

“SB 976 frustrates young people’s ability to use the internet to its full potential, prohibiting them from relying on tools that disseminate their speech and help them view and interact with other users’ speech,” the brief argues.

Recommendation systems have a dual purpose on social media: they help all users discover speech and content by other users, and to get their own speech in front of a wider audience.
snippet: A California law that prohibits teens from receiving recommended social media content from other social media users violates their First Amendment rights, EFF argued this week.

title: Woman Executed at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan
content:
According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan at dawn on Monday, September 14, 2026.

HRANA has identified the prisoner as Rezvan Asgharzadeh, a 45-year-old mother of six. On Sunday evening, one day before her execution, she was transferred from Dowlatabad Prison in Isfahan to Dastgerd Prison.

According to information received by HRANA, Asgharzadeh was arrested approximately six years and six months ago in connection with drug-related offenses. About two years ago, Branch 5 of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hemmat-Nejad, sentenced her to death. The sentence was subsequently upheld by the Supreme Court.

An informed source close to her family told HRANA: “During her imprisonment, Ms. Asgharzadeh memorized several sections of the Quran in hopes of qualifying for clemency, and until her final days she remained hopeful that her sentence would be commuted. Her name was initially included on the list of prisoners eligible for clemency. However, following a negative report submitted by Fatemeh Asgarian, the head of Dowlatabad Prison in Isfahan, her name was removed from the list.”

title: Växtbaserade alternativ till mejeriprodukter är i huvudsak säkra, men mer forskning behövs
content:
Växtbaserade alternativ till mejeriprodukter och veganska desserter som säljs i Finland håller i huvudsak en god livsmedelssäkerhetsnivå. Enligt den riskbedömning som genomfördes inom VEGETURVA-projektet av Livsmedelsverket och VTT var de mikrobiologiska riskerna i allmänhet mycket låga, och halterna av de undersökta mykotoxinerna låg under kvantifieringsgränserna. Samtidigt visar resultaten att konsumenternas förvaringspraxis, produkternas råvaror och förekomsten av vissa skadliga ämnen kan ha betydelse för säkerheten.

Användningen av växtbaserade alternativ till mejeriprodukter har ökat snabbt under de senaste åren. Trots att produkternas näringsmässiga egenskaper har undersökts ingående finns det fortfarande betydligt mindre information om deras livsmedelssäkerhet. Inom VEGETURVA-projektet, som genomfördes i samarbete mellan Livsmedelsverket och VTT, kartlades mikrobiologiska och kemiska risker i växtdrycker, fermenterade växtbaserade produkter och veganska desserter samt säkerhetsaspekter kopplade till deras användning.

title: Tallinnassa muurattiin uuden suomalaishotellin peruskivi
content:
Original Sokos Hotel Talsinki nousee aivan Tallinnan matkustajasataman tuntumaan, muutaman askeleen päähän Rotermannin korttelista. Sijainti keskellä satamasta kohti Tallinnan ydinkeskustaa kehittyvää uutta kaupunkialuetta on yksi hotellin tärkeimmistä lähtökohdista.

”Talsinkista tulee kahden kaupungin, Helsingin ja Tallinnan, yhteinen olohuone ja paikka, jossa kohdataan ja luodaan yhteisiä muistoja ja hienoja hetkiä. Olen erittäin iloinen, että saamme olla osa tätä arvokasta tulevaisuuden korttelia. Hankkeen eteen on tehty paljon työtä, käyty lukuisia keskusteluja ja rakennettu yhteisiä unelmia ja visioita. Tämän peruskiven muuraus tekee näkyväksi sen, kuinka yhteiset unelmamme muuttuvat konkreettiseksi rakentamiseksi”, sanoo Sokotel AS:n toimitusjohtaja ja Sokos Hotelsin Tallinnan hotellien johtaja Teemu Kilpiä.

Original Sokos Hotel Talsinki on S-ryhmän hotelliyhtiön Sokotelin toinen hotelli Virossa. Hotellivieraat pääsevät käyttämään myös Talsinki-korttelin hyvinvointi-, spa- ja kuntosalipalveluita. Suomen ja Viron sekä Helsingin ja Tallinnan välinen yhteys näkyy myös hotellin tunnelmassa ja sisustuksessa.

Longevity osaksi kaupunkielämää

title: Cross-border community in action: How the Historic Centre of Stolberg (Germany) came back to life
content:
After a mass flood in mid-July 2021 devastated the Historic Centre of Stolberg in the western part of Germany, causing severe damage to hundreds of buildings, the centre of the 500-year-old town was listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2022. Since its involvement in the 7 Most Endangered Programme run by Europa Nostra, the Historic Centre of Stolberg  has not only been successfully rebuilt, but strengthened its network and community in the process — a completely unexpected, and very welcome outcome of the selection. Europa Nostra sat down with Dr. Karl Schmeer, Chemist and Biologist, who was involved in the nomination of the site for the 7 Most Endangered Programme, to hear about the Historic Centre of Stolberg’s inspiring journey.

It was a bad situation, the Historic Centre of Stolberg was badly flooded. It happened at an unexpected time. It was mid-July, and it had been raining for six weeks, when suddenly two meters of water flooded the main streets. It was dangerous and rough. This was a wakeup call, everyone’s talking about climate change and the effects and now we saw it. Two days later, the city centre was devastated.

title: The Guardian view on the Nepal-Tibet floods: a spur to action on climate | Editorial
content:
New research links last month’s disaster to fossil fuel pollution. Supporting disaster-hit countries must be at the centre of climate politics

Following a familiar pattern, coverage of the glacier collapse on the Nepal-Tibet border three weeks ago has subsided with the initial shock. But while the world’s attention has shifted, Nepal remains in the midst of an appalling tragedy. As well as at least 1,300 people who are known to have been killed, more than 5,000 are missing, some of them trapped in tunnels linked to the 13 hydropower plants that were damaged by the floods. On Wednesday four bodies were recovered from one of these tunnels, with searches ongoing. Families of the missing people are desperate for news.

title: Jeffrey Barrettin tavoitteena on sairauksien havaitseminen aiemmin ja tarkemmin
content:
Jeffrey Barrett, the new Professor of Computational Predictive Medicine at the University of Helsinki and ELLIS Institute Finland, has a career spanning genomics, public health and industry. He uses AI methods and large-scale health data to identify practical and clinically relevant biomarkers.

For Barrett, the professorship represents a return to academia after several years in industry, but also an opportunity to bring new ways of thinking into academic research.

"I've been fortunate to have worked both in academia and in companies, and I think there is a lot we can learn from both worlds," he says.

Computational predictive medicine combines large-scale health data, molecular measurements and advanced AI methods to uncover biological signatures of disease. Rather than simply predicting who may become ill, the goal is to recognise emerging disease processes earlier and identify the patients most likely to benefit from preventive treatments.

title: US Revokes Limits on Power Plants’ Climate Pollution
content:
The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced on September 14 that it is repealing limits on climate-warming pollution from coal and gas-fired power plants, the second largest source of greenhouse gas emissions in the country.

By gutting the 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards, the EPA is eliminating most of the limits on power plants’ carbon emissions. The move is one of the Trump administration’s most significant attacks yet on the US government’s ability to confront the climate crisis and protect communities devastated by pollution.

The 2024 standards required existing coal plants and new gas plants to capture 90 percent of carbon emissions or shut down by 2039, which would have reduced carbon pollution by an estimated 1.38 billion metric tons through 2047. The Biden-era rule was also projected to help reduce power plants’ emissions of health-harming pollutants, including sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and fine particulate matter.

title: The End Of Upward Mobility
content: In April 1941, with the Wehrmacht in Paris and the Ribbentrop–Molotov pact still in force, the political theorist James Burnham published “The Managerial Revolution,” which famously declared that capitalism was finished. His claim was not that it ought to be finished, but that it was, as a matter of observable fact, being replaced. The successor system would not, however, be socialism, as he had hoped during his earlier days as a Trotskyist. Socialism, he argued, was a utopia: it required abundance, and since human wants are unlimited, abundance is unreachable.

title: Independent Journalism Is Critical For European Resilience
content:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen delivered the EU’s annual state of the union address on Wednesday, calling for the robust defense of European values and warning of the dangers of cognitive warfare, foreign propaganda, and disinformation powered by viral deepfakes. 

Shaped by social media algorithms and surging AI, the integrity of Europe’s information space has become a core security and economic concern as foreign adversaries and extremists seek to paralyze democracies. Von der Leyen promised to respond by toughening sanctions enforcement and putting more funds towards promoting the rule of law. 

Europe is right to treat these issues as a high-stakes, generation-defining challenge. But there was a key omission in her speech: Independent journalism is a precondition for democratic resilience, and supporting it must remain a priority for the EU. Journalism exposes the inner workings of the threats facing our institutions, and populates our public spaces with reliable, factual, nuanced information. It is the most durable answer Europe has to the disinformation and foreign interference the President warned against. Only an informed public can make free choices.

title: Six Convicted, €300M Confiscation Ordered in Mafia-Linked EU Tax Fraud
content:
A Milan court has sentenced six individuals to prison and ordered the confiscation of more than 300 million euros ($344.66 million) for their roles in a transnational tax fraud and money laundering syndicate tied to the Italian mafia, the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) announced on Thursday.

The convictions mark the latest judicial actions in "Operation Moby Dick," a massive EPPO investigation into a VAT carousel fraud scheme. Between 2020 and 2023, the network issued over 1.3 billion euros ($1.49 billion) in fake invoices for AirPods, laptops, and other electronics, resulting in 520 million euros ($597.35 million) in losses to EU and national budgets.

The Milan judge confirmed aggravated circumstances for the criminal syndicate’s aiding and abetting of a mafia association. According to the EPPO, one of the convicted defendants received illicit funds from a Camorra clan—which investigators previously linked to the Nuvoletta and Di Lauro groups—and funneled the money into the scheme to launder the mafia's proceeds.

title: How Reading Changes the Way Your Brain Works
content: Reading is unnatural. This will hardly come as a surprise to any child trying to put off his homework for just one more hour of watching other kids play Minecraft. Yet there really are implications worth considering if we accept that our cognitive systems didn’t evolve to process text in the same way as they evolved to handle vision and speech. Speaking on an evolutionary historical scale, “we haven’t had enough time to develop a dedicated reading brain,” says UCLA neuroscientist Rebecca Gotlieb in the BBC World Service video above. For the time being, in a kind of cognitive jerry-rigging, “we co-opt parts of the brain involved in vision and auditory processing and language and attention and affect.”

title: AI titans invited to Trump-Xi dinner
content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon plan to attend next week’s state dinner with President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, four people familiar with the event told POLITICO.

The executives’ attendance at the White House summit signals artificial intelligence will likely be a key talking point during negotiations and comes as fear the technology could destroy humanity has roiled the industry.

An OpenAI spokesperson, who confirmed Altman’s attendance, did not detail his goals for the summit and instead pointed to his recent comments that the two leaders could earn a Nobel Peace Prize if they reach a deal on AI. Another person, who was granted anonymity to speak on details not yet made public, confirmed Huang’s attendance, but did not provide details on his goals for the summit.

Amon, whose attendance was confirmed by a Qualcomm spokesperson, said the CEO will represent the company and “the strength of American technology leadership on the global stage.”

Anthropic declined to comment on whether it received an invitation. Spokespeople for Google, Meta and AMD did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: Vihreiden Mikkonen ja Pitko: Suomen tärkein luontopäätös valmistellaan pimennossa
content:
Hallitus salailee Suomen ennallistamissuunnitelman valmisteluja, kritisoivat vihreiden kansanedustajat Krista Mikkonen ja Jenni Pitko. Esimerkiksi Suomen suurin luontotyyppi, pohjoiset havumetsät, on poistettu nyt suunnitelmasta kokonaan.

Lisäksi lausuntokierrokselle lähetettiin kesällä muiden luontotyyppien, kuten soiden ja vesistöjen, osalta vain tiivistelmä, ei koko suunnitelmaa eikä vaikutusten arviota, mikä tekee Pitkon mukaan asiallisen lausunnon antamisen lähes mahdottomaksi.

He vaativat EU:lle valmisteilla olevalle suunnitelmaluonnokselle kunnollista lausuntokierrosta.

"Hallitus on lähettämässä komissiolle suunnitelman, jossa ei ole kerrottu, miten Suomi tulee varmistamaan luonnon tilan elpymisen ja luontokadon pysäyttämisen. Suunnitelmassa on metsien kohdalla tyhjä rivi, vaikka pitkälti metsissä ratkaistaan luontomme monimuotoisuus, sillä kolmasosa uhanalaisista lajeistamme ovat metsälajeja", korostaa Krista Mikkonen tiedotteessa.

"Kyse on Suomen suurimmasta luontotyypistä ja tärkeimmästä luontoa koskevasta päätöksestä vuosikymmeniin. Silti sen tulevaisuudesta päätetään suljettujen ovien takana. Tämä ei ole avointa lainvalmistelua, vaan sen vastakohta", Pitko sanoo.

title: Matias Karsikas: Nord i blom
content:
Tid: 17/10–12/12 2026, vernissage lördagen den 17/10 kl. 13
Plats: Finlandsinstitutets galleri, Snickarbacken 4, Stockholm
Galleriets öppettider: tis–ons kl. 11–18 samt fre–lör kl. 11–15
Fri entré.

Varmt välkommen på vernissage lördagen den 17/10 kl. 13.00 i konstnärens närvaro!Samma dag invigs den nya barnavdelningen på Finlandsinstitutets bibliotek. Utställningen är öppen för publiken mellan kl. 11 och 15 på lördag.

Matias Karsikas glaskonst visas i oktober–november även i en utställning på Galleri Glas i Stockholm. Utställningen Tusen sjöars glöd öppnar den 22/10. Läs mer om utställningen hos Galleri Glas.

I oktober öppnar utställningen Nord i blom med den finska skulptören Matias Karsikas i Finlandsinstitutets galleri. I utställningen presenteras Karsikas blomsterinspirerande glasskulpturer samt ett ryaliknande verk i keramik, en teknik som är karakteristisk för konstnären.

Naturen är ett återkommande tema i Matias Karsikas arbete. Konstnären är särskilt intresserad av spänningen mellan naturen och den den mänskligt skapade världen. För Karsikas framstår naturen inte som en romantisk idyll, utan som en kontinuerlig process av överlevnad, skörhet och motståndskraft på samma gång.

title: Matias Karsikas: Nord i blom

Tervetuloa näyttelyn avajaisiin lauantaina 17.10. klo 13 taiteilijan läsnäollessa! Samaan aikaan talossa juhlistetaan Suomen Tukholman-instituutin kirjaston uuden lastenosaston avajaisia. Näyttely on avoinna yleisölle lauantaina klo 11–15 välisenä aikana.

Matias Karsikkaan lasitaidetta on esillä myös tukholmalaisen Galleri Glasin 22.10. avautuvassa lasitaidenäyttelyssä Tusen sjöars glöd.

Instituutin katutasossa avautuu suomalaisen kuvanveistäjän Matias Karsikkaan näyttely Nord i blom. Esillä on Karsikkaan kukka-aiheisia lasiveistoksia ja taiteilijalle ominaisella tekniikalla toteutettu keramiikkaryijymäinen teos.

Luonto on Matias Karsikkaan työskentelyssä usein toistuva teema. Taiteilijaa kiinnostaa erityisesti luonnon ja ihmisen rakentaman maailman välinen jännite. Luonto ei näyttäydy Karsikkaalle romanttisena idyllinä, vaan jatkuvana selviytymisen prosessina: haurautena ja sitkeytenä samanaikaisesti.

title: The long journey from ‘Indigenous’ to citizen in Mozambique
content:
From “Indigenous” to achieving citizenship, the story of resistance, transformation, and rights in Mozambique.

Originally published on Global Voices

Photo taken by Speak Media Uganda. Used under the Pexels license.

Under the Portuguese Empire (roughly 1505 until 1975), the word “Indigenous” was not just a descriptive word for the African population of Mozambique. It was a legal category that determined rights, duties, and life possibilities. For Africans in Mozambique — including communities such as the Ronga, Changan, and others in the region — the colonial experience was characterized by deep inequality before the state. Being African and born in Mozambique did not entail being treated as a citizen with the same rights as a European.

The Portuguese colonial system established a distinction between the “Indigenous,” “assimilated,” and  Portuguese citizens. Most of the African population remained in the category “Indigenous.” Access to formal education, qualified employment, public administration, and other opportunities was much more limited. The education system particularly revealed this inequality.

title: Ten Heritage Projects in N. Mexico Receive Funding
content:
The Heritage Management Organization (HERITΛGE) is delighted to announce the 10 projects selected to receive funding through HerMaP Mexico, its major initiative to strengthen cultural heritage management across Mexico’s northern border region.

The selected projects represent Baja California, Sonora, Chihuahua, Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas, ensuring that all six states within HerMaP Mexico’s geographic scope are represented in this first round of funding.

The projects were chosen from 115 applications submitted through an open call launched in early 2026, demonstrating both the extraordinary richness of the region’s cultural heritage and the commitment of communities, practitioners and institutions working to safeguard it. 

The selected initiatives offer a window onto the remarkable diversity of northern Mexico. They encompass heritage ranging from traditional farming techniques and gastronomic traditions to crafts, music, memorial sites, museums and the photographic documentation of intangible cultural heritage. They are rooted in landscapes that stretch from ocean coasts and vast deserts to mountain regions and complex urban environments.

title: Your robotic vacuum is a witness: What home robots mean for evidence, privacy and the law
content:
A husband in Taiwan suspected his wife of having an affair. In September 2023, he found a used toothbrush at their holiday home, and garage video showed an unfamiliar man driving his wife there. Three months later, he opened their robot vacuum’s app to speak with her and saw an intimate encounter through its live camera.

He recorded the feed and used it to win about US$16,000 from his wife and her lover for infringing on his marital rights. Then the Taoyuan District Court sentenced him to five months in jail and fined him roughly $4,700 for recording private activity without consent.

Both rulings are defensible. Together, they expose a troubling gap: Devices in homes now generate evidence continuously and often invisibly, while the governing law remains a patchwork. As faculty members in a school of interdisciplinary forensics, we see such cases where forensic practice meets law that has not kept pace.

A modern robot vacuum is a mobile sensor platform. Some models combine cameras, microphones, laser navigation and remote video access, while app-connected models create detailed floor maps and cleaning histories. Their data may also reach manufacturers’ servers.

title: Kansanedustaja Vornasen pestin jatko halutaan eduskunnan käsittelyyn
content:
Joukko kansanedustajia eri puolueista on esittämässä, että eduskunta käsittelee kansanedustaja Timo Vornasen (tv.) jatkon tehtävässään. Asiasta kertoo STT:lle vasemmistoliiton kansanedustaja Mai Kivelä, joka on ollut asiasta yhteydessä muiden puolueiden edustajiin.

- Hän on syyllistynyt mielestäni erittäin vakaviin ja aika poikkeuksellisiin rikoksiin, joten olisi todella erikoista, jos eduskunta ei tähän millään tavalla reagoisi, Kivelä sanoo.

Vornasen ehdollisesta vankeusrangaistuksesta tuli heinäkuussa lainvoimainen. Hän ampui pistoolilla maahan helsinkiläisravintolan ulkopuolella keväällä 2024.

Kivelän mukaan tapauksen käsittelyä on hänen lisäkseen vaatimassa edustajia ainakin kokoomuksesta, SDP:stä ja vihreistä.

- Esitämme eduskunnalle, että tätä käsitellään. Sitten perustuslakivaliokunta tekee lausunnon, jonka jälkeen asiaa käsitellään täysistunnossa, Kivelä sanoo.
