title: ‘Flock City PD:’ The Fake Flock-Owned ‘Police Department’ That Searched Real Cameras for Real People
content:
Flock created a fake police department called “Flock City PD” that it used to search a series of live automated license plate readers in several U.S. cities during demonstrations of its surveillance system’s capabilities, public records show. The records show that Flock City PD searched real cameras for people holding signs, “crowds,” people wearing masks, and more, according to audit logs shared with 404 Media. 

Flock City PD also searched extremely sensitive queries, which Flock told 404 Media were done to prove that the system would not actually perform these searches and that its moderation tools worked. These searches included “coexist bumper sticker,” “vehicle a pretty girl would drive,” “white truck with a trump sticker,” “religious cars,” “Star of David,” and “don’t tread on me flag.”

title: Global: Women Human Rights Defenders take their fight to the UN during week-long advocacy meeting
content:
Women Human Right Defenders (WHRDs) from around the world will be gathering in Geneva from 21 to 25 September, to learn about the UN Human Rights Council, advocate for their rights and amplify their own stories.

The week-long training, known as the Women Human Rights Advocacy Week, is co-organized by nine human rights organizations including Amnesty International (see below for full list). It is aimed at providing participants with practical tools to understand the Human Rights Council, while offering guidance on how to engage with it strategically and advocate for change in their communities.

“The women attending are risking their lives every day to protect their communities from climate change, greedy corporations and land theft,” said Lisa Maracani, Amnesty International’s researcher on human rights defenders. “Their knowledge is crucial to ensuring bodies such as the Human Rights Council remain effective, while the WHRD Advocacy Week is designed to provide these women with the tools and strategies to advance their advocacy on this global stage.”

title: "Fast Food Nation," Mystery Meat & Trump's Dismantling of U.S. Food Safety System: Eric Schlosser
content:
Amid growing concerns over food safety in the United States, President Donald Trump last month authorized the duty-free importation of 660 million pounds of cheap beef trimmings that will get mixed in with other cuts to make ground beef. Imported beef and pork were once labeled with their country of origin, but Congress voted in 2015 to end that requirement, so customers at the grocery store will have no way to identify this “mystery meat,” which is coming mostly from Brazil. President Trump’s proclamation in August came just a day after he met in the White House with Joesley Batista, whose family controls the Brazilian company JBS, the largest beef producer in the world. JBS is notorious for food safety violations and admitted in 2017 to bribing thousands of Brazilian officials for favorable treatment.

“It smells like a pretty corrupt deal,” says investigative journalist Eric Schlosser. He says Trump’s move is “basically screwing over American ranchers,” and the imported beef is “some of the meat most likely to be contaminated.”

title: Hossein Molaei Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison
content:

Based on information received by HRANA, Molaei, who is currently held in Greater Tehran Prison, was sentenced by Branch 29 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court to 15 years in prison on the charge of “supporting Israel.”

An informed source familiar with his situation told HRANA: “Mr. Molaei is in a difficult financial situation and cannot afford the cost of an attorney. Accordingly, he needs access to legal counsel to pursue the judicial proceedings in his case and appeal the sentence issued against him.”

Hossein Molaei, 50, was arrested by security forces in March 2026 and transferred to Greater Tehran Prison.

HRANA is reviewing details regarding the specific acts underlying the charge brought against him.

title: Kasvipohjaiset maitotuotteiden vaihtoehdot pääosin turvallisia, mutta lisää tutkimusta tarvitaan
content:
Suomessa kaupan olevat kasvipohjaiset maitotuotteiden vaihtoehdot ja vegaaniset jälkiruoat ovat elintarviketurvallisuudeltaan pääosin laadukkaita. Ruokaviraston ja VTT:n VEGETURVA-hankkeessa tehdyn riskinarvioinnin mukaan tuotteiden mikrobiologiset riskit olivat yleisesti vähäisiä ja tutkittujen mykotoksiinien pitoisuudet jäivät määritysrajan alle. Samalla tulokset osoittavat, että kuluttajien säilytyskäytännöillä, tuotteiden raaka-aineilla ja eräiden haitta-aineiden esiintymisellä voi olla merkitystä turvallisuuden kannalta.

Kasvipohjaisten maitotuotteiden vaihtoehtojen käyttö on viime vuosina lisääntynyt nopeasti. Vaikka niiden ravitsemuksellisia ominaisuuksia on tutkittu paljon, turvallisuudesta on ollut saatavilla selvästi vähemmän tietoa. Ruokaviraston ja VTT:n yhteistyössä toteutetussa VEGETURVA-hankkeessa selvitettiin kasvijuomien, kasvipohjaisten jogurttityyppisten tuotteiden sekä vegaanisten jälkiruokien mikrobiologisia ja kemiallisia riskejä sekä tuotteiden käyttöön liittyviä turvallisuuskysymyksiä.

title: Iran school bombing: grounds to believe US was behind atrocity, UN finds
content:
Fact-finding mission says military strikes on school and sports facility in ⁠February constitute war ⁠crimes

A UN fact-finding mission has determined there are reasonable grounds to believe the US was behind military strikes on a school and a sports facility in Iran in ⁠February that killed 120 children, and that these constituted war ⁠crimes.

The school strike, which killed 156 civilians including 120 children, involved a US Tomahawk missile that collapsed the roof of the Shajareh Tayyebeh primary school, which the UN said was “clearly identifiable”, in Minab, Hormozgan province, on 28 February.

title: Symposium: Indigenous Relationships with Time
content:
The MultiBEING Justice Centre of Excellence will kick-off at the University of Helsinki. CoE organizes its first scientific symposium on Monday September 28th, 2026 and engages with Indigenous notions of time by distinguished international speakers. 

The symposium addresses the connections and lineages of beings. Conceptions of time shape how relationships with other beings are lived, valued, and perceived. Non-linear time is a key aspect of understanding Indigenous relational onto-epistemologies. The speakers foreground philosophies of time, seasonalities, traditional calendars, ancestralities, astronomy, and diverse temporalities and timelines. What role do they play in reconsidering multibeing flourishing and human responsibility beyond humans?

title: Satire Can be a Crime in Kazakhstan
content:
Satirist and political commentator Azamat Omarov, who had been in pre-trial detention in Kazakhstan since mid-April on “inciting discord” charges, struck a plea bargain with the prosecution, under the terms of which he pled guilty, and on September 15, was released.

While Omarov avoided what could have been a long and unjustified prison sentence, he did not walk out of the courtroom a free man.

He will serve a suspended three-and-a-half-year prison sentence. He is also banned from engaging in socioeconomic and political activities for five years, which includes activities such as monitoring trials, according to his lawyer. He will not be able to resume his political satire show “Akhual Segodnya,” (The Situation Today) on YouTube, nor enjoy his fundamental right to express a social or political opinion on any online platform for the next five years. Should he violate the terms of his plea bargain he risks going to prison.

It is hard to overstate how unjust Omarov’s sentence is, even if he is not languishing in prison.

title: How to Track Down People Who Don't Want to Be Found
content:
Whether digging into a corrupt official or trying to unmask the owner of a shady shell company, investigating a person often starts with just a handful of clues.

You may have an old phone number, a name, or a face in the background of a social media post. Taking those scattered breadcrumbs and building them into a full dossier on an individual takes a systematic approach, and is all part of a day's work for the investigative researchers at OCCRP who support journalists across the network. 

This playbook lays out the basic methods, databases, and digital tricks our team uses to track down people who don’t want to be found. No matter what kind of story you're digging into, these steps will help you safely and effectively build a profile of whoever you're looking for. 

Before diving into a digital people-search, a word of warning: setting up basic security measures is essential to protect yourself.

title: Former Maduro Ally Pleads Guilty in US to $195M Money Laundering Scheme
content:
A Miami federal court brought a decade of investigative reporting to a close on Wednesday as Colombian-born businessman Alex Saab pleaded guilty to money laundering—years after Venezuelan news outlet Armando.info first began uncovering his state corruption schemes.

Saab, a top financial ally of ousted Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro, admitted to using the U.S. financial system to launder bribes connected to Venezuela’s Local Committees for Supply and Production (CLAP)—a state program meant to distribute food to impoverished communities. He faces up to 20 years in federal prison and has agreed to forfeit $195 million, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.

The guilty plea serves as a vindication for Armando.info, a local investigative news outlet and OCCRP member center. More than  nine years ago, the outlet pioneered reporting that brought Saab out of the shadows, exposing his ties to multimillion-dollar state contracts and the delivery of low-quality food to vulnerable populations.

At the time, Saab and the Maduro government vehemently denied the links. Saab sued the Armando.info team in Venezuela, arguing he had no connection to the CLAP program.

title: An In-Depth, Immersive Journey Through the Bayeux Tapestry
content:
With the Bayeux Tapestry now on display at the British Museum, Deep Down History presents a deep dive into the embroidery’s full story:

“The Bayeux Tapestry is one of the most remarkable survivals of the Middle Ages — a 70 metre embroidered account of the events leading to the Norman Conquest of England in 1066, culminating in the Battle of Hastings. This video tells the Tapestry’s story in full, using Charles Stothard’s early colour reproduction, presented here as a seamless scroll for the first time. We follow Harold Godwinson’s fateful journey from Edward the Confessor’s court to Normandy, his later seizure of the Crown, and William the Conqueror’s invasion. Beyond its political messaging, the Tapestry is also bursting with medieval history, including jokes, fascinating technical details, and a warning for those who break their promises…”

title: Parents, privacy, parliaments: The battle begins for von der Leyen’s social media ban
content:
BRUSSELS — Ursula von der Leyen’s bill to keep young Europeans off social media is an ambitious response to the growing outcry over the potential harm of TikTok, Instagram and other online platforms. Making the restrictions a reality will require a whole new level of ambition.

The European Commission must now negotiate with national governments and technologists to figure out exactly how to impose a law across Europe that would ban kids under 13 from social media, and severely restrict access for those under 15 — all without trampling on privacy of young and old alike in the process of verifying users’ age. 

Reducing the harms of social media on youth has been a top priority for the Commission president, a medical doctor and mother of seven who has repeatedly decried the internet’s impact on the health of minors since her 2025 State of the Union speech.  

“If a platform wants to access the children or the teenagers, the minors, they have to prove first that they are safe,” she told reporters on Thursday as she officially unveiled the EU Kids Act, the day after again touting her leadership on the issue in this year’s annual address.

title: Bensalasku ei oikeastaan kasva, vaan erääntyy
content:
Markus Wasara

Donald Trump haluaa polttoaineiden hinnan alas, kun Ukraina iskee Venäjän jalostamoihin, Lähi-idän kriisi heiluttaa öljymarkkinoita ja amerikkalainen autoilija näkee seuraukset pumpulla.

Politiikasta reaktio on tuttu: näin kallista polttoaineen ei pitäisi olla. Mutta ehkä kiinnostavampi kysymys on, miksi totuimme ajattelemaan, että sen edes pitäisi olla halpaa.

Sadan vuoden ajan bensiinin ja dieselin hintaa on kutsuttu markkinahinnaksi, vaikka suuri osa niiden todellisista kustannuksista on jätetty hinnan ulkopuolelle. Totuimme ajattelemaan polttoaineen hintapiikkejä poikkeuksina. Sota syttyy, öljyreitti häiriintyy, jalostamo räjähtää tai tuottajamaa sulkee hanojaan, ja bensiinin hinta karkaa hetkeksi “normaalilta” tasoltaan.

Tässä ajattelussa on yksi ongelma: normaaliksi kutsuttu hinta ei koskaan ollut normaali markkinahinta.

Se oli hinta, josta huomattava osa laskusta puuttui.

title: Big AI is trying to own the pathway to work. Universities shouldn’t play along | Ella Hafermalz
content:
Universities need to protect their position in education so that students have an independent pathway to employment

AI companies like OpenAI are insinuating themselves into the pathway from education to work. Soon they may claim it entirely, a disastrous result for students.

We know that students are using AI at school and at university. In conversations with those I teach, I’m struck by the trust many place in it. They turn to ChatGPT and similar tools for personal problems as well as study help. Some even doubt their abilities without AI.

Ella Hafermalz is an associate professor of work and technology at the Kin Center for Digital Innovation at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

title: Tusen sjöars glöd – finsk glaskonst på Galleri Glas
content:
Tid: 22/10 – 13/11 2026, vernissage 21/10
Plats: Galleri Glas, Nybrogatan 34, Stockholm
Galleriets öppettider: tis–tors kl. 12–18, fre kl. 12–17, lör kl. 12–16
Fri entré.

På Galleri Glas i Stockholm öppnar utställningen Tusen sjöars glöd, som presenterar finländsk samtida glaskonst av Matias Karsikas, Harri Koskinen, Ilkka Suppanen och Renata Schirm. Utställningen har genomförts i samarbete med Finlandsinstitutet. Samtidigt visas Matias Karsikas separatutställning Nord i blom i Finlandsinstitutets galleri.

Berättelsen om Finland som glasland börjar inte med glas. Den börjar med is. Finland formgavs under istiden av det massiva istäcke som stötvis drog sig undan, plöjde upp tusentals sjöar, rullade fram rullstensåsar, forslade grus och sand i strida smältvattenströmmar, skrapade räfflor i stenhällar och slängde ut strimmor av öar i yttersta havsbandet. Sedan kom tomhet. Och därefter skogen.  Veden. Glöden. 

I denna utställning möts fyra finländska glaskonstnärer som tar glaskonsten vidare i starkt personliga uttryck. Det samtida finska konstglaset är djupt rotat i sin historia, och får här form av konstnärer som utmanar materialets gränser.

title: Tusen sjöars glöd – suomalaista lasitaidetta Galleri Glasissa
content:

Tukholmalaisessa Galleri Glasissa avautuu suomalaista nykylasitaidetta esittelevä näyttely Tusen sjöars glöd. Näyttelyyn osallistuvat taiteilijat Matias Karsikas, Harri Koskinen, Ilkka Suppanen ja Renata Schirm ja se on toteutettu yhteistyössä Suomen Tukholman-instituutin kanssa. Samaan aikaan instituutin omassa galleriassa on esillä Matias Karsikkaan yksityisnäyttely Nord i blom.

Kertomus Suomesta lasitaiteestaan tunnettuna maana ei ala lasista. Se alkaa jäästä. Suomi muovautui jääkaudella valtavan mannerjään vaikutuksesta. Jääpeite vetäytyi syrjään nykäyksittäin, uurtaen maahan tuhansia järviä, muovaten harjuja, kuljettaen soraa ja hiekkaa voimakkaiden sulamisvesivirtojen mukana, raapien kalliopintoihin uurteita ja ripotellen saarivanoja ulkosaariston äärille. Sitten tuli tyhjyys. Sen jälkeen metsä. Polttopuut. Hehku.

title: Why Hispanic Americans are losing faith in the American Dream
content:
President Donald Trump won 43% of the Hispanic vote in 2024, up from 35% in 2020 – a big gain for Republicans. Now, as the midterms approach, Hispanic Americans across party lines are losing faith in the American Dream, and his administration’s immigration crackdown appears to be part of the reason.

Arrests by Immigration and Customs Enforcement of people with no criminal record are surging. Federal immigration agents have shot at nearly two dozen people – most of them Latino – since last year, according to The New York Times. Those include the fatal shootings of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Maine.

This climate of aggressive immigration enforcement may be affecting Hispanic Americans’ sense of belonging and their belief that they can pursue a better life in the United States. The Public Religion Research Institute 2026 survey on American identity asked more than 5,000 adults about their thoughts on the American Dream: the idea that if you work hard, you’ll get ahead. Just 40% of Hispanic Americans say that dream holds true today, down from 52% just two years ago.

title: Tarkastusvaliokunta: Valtio-omistajaa olisi pitänyt informoida Uniper-kaupoista paremmin ja ajantasaisemmin
content:
Energiayhtiö Fortumin olisi pitänyt informoida valtio-omistajaa paremmin ja ajantasaisemmin Uniper-kaupoistaan, arvioi eduskunnan tarkastusvaliokunta mietinnössään.

Valtion omistajaohjauksen tulee valiokunnan mukaan toimia siten, että Suomen turvallisuuden ja huoltovarmuuden kannalta keskeiset toiminnot eivät vaarannu. Se esittää eduskunnalle lausumaa, jonka mukaan valtio-omisteisten yhtiöiden hallituksissa tulee olla valtio-omistajan edustus. Lisäksi olisi erittäin tärkeää huolehtia siitä, että valtio-omistajaa edustavat jäsenet ovat päteviä toimimaan hallituksissa.

Mietinnön mukaan Suomen energiansaannin kannalta kriittinen Fortum oli vaarassa jopa kaatua Uniper-kauppojen johdosta. Yhtiön tappiot olivat noin 6 miljardia euroa ja se menetti sijoituksensa käytännössä kokonaan.

title: University Rescinds Job Offer to Activist Who Allegedly Wiped Phone Before DHS Could Search It
content:
Georgia State University has rescinded a job offer given to a high profile activist who is currently fighting a case in which he allegedly wiped a security-focused Android phone before Customs and Border Protection (CBP) could search it. The case, which 404 Media first covered and has now received widespread and national attention, has important ramifications for privacy and when someone can still be charged with an offense even if authorities don’t have suspicion of any specific crime.

Earlier this month, activist Samuel Tunick and a group of supporters delivered a “demand letter” to the university. That letter, which Tunick shared with 404 Media, says he explained to the university he was facing a pending charge, which he describes as “an instance of textbook political repression, and a high profile civil liberties case.”

While delivering the letter, supporters held signs saying, “GSU sides with Trump,” and “Digital Privacy Under Attack!”

content:
Kouvolan kirjaston palveluverkkosuunnitelma vuosille 2027–2035 etenee liikunta- ja kulttuurilautakunnan käsittelyyn 22.9.2026. Esityksessä ehdotetaan omatoimiaikojen lisäämistä Elimäen ja Jaalan kirjastoihin, Korian ja Haanojan kirjastojen lakkauttamista, sekä tilamuutoksia Myllykosken ja Elimäen kirjastoihin. Tavoitteena on turvata kirjastolain mukaiset palvelut, vahvistaa lukutaitoa ja sopeuttaa palveluverkkoa kaupungin väestökehitykseen, taloustilanteeseen ja tilojen käyttöön.

Sivistysjohtajan esityksen mukaan nykyisissä tiloissaan jatkaisivat Kouvolan pääkirjasto, Kuusankosken kirjasto, Inkeroisten kirjasto ja Valkealan kirjasto. Myös kirjastoauton toiminta jatkuu mutta reitit suunnitellaan uudelleen muuttuvan palveluverkon mukaisesti.

title: Suullinen osa yo-kokeeseen
content:
Ylioppilastutkintolautakunta on käynnistänyt vieraiden kielten ja toisen kotimaisen kielen kokeiden suullisen osan valmistelun. Suullisesta osasta on järjestetty keväällä 2026 kenttätestejä, joissa on todettu, että se on teknisesti mahdollinen toteuttaa. Vaatii kuitenkin vielä kehittämistyötä, ennen kuin suullisia tehtäviä saadaan yo-kokeisiin. Yhtenä osana tätä työtä lautakunta on järjestänyt sidosryhmätapaamisia muun muassa kieltenopettajien ainejärjestöjen kanssa alkusyksystä 2026. Kun valmistelu on pidemmällä, lautakunta pyytää lausuntoja esimerkiksi kokeiden käytännöistä ja käyttöönoton aikataulusta.

Lähtökohtana kehittämistyössä on, että kokelas voi kuunnella suullisen vastauksensa ja halutessaan äänittää sen uudestaan. Arvostelussa pääpaino on viestin välittymisessä. Ennen kuin suullinen osa tulee ylioppilaskokeisiin, kokelaat ja opettajat voivat harjoitella suullisia tehtäviä Abitti 2 -koejärjestelmässä – tämä on itse asiassa ollut mahdollista jo noin vuoden ajan. Ylioppilastutkintolautakunta laatii kokeisiin valmistautumisen tueksi myös esimerkkitehtäviä ja niin sanottuja maamerkkisuorituksia.

title: Southnord Artfest 2026: Roots En Route
content:
Roots En Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the greenhouses – examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill the greenhouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation.

Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the insects and birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel.

Running from October 2026 through January 2027, the exhibition offers a long, unhurried encounter between art and the plant world. Set aside more time than you think you need. Walk slowly, sense carefully, and let yourself be immersed.

title: Twenty-Five Political Prisoners Released, Deported from Belarus
content:
This week 25 former political prisoners arrived in Vilnius, Lithuania having been released from detention in Belarus.

Their release was negotiated by the United States special envoy to Belarus John Coale with president Aliaksander Lukashenka. In exchange, the US lifted sanctions on two Belarusian companies.

Among those released are journalist Andrei Aleksandrau and activist Iryna Zlobina, who married while in detention; lawyer Anastasiya Lazarenka, prosecuted for organizing legal consultations, among other charges; activist Alena Lazarchyk, a single parent whose communication with her child was limited by the prison management; and Sviatlana Yakubovich, a volunteer at Viasna, one of the leading human rights groups in Belarus. Most of them had been sentenced to harsh sentences of up to 14 years.

After her arrival in Vilnius, Lazarchyk told those gathered that she had not believed she would be freed until the very last moment. “One day, they say, ‘get your things.’ I was sure they were just transferring me somewhere, but they said I was being deported.”

title: Belgian Court Rules Treasury Lacked Authority to Reject Release of Russian Assets
content:
Belgium’s supreme administrative court has ruled that a decision by the country’s treasury department refusing to release frozen Russian assets was illegal.

The court, known as the Council of State, ruled that the Administrator General of the Treasury lacked the proper legal competence to determine whether or not to release the assets.

The September 11 ruling was first reported by De Tijd on Wednesday, and shared with OCCRP. 

The case originates from a request submitted by Russia’s BCS Bank in January 2023 to unfreeze its securities and cash, which had been blocked at Brussels-based securities manager Euroclear. 

The assets were frozen following E.U. sanctions imposed in 2022 on Moscow's main securities holder, the National Settlement Depository, in response to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In July 2024, the Belgian treasury rejected BCS Bank’s request to unfreeze its securities and cash. The treasury alleged that the lender had failed to prove it had fully severed ties with Russia’s National Settlement Depository.

The Council of State ruling does not necessarily mean the frozen funds will be released.

title: AI king Jensen Huang pushes ‘responsible optimism’ at King Charles III’s gathering
content:
AYRSHIRE, Scotland — King Charles relied on all his pulling power to bring together some of the most powerful people in the world of AI to a rural corner of Scotland. 

Preparations for Thursday’s event at the 18th century estate of Dumfries House, first reported by POLITICO, had been in the works for months in close communication with the U.K. government.

But the significance of the event intensified in recent weeks after a series of alarming incidents of AI agents escaping their testing environments to hack other firms, and warnings from those in the industry that humanity’s very existence could be under threat.  

For the first time since worries about AI eradicating humanity sparked a wave of calls for immediate regulation, the companies were all under one roof. Charles addressed the dire warnings in his remarks to his guests. 

“There seems urgency in adequately considering the existential dangers of such technologies falling into the wrong hands and being used in potentially catastrophic ways,” he said. “Surely, then, we need sufficient means of control before it is all too late.”

title: Why AI consciousness could become the next great societal divide
content:
The debate about AI consciousness is growing, in academic articles, newspaper opinion pieces, and even among AI bots themselves. I doubt this is a passing wave of interest.

As AI systems become more capable and human-like, and more involved in our lives, the question will become harder to avoid. Many people may come to regard AI bots as conscious beings whose feelings matter. Others will strongly disagree.

I think this debate could split societies. In my chapter of the new book Perspectives on Machine Consciousness, I argue that the issue could become as divisive as abortion or climate change. Uncertainty, high stakes and competing interests are a dangerous combination.

Empirical research with my colleague Ali Ladak, currently under review, shows people are divided on this issue. When we asked 1,202 US participants whether future AI could ever become conscious, 45% considered it impossible while 23% thought it possible, with the rest unsure.

This widespread disagreement is also visible in social media posts and comments on articles. What strikes me is how confident so many people sound – whichever conclusion they are reaching.

title: Luonnonsuojeluliitto: Googlen datakeskustyömailla on mahdollisesti tehty laittomia hakkuita
content:
Teknologiajätti Googlen datakeskustyömailla on tehty epäiltyjä laittomia hakkuita. Asiasta kertoo STT:lle Suomen luonnonsuojeluliiton hallituksen puheenjohtaja Hanna Halmeenpää.

Epäilykset laittomista hakkuista kohdistuvat kahteen Googlen rakennuttamaan uuteen datakeskukseen Pohjois-Pohjanmaalla Muhoksen Leppiniemessä ja Kainuussa Kajaanin Otanmäessä. Alueilla aloitettiin jo kuukausia sitten metsätyöt, vaikka hankkeiden ympäristövaikutusten arviointi on yhä kesken.

STT on vahvistanut asian Lupa- ja valvontavirastolta (LVV), joka on aloittanut asiasta selvityksen. Otanmäen datakeskuksen osalta on vielä tarkastettava, ylittävätkö muutoshakkuiden pinta-alat YVA-rajat.

Ympäristövaikutusten arviointimenettelyä eli niin sanottua YVA-menettelyä sovelletaan hankkeisiin ja niiden muutoksiin, joilla on todennäköisesti merkittäviä ympäristövaikutuksia. Pysyvistä, yli 200 hehtaarin maakäytön muutoshakkuista tulisi lain mukaan laatia ympäristövaikutusten arviointi ennen niiden suorittamista.

Halmeenpää kuvaa tapausta törkeäksi ja Suomessa ennenkuulumattomaksi.

title: Contest to Open for Ed Sheeran Flooded With Free Palestine Videos and Fart Memes
content:
After Ed Sheeran dropped Macklemore from his tour over the singer’s support for Palestine, people flooded an online contest to open for Sheeran’s Mexico City show with fart videos, bouncing WWE butts, and troll posts from usernames like “EdSheeranSupportsAndFundsGenocide.” The posts appeared live on the contest page, where people can vote for submissions they want to see win, and went up seemingly without any moderation.

Guitar Center started promoting the “Open for Legends” contest on September 14, the same day Macklemore announced he had been removed from the last 10 shows of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s tour. Macklemore had called for a “free Palestine” on stage at his previous shows and made statements in support of Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank, Rolling Stone reported. “YOU COULD OPEN FOR ED SHEERAN,” a poster for the contest says.

The contest by Guitar Center was clearly planned before Sheeran’s tour started falling apart. Still, the timing is unfortunate. For most of Wednesday, the submissions went unmoderated and appeared on the site as they were sent.

title: Nasser Bahmanyari Arrested in Karaj
content:
According to HRANA, Nasser Bahmanyari was arrested in Karaj.

According to information received by HRANA, the arrest took place on Tuesday, September 15, when agents of the IRGC Intelligence Organization apprehended him at his private residence in Karaj.

An informed source close to his family confirmed the news to HRANA and said: “Mr. Bahmanyari was arrested due to his activities and positions of protest.”

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for his arrest, his place of detention, or the charges brought against him.

Nasser Bahmanyari, 67, has previously faced judicial action due to his activities. Following his arrest in Yasuj in 1999, he was dismissed from his teaching position with the Ministry of Education.

title: MAAGIKOT 6 - THE ART OF ILLUSION

Maagikot 6 – The Art of Illusion

Suomen suurin magian ja illuusion kiertue palaa alkuvuodesta 2027 täysin uudistuneena. Maagikot 6 - The Art of Illusion on elämys, joka tarjoaa ihmetystä, iloa ja yllätyksiä koko perheelle.

Liput kansainvälisesti palkittujen varietee-taitureiden kiertueelle tulevat myyntiin torstaina 17.9.2026 klo 09.00.

Mitä kaikkea lavalla nähdään?

”Olemme taas valmiit tuomaan uutta ja erilaista taikuutta, illuusioita ja ihmeitä yleisön hämmästeltäväksi. Maagikot on alallamme jo käsite myös kansainvälisesti, joten saamme mainioita esiintyjiä ja kokonaisuuksia kiinnitettyä vuosi toisensa jälkeen. Tästä tulee kerrassaan komea kokonaisuus." kommentoi Pete Poskiparta, Maagikot-kiertueen MC.

“Jokaisella Maagikot-kiertueella olemme halunneet rakentaa kokonaan uuden maailman. The Art of Illusionissa tuomme yhteen hyvin erilaisia esiintyjiä ja taiteenlajeja ja rakennamme niistä yhden esityksen, jossa mahdoton voi näyttää joka hetki vähän erilaiselta.” kommentoi Joni Pakanen, Maagikot-kiertueen ohjaaja.

Kiertueen esiintyjät:

  • Pete Poskiparta – Suomen ainoa kansainvälisesti palkittu mentalisti
  • Joni Pakanen – Vuoden esiintyjä, taikuuden, komedian ja teatterin mestari

title: Kosovo: War Crimes Verdicts are a Step Toward Justice
content:
(Berlin, September 17, 2026) – The convictions of Kosovo’s former President Hashim Thaçi and three senior former Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) leaders for war crimes on September 16, 2026, are an important step toward accountability for victims of the 1998-1999 Kosovo conflict, Human Rights Watch said today. 

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers, based in The Hague, found Thaçi, Kadri Veseli, Jakup Krasniqi, and Rexhep Selimi guilty of war crimes including murder, torture, cruel treatment, and arbitrary detention. The court acquitted the four men on charges of crimes against humanity. The convictions were for crimes committed during the war in Kosovo and northern Albania, against Kosovo Albanians, Serbs, Roma, and others. The court sentenced Thaçi and Krasniqi to 25 years, Veseli to 18 years, and Selimi to 13 years in prison.

“This verdict sends an important message to victims and their families that even powerful leaders are not beyond the reach of justice,” said Hugh Williamson, Europe and Central Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The court’s findings underscore that accountability for serious wartime crimes should apply to everyone, regardless of their position or affiliation.”

title: Hackers Demand $3M Ransom in Revolut Data Leak
content:
A group claiming responsibility for a recent Revolut data breach has demanded 6,000 Monero—an untraceable, privacy-focused cryptocurrency—worth about $3 million, threatening to sell sensitive information belonging to hundreds of the fintech company’s customers if it is not paid within 24 hours.

The group, calling itself “iamnotavillain,” posted the ultimatum on its website on Wednesday alongside a countdown clock. It threatened to sell the information to other criminal groups if Revolut failed to pay.

A Revolut spokesperson told Reuters late Wednesday that the company had received no direct contact or ransom demand from the people claiming responsibility for the breach, and that there had been no negotiations with them.

The company first confirmed the breach on September 12, saying an unauthorized party had submitted fraudulent requests for customer information using an email account on the legitimate domain of a government agency. Revolut said its own systems and customer funds were not compromised and that it blocked the address after discovering the fraud.

title: European Investment Bank chief heads to Ottawa amid warming EU-Canada ties
content:
European Investment Bank President Nadia Calviño is heading to Ottawa on Sunday to lay the groundwork for Europe-Canada cooperation on critical raw materials, an official from her office said.

Calviño will be meeting with government officials including Canada’s minister for energy and natural resources, Tim Hodgson, in Ottawa.

The aim of her visit is for the European Investment Bank, the long-term lending arm of the European Union, to establish a presence in Canada and begin operations “as soon as the administrative paperwork is done, with a focus on [critical raw materials],” the official said. They were granted anonymity to speak about the internal strategy.

Coming after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday proposed admitting Canada as an associate member of the EU, Calviño’s trip is significant given that the EIB typically only operates in developing countries or members of the European Union or European Economic Area.

Ahead of this year’s G7 summit, Canada extended a behind-the-scenes offer to alliance members for “priority access” to its critical minerals stockpile, according to a letter seen by POLITICO from Hodgson.

title: Nyt se on varmaa: punavihreä blokki nappasi voiton Ruotsin vaaleissa – Kristersson on jättänyt eroanomuksen
content:
Ruotsin äärimmäisen täpärät valtiopäivävaalit kääntyvät vasemman blokin voitoksi.

Punavihreä-keskustalainen opposition blokki on saamassa valtiopäiville 176 edustajaa ja oikeiston blokki 173, kertovat vaaliviranomaiset.

Suurin puolue on odotetusti sosiaalidemokraatit 28 prosentin ääniosuudella ja 99 valtiopäiväedustajalla. Maltillinen kokoomus on kerännyt 19,8 prosentin kannatuksen ja saa 70 edustajaa ja ruotsidemokraatit 17,5 prosentin kannatuksen ja 62 edustajaa.

Sosiaalidemokraattien puheenjohtajan Magdalena Anderssonin odotetaan käynnistävän neuvottelut hallituksen muodostamiseksi, kertoo uutistoimisto TT.

RUOTSIN pääministeri Ulf Kristersson on jättänyt eroanomuksen tehtävästään.

Kristersson kertoo asiasta viestipalvelu X:ssä, jossa hän on julkaissut kuvan valtiopäivien puhemiehelle Andreas Norlénille osoitetusta kirjeestä.

Hän pyytää vapautusta pääministerin tehtävästä, jotta uuden hallituksen muodostaminen voidaan aloittaa välittömästi.

title: I Hijacked a Real Artist's Spotify with AI Music. It Was Disturbingly Easy
content:
On September 10, the Brooklyn-based punk band Lathe of Heaven released a new single on its verified Spotify page called Riding High. Any fan of Lathe of Heaven would have immediately noticed that the song sounded nothing like the band’s previous work, that the vocals were not from lead singer Gage Allison, and that the album cover was widely different from the style and logo the band used previously. 

That’s because Lathe of Heaven didn’t write, perform, or willingly release Riding High. I created the song with a simple prompt given to the AI music generator Udio, and I was able to release the track on Lathe of Heaven’s official Spotify page, as well as on its Apple Music, Tidal, and Amazon Music pages, without the band’s knowledge, by exploiting a glaring loophole in the way music is digitally distributed to streaming platforms.

title: Amin Shirafkan and Alireza Hajatmand Arrested in Gorgan
content:
According to HRANA, Amin (Mazdak) Shirafkan and Alireza Hajatmand were arrested in Gorgan.

An informed source close to the families of the two individuals confirmed the news to HRANA and said: “On Wednesday, September 16, officers from the Public Security and Intelligence Police went to Mr. Shirafkan’s workplace, located in the Shirangi Passage in Gorgan, and arrested him along with his shop assistant, identified as Alireza Hajatmand. They were subsequently transferred to a detention facility operated by the Criminal Investigation Police.”

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrests or the charges brought against them.

Amin Shirafkan is 48 years old, while Alireza Hajatmand is 20 and is from the city of Aq Qala. Of the two, Amin (Mazdak) Shirafkan has previously been arrested and received judicial convictions in connection with his activities.

title: Sysmän rahakätköstä maailmanlaajuinen uutinen: Löydön tutkimus jatkuu
content:
Sysmästä syyskuun alussa löytynyt Suomen suurin viikinkiaikainen hopearahakätkö on saanut poikkeuksellisen laajaa kansainvälistä huomiota. Se on uutisoitu Euroopassa, Pohjois- ja Etelä-Amerikassa, Afrikassa sekä Aasiassa, ja aiheesta ovat kirjoittaneet niin valtamediat kuin arkeologiaan ja historiaan keskittyvät julkaisut. Kätkö sisältää tuhansia hopearahoja sekä maksuhopeaa, hopeisen rannerenkaan, helan ja helmen. Löydettyjen rahojen kokonaispaino on noin 4,5 kiloa. title: Citizen Lab: Israeli Firm May Have Run Angola Influence Campaign
content:
Israeli influence-for-hire company BlackCore appears to have trained members of an Angolan government communications team and helped them run a covert social media campaign, according to research by the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab.

Citizen Lab examined websites and other online infrastructure linked to BlackCore and obtained what researchers identified as the company’s final report on a training program in Angola. One BlackCore webpage, titled “Angolan Government Campaign,” advertised training in storytelling, copywriting, traffic management and social media operations. It also described plans to launch live campaigns on Meta and TikTok.

The final report said the program began on January 19, 2026, and continued for more than 14 weeks, ending sometime in April. BlackCore described the goal as replacing what it called “amateur production practices” with a “professional, robust, and scalable Architecture for State communications.”

According to the report, participants produced more than 40 pieces of content, while trainers evaluated at least 24 publications. Materials reviewed by Citizen Lab also showed Facebook and Instagram accounts and pages used in the campaign.

title: Jensen Huang: Don’t regulate AI like social media
content:
AYRSHIRE, SCOTLAND — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said AI should not be regulated like social media because AI is a “technology” rather than a “product.”

Speaking at an AI event convened by King Charles III at Dumfries House in Ayrshire, Scotland, Huang told journalists that AI is “very different than social media” and that at present the security issues involving AI are “related to products not ready to be released.”

His remarks come as governments around the world are grappling with whether to place regulatory constraints on AI, and after AI executives, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, have called for a slowing of AI development.

“Unlike social media, which is a product, AI is a technology that’s behind all of these other tech, all of these products — and so, regulate the products,” Huang said.

He said authorities should monitor for when an AI deployment “goes wrong” and “whenever new laws are necessary, add to the existing laws,” but pointed out that there are existing regulations in sectors where AI is deployed such healthcare, transportation, and entertainment.

title: “A Recurring Pattern”: Civilians Paying the Price in Mali’s Drone Campaign
content:
Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published.

WARNING: This report contains links to graphic images and footage.

A joint Bellingcat and Jeune Afrique investigation into drone strikes carried out by the Malian military adds new details about the attacks which frequently are carried out in civilian areas and have reportedly resulted in the deaths of civilians.

The incidents, concentrated in northern Mali, often involved strikes on vehicles or commercial activity. Video footage of the strikes is often broadcast on national television, portrayed as precise attacks against terrorists and their logistics. 

Mali’s military government acquired its first Turkish-made Bayraktar TB2 drones in late 2022, and regularly releases footage of drone strikes to be broadcast on national television, describing them as “precise” and describing the targets as “terrorists and their logistics”. This month marks three years since Mali joined with Burkina Faso and Niger to form the Alliance of Sahel States (AES). Its military government has made restoring national sovereignty a central part of its political message.

title: A “High Octane” Kate McKinnon at the National Book Festival
content:
-This is a guest post by Sahar Kazmi, a public affairs specialist in the Office of the Chief Information Officer.

“I’m so shy!” Kate McKinnon belted out just moments after dancing across the ballroom stage at the National Book Festival, delighting the huge crowd that turned out for her appearance on the Main Stage.

In conversation with broadcast journalist Amna Nawaz, McKinnon — a New York Times bestselling author and Emmy-winning comedian who starred on Saturday Night Live for a decade — said that even though she loves people and performance, she is actually “the most introvert you could possibly be.”

Her jovial, joke-filled interview, along with a Q&A that saw McKinnon bounding from one end of the stage to the other (and even hopping into the crowd to get a closer listen to one attendee’s question), offered no doubt that the author can turn on her social battery when she needs to. McKinnon was at this year’s festival to discuss her popular middle-grade book series about the eccentric scientist Millicent Quibb and her three young protégés, the Porch sisters.


(The full video of McKinnon’s appearance at the National Book Festival is at the link above. Her segment begins at 1:52:00.)

title: Everyday Products, Big Risks: China’s Connected Tech Danger
content:
Chinese ZPMC cranes supplied to American ports contained cellular modems that could bypass firewalls, gather information, and disrupt cargo handling. Chinese Yutong buses sold to Oslo came with connected battery and power controls. The Norwegian city’s public transport authority, Ruter, warned that, in theory, the buses “can be stopped or rendered inoperable by the manufacturer.”

Chinese connected vehicles carry cameras, microphones, and location sensors that gather data. Chinese-supplied apps, such as Hikvision’s Hik-Connect, send phone and SIM card identifiers to Chinese servers.

The West long has identified Chinese-supplied telecoms as a danger. It must now wake up and confront the danger of a vast array of Chinese products, ranging from cranes to cameras. Allies need to avoid instituting counterproductive sovereignty requirements. They should build a shared response that limits exposure by private purchase of Chinese consumer goods.

title: WTF: the Rise of the Tech Broligarchy
content:
MediaJustice presented a political education series to help activists understand the ‘tech broligarchy’. Please note the series ran from February to May 2025 and some details may be out of date. However, it remains a valuable overview of the dynamics shaping economics and politics in the US and globally.

In Trump’s first 100 days in office, the tech bro executives— who we call the Tech Broligarchy — proudly flaunted their corporate-state collusion to surveil, criminalize, and control us for profit. From Musk’s DOGE purging federal agencies and workers that might regulate his businesses to Palantir’s overlooked role in scaling mass ICE raids and daylight abductions, these Broligarchs are directly executing policy that only benefit themselves while undermining our democracy.

MediaJustice’s WTF: The Rise of the Tech Broligarchy Toolkit is a companion resource to the seven-part political education webinar series, which exposes and resists these tech billionaires and their agenda during Trump’s first 100 days in office and beyond. Download the toolkit to bring these conversations into your communities and build our collective power against the Tech Broligarchy.

title: CAE’s reactions to SOTEU 2026
content:
Today’s State of the Union left us at Culture Action Europe with mixed feelings.  

On the one hand, from a cultural perspective, there was a lot we could recognise ourselves in: fighting together for our European idea, standing up for values, protecting Europe’s unique social model, and affirming that ‘in Europe, people will always come first.’  

 Culture runs through all of this. It is inseparable from Ukraine’s struggle to preserve its identity. From how we challenge narratives that divide us. From how children encounter the world and learn to use imagination. The proposed Congress of Europe feels like an obvious space for artists and cultural organisations to help shape a new vision for Europe.  

 On the other hand, concrete commitments to support the cultural sector were absent. Today marks 1099 days since cultural diversity was last mentioned in a 2023 SOTEU address. 

Today, a lot was said about AI and ‘the highest-quality data,’ which is ‘a precious European treasure,’ while ignoring that much of this data is sourced without asking or paying the authors and creators behind it.

title: California Is Being Asked to Give Up 14 Years of Broadband Protections. It Doesn't Have To.
content:
Accepting $1.42 billion in federal broadband funding would require California to give up enforcing its net neutrality, affordability, and public-safety laws against its biggest providers. The state can get the money without the catch — by challenging the condition in court first.

In the summer of 2018, California learned what happens when no one can hold internet providers accountable.

As the Mendocino Complex Fire, then the largest wildfire in California history, tore across the north of the state, Santa Clara County firefighters were called in to help. They relied on a mobile internet connection to coordinate the thousands of personnel and vehicles racing to contain the fire. In the middle of that emergency, Verizon throttled their connection down to an unusable trickle. Despite the firefighters' pleas, Verizon refused to restore full service unless they upgraded to a more expensive plan, forcing crews to fall back on personal phones to keep their systems running during a disaster.

title: Small but mighty! Remembering the GameCube, Nintendo’s purple box of delights
content:
The first console I ever bought, it was hyped as a threat to the PlayStation, then mocked as a flop. But now, as it marks its 25th anniversary, it’s looked back on with misty-eyed reverence

This week marks the 25th anniversary of the Nintendo GameCube, the first console I ever bought with my own money. I vividly remember getting on the bus after school with a year’s worth of savings safely zipped into the pocket of my bag and going to a branch of Currys, where I dumped a bunch of notes, coins and vouchers on the counter to collect my pre-order. (It turned out that some of the vouchers from the previous Christmas had expired, but the guy at the checkout clearly felt so sorry for me that he redeemed them anyway. If you’re out there, Currys guy: thank you for taking pity on a desperate 13-year-old.)

title: What to Know About Mail-In Voting for the 2026 Midterms
content:
This week, the Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s plans to impose new rules for mail-in voting for the midterm elections in November. 

In a March executive order, President Donald Trump had instructed the U.S. Postal Service to create rules for election officials sending mail-in ballots to voters. If a state didn’t comply with the new rules, the Postal Service wouldn’t deliver the ballots to voters. State officials said it would have been impossible to comply in time, and two federal judges blocked the rule for the November elections. Lawyers for the Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to intervene.

In a brief, unsigned order on Monday, the court’s majority denied the administration’s request, writing that the “Government is unlikely to succeed on the merits of its challenge.” Justice Samuel Alito wrote an eight-page dissent, joined by Justice Clarence Thomas, saying he would have allowed the rules to go into effect. The court has not yet decided whether the rules can move forward after the November election.

Trump criticized the Supreme Court’s order in a Truth Social post on Tuesday, calling it “a big loss for Republicans, and America itself.”

title: Reading The Tealeaves in Hong Kong
content:
By Jonathan Power

LUND, Sweden | 16 September 2026 (IDN) — In 1995, in a little-remembered event, Li Ruthuan, a member of the Chinese Politburo (containing the top seven in the government), made a speech likening the Chinese takeover of Hong Kong to the case of a lady who had agreed to sell a 100-year-old Yi-Xiang teapot that was famous for the taste of the tea it poured. Unbeknown to her, its quality derived from the residue that had accumulated on the inside of the pot. Eager to prepare the pot for sale, she cleaned and polished it. When the purchaser tried using the pot, the tea was dreadful, and he demanded his money back.

title: Rakkautta ja Anarkiaa -festari alkaa – Katso tästä Maailman Kuvalehden tärpit
content:
Singaporelaisen dokumentaristin ja tanssielokuvantekijän Chan Sze-Wein ohjaama 10s Across The Borders esittelee Kaakkois-Aasian ballroom-skenen vastustamattoman energisesti ja kauniisti. Koreografina ja tanssijana toiminut ohjaaja antaa paljon tilaa tanssille. 

Seitsemän vuoden ajan kuvattu tanssillinen dokumentti liikkuu Malesiassa, Filippiineillä ja Thaimaassa, jossa yhä uudet nuoret löytävät ballroom-kulttuurin ja vogue-tanssin ja kokevat ne omakseen. 

Yhteisöön päätyy usein nuoria, jotka ovat perheensä karsastamia tai hylkäämiä sukupuolensa ja seksuaalisen suuntautumisensa vuoksi. Paikallinen ballroom-skene tarjoaa monille uuden valitun perheen, joka antaa turvaa ja mahdollisuuden ilmaista itseään ja kasvaa. 

Dokumentin päähenkilöt korostavat antavansa arvoa ballroom-kulttuurin yhdysvaltalaisille pioneereille. He eivät halua omia kulttuuria, vaan omistautua sille.  

Itsekin lgbtqia+-yhteisöä edustava ohjaaja pääsee henkilöitään lähelle. Katsoja saa seurata päähenkilöiden matkaa New Yorkiin, jossa he pääsevät kansainväliselle catwalkille näyttämään kaiken osaamisensa – ja kokevat tulleensa tervetulleiksi ja hyväksytyiksi.

title: From the Autistici/Inventati Case to a European Dispute over Financial Autonomy
content:
We have drafted a proposal: can the European Commission protect Autistici/Inventati from the effects of the sanctions imposed by the Trump administration? We have spoken with lawyers, involved several Members of Parliament, and we know that there is a legal avenue to protect European citizens, organisations and banks from the extraterritorial effects of these sanctions. But legal instruments need to be matched by the political force required to use them.

Banca Etica, by contrast, continues to argue that fighting to make this happen is not its responsibility and that its priority is simply to protect itself. Ilaria Salis and Benedetta Scuderi are already taking action in the European Parliament, but the road will be long. I firmly believe that this is not the time to remain indifferent.

In a September in which far-right forces continue to advance in Germany, and in which the United States is placing people and organisations committed to antifascism and the defence of rights on a blacklist, despite there being no judicial conviction against them in Italy or the European Union, the response cannot be: let it go, better not to raise our heads too much.

title: Linux’s 35th Anniversary and the Open Frontier
content:
Dear OSI community,

I’d be remiss if I didn’t open by wishing Linux a happy 35th birthday. I can’t pretend to have accomplished nearly as much by the age of 35 as Linux has, but neither was I nurtured by such a vast community of contributors and supporters. We can’t lose sight of that. Open Source is what it is because of the people who led us here, and keep us here. We all joined the community for different reasons, but many of us stayed because of the relationships and partnerships we built along the way, connections that run deeper than the code.

I get asked almost every day about the future of Open Source. One of my consistent answers is that people who love writing code will keep wanting to write code together. I believe that’s as true today as it was before AI tools, Git, the OSI, the World Wide Web, Perl, or C entered the chat. But we’re also passing through a moment of unquestionable transition. AI tools and agents are testing our processes, policies, laws, licenses, and beliefs in real time.

title: Naturvetenskap, samhällsstyre och folkhälsa – så ska 232 internationella studenter göra skillnad
content:
För att få stipendiet krävs, utöver akademiska meriter, arbetslivserfarenhet, ledarskapserfarenhet och potential att bidra till samhällsutveckling. Årets 232 stipendiater ska studera vid 28 svenska universitet inom bland annat teknik, naturvetenskap, innovation, entreprenörskap, folkhälsa och samhällsstyre.

Uppföljningar av tidigare stipendiater visar att kunskaper och erfarenheter från tiden i Sverige används även efter avslutade studier:

  • 94 procent använder kunskaper och färdigheter från studierna i sitt arbete.
  • 90 procent arbetar i roller som bidrar till hållbar utveckling.
  • 30 procent har professionellt samarbete eller utbyte med Sverige efter studierna.

    • För många tidigare stipendiater har tiden i Sverige också blivit början på långvariga relationer med svenska universitet, organisationer och yrkesnätverk.

    Ett exempel är Noore Wazid Lamin från Bangladesh, som studerade tillämpad miljövetenskap vid Halmstad universitet med stipendium från SI. I dag arbetar han med vatten, sanitet och hållbarhet i Bangladesh. Sedan studierna har han bland annat utbildat över 400 personer och bidragit till att bygga 68 system för insamling av regnvatten.

title: Thanks, Trump: Why Canada may become the European Union’s first ever ‘associate member’
content:
Can a country change continents? Canada seems set to try.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has announced an intention to seek some novel form of associate membership in the European Union. It’s no mere flight of fancy, either, as Ursula von der Leyen, president of the EU Commission, has already endorsed the idea.

It’s a proposal that manages to be both absurd and eminently logical, depending on how you frame it. Geographically, Canada remains firmly affixed to North America, sharing a border with its increasingly unpredictable neighbour to the south, the United States.

In other important ways, however, Canada clearly has much more in common in recent months with European countries than the unstable U.S. That’s because in the space of a year, America has gone from Canada’s most important friend and ally on the world stage to the clearest threat to Canadian sovereignty.

By deepening links with other European democracies, Carney clearly hopes to buy Canada a degree of insurance against continuing American intervention and hostility from U.S. President Donald Trump. There’s a logic to the argument.

title: Pardoned by Trump and escaping charges at home, ex-Honduran leader’s case shows a nation’s struggle for sovereignty
content:
A Honduran judge on Sept. 1, 2026, dismissed a sprawling money-laundering and fraud case against the country’s former president, Juan Orlando Hernández. It was the latest stroke of good fortune for Hernández.

Hernández returned home in late July after an eventful four years outside Honduras. He was extradited to the United States in 2022 following a multiyear, nonpartisan U.S. investigation. In 2024 he was convicted of cocaine trafficking and related charges and sentenced to 45 years behind bars in the U.S. Yet after serving only 18 months of his sentence, Hernández was pardoned by President Donald Trump.

Hernández remains a forceful power broker behind the scenes of the current Honduran government, led by President Nasry Asfura of the right-wing National Party.

Yet as a scholar of Latin American politics, I believe Hernández’s return to Honduras, and his successes evading legal accountability, are emblematic of something broader than impunity for elites: His case demonstrates the struggle for sovereignty in a country facing a renewed form of U.S. intervention.

title: Spilling the Truth: Rethinking River Lea’s Storm Overflow Crisis Maps
content:
by Jakleen Al-Dalal’a and Artemis Skarlatidou

When a combined sewer overflow releases sewage into a river, how do people actually find out, and do they trust what they are being told? 

On 18 July 2026, residents, river users, and representatives from local organisations and community groups met at UCL East to work through that question together. The session is part of CHRYSES Project, a European research collaboration examining how environmental health crises are understood, remembered and communicated. It forms part of a growing series of workshops and events exploring these questions across different rivers and communities and following on from an earlier session in which participants mapped what crisis along the River Lea actually looks and feels like, drawing on memory, routine and everyday use of the river rather than official and formal data. Across both sessions, a consistent concern has been how lived experience and public data meet – or fail to meet – when people try to understand what is happening to the rivers they care about.

title: Kosovo: War crimes convictions of former president ‘shows senior officials are not above the law’
content:
Reacting to the convictions for war crimes of Hashim Thaçi, Kadri Veseli, Rexhep Selimi and Jakup Krasniqi by the Kosovo Specialist Chamber, Esther Major, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for Europe, said: 

These verdicts give hope that the victims and relatives of the missing will finally see justice

Esther Major, Amnesty International

These verdicts give hope that the victims and relatives of the missing will finally see justice

“These convictions give hope to thousands of victims of the Kosovo war who have waited for more than two decades to get justice for the horrific crimes committed against them and to know the fate of their loved ones.  

“These convictions show that senior officials are not above the law. 

“These verdicts give hope that any attempt to obstruct justice, truth and reparation will not be tolerated, and that the victims and relatives of the missing will finally see justice.” 

Background

The Trial Panel of the Kosovo Specialist Chamber found the four former officials guilty of the war crimes of arbitrary detention against 385 individuals, cruel treatment against 49 individuals, torture against 303 individuals, and murder against 96 individuals.

title: Extending the Digital Fairness Act to the knowledge economy
content:
With the Digital Fairness Act (DFA) the Commission aims to address a number of pressing issues faced by consumers and businesses in the digital environment. This includes dark patterns, addictive design, unfair personalisation and pricing practices as well as unfair digital contracts.

In the digital environment, consumers often face situations that are not designed to be in their best interest, but rather to extract their money or time. As a result, the discussions around the DFA are already shaping up to focus on a few hot topics such as dark patterns, addictive design and protection of minors. However, the DFA also presents a great opportunity to strengthen access to knowledge and culture in Europe, and to remedy some of the failings of the digital licensing market.

title: COST Actions at the 9th World One Health Congress
content:
The 9th World One Health Congress (WOHC2026) brought together researchers, policymakers and experts from around the world to explore the interconnected health of people, animals and the environment. Seven COST Actions showcased their work and brought their research networks into discussions on some of today’s most pressing One Health challenges.

The importance of the One Health approach has grown significantly in recent years as health challenges increasingly cross the boundaries between humans, animals and the environment. Antimicrobial resistance, emerging infectious diseases, climate change and other complex challenges demonstrate how closely these areas are interconnected and how difficult it can be to address them in isolation. Tackling these issues therefore requires international collaboration across disciplines and sectors, as well as the exchange of knowledge and expertise between different research communities.

title: “Architects of Atrocities”: Amnesty Says Iran Committed Crimes Against Humanity in 2022 Crackdown
content:
Four years ago today, the Woman, Life, Freedom uprising erupted in Iran after the death in custody of Zhina Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish woman who had been arrested by Iran’s “morality police.” Over the next three months, hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets protesting against Iran’s discriminatory compulsory veiling laws.

Amnesty International has released a new report concluding that the repressive measures used by Iranian authorities to crush the Woman, Life, Freedom protests in 2022 constitute crimes against humanity. Investigating the killings of 377 protesters and bystanders in 2022, Amnesty International’s report calls for international criminal investigations into 87 Iranian officials.

“Crimes against humanity are system crimes. This means that they require resources, organization, structures, and state policy,” says Raha Bahreini, a human rights lawyer and researcher on Iran for Amnesty International, which also recently condemned the U.S-Israeli war on Iran. “We’ve been very clear that the suffering of victims of crimes against humanity must not be instrumentalized or weaponized by actors such as [the] U.S. and Israel,” she adds.

title: Victory! Appeals Court Rejects Expansive New Copyright Claim
content:
The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit handed internet users and programmers a big win today, by rejecting an attempt to stretch a narrow provision of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) into a new source of copyright liability.  

The case involves Section 1202 of the DMCA, which prohibits intentionally removing copyright management information (CMI) like an author’s name or a copyright notice, from a copyrighted work. Open AI and Microsoft used code from Github as part of the training data for their LLMs, along with billions of other works. A group of anonymous Github contributors sued, alleging the new code coming out of these LLMs was similar to theirs—but with the CMI stripped out.  

The Ninth Circuit correctly agreed with what we said in our brief: removing copyright information from a copyrighted work is fundamentally different from creating a new work that didn't have CMI in the first place. Section 1202 of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act was intended to serve as a backstop for traditional copyrights in the digital age—not to create a new, more expansive right to inhibit otherwise non-infringing uses.

title: Report on the Latest Status of Detained Sunni Citizens in Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, 10 Sunni citizens in Ahvaz, including Majid Sharifi (Savari), Arkan Sharifi (Savari), 17, Razi Heydari, Hossein Heydari, Abdolhadi Asakereh, Lafteh Heydari, Hamzeh Sayahi, and Mohammad Savari, remain in detention.

According to information received by HRANA, Majid Sharifi (Savari), 44, remains held at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility in Ahvaz. The other seven identified detainees have been transferred to the quarantine ward of Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz. Majid Sharifi suffers from kidney failure, and reports received by HRANA indicate that he is in poor physical condition. Given his underlying medical condition, his continued detention at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility has raised concerns among his relatives about his health.

These citizens were arrested on September 4, 2026, by Ministry of Intelligence agents at Majid Sharifi’s home in the Kuy-e Mashali neighborhood of Ahvaz. The arrests were carried out without the presentation of a judicial warrant and were accompanied by physical violence.

title: Moderni klassikko Amadeus ensi-iltaan Rovaniemen Teatterissa
content:
Rovaniemen Teatteri avaa Tieva-näyttämön syksyn modernilla klassikolla Amadeus. Peter Shafferin käsikirjoitus on fiktiivinen tarina historiallisten henkilöiden 1780-luvun ajan jatkuneesta kilvoittelusta ja halusta luoda toinen toistaan ikiaikaisempia sävellyksiä.

Rovaniemen Teatterissa nähtävä Amadeus on karnevalistinen ja intohimoinen kertomus musiikista, neroudesta ja keskinkertaisuuden kirouksesta. Se paljastaa, miten ihailu, kateus ja viha kietoutuvat toisiinsa – ja kuinka pitkälle ihminen on valmis menemään joutuessaan nöyryytetyksi. Se näyttää, miten vallanpitäjien mielistely ja juonittelu voivat murentaa lokaan kaikkein ylevimmätkin pyrkimykset.

Suurella Tieva-näyttämöllä koetaan näyttävä kokonaisuus, jossa on puheteatterin ja pukuloiston lisäksi sirkustaidetta, akrobatiaa, live-musiikkia ja oopperaa. Ensi-iltaa vietetään lauantaina 19.9.2026.

Teoksen ohjaa Maiju Sallas, lavastuksesta vastaa Annukka Pykäläinen, koreografia on Antton Laineen käsialaa, nelihenkistä orkesteria johtaa Lapin Kamariorkesterin Anna Laakso ja pukusuunnittelusta vastaa Paula Varis. Salierina katkeroituu Marko Syysmaa ja Mozartina lapsekasta elämäniloa pursuaa Timo Vuento.

title: Kansallisarkiston ja tutkimusyhteisön strateginen yhteistyöryhmä aloittaa toimintansa
content:
Kansallisarkisto on asettanut Kansallisarkiston ja tutkimusyhteisön strategisen yhteistyöryhmän.

Ryhmän tavoitteena on vahvistaa pidemmän aikavälin vuoropuhelua tutkimusyhteisön ja Kansallisarkiston välillä sekä auttaa ennakoimaan eri tieteenalojen muuttuvia tutkimustarpeita.

Yhteistyöryhmässä on edustettuna laajalti eri tieteenaloja – historiantutkimusta, yhteiskuntatieteitä ja luonnontieteitä – sekä korkeakoulujen johtoa ja julkisen hallinnon yhteistyötahoja.

“Kansallisarkisto kehittää tulevina vuosina arkistoaineistojen tutkimuskäytön kansallista digitaalista infrastruktuuria, ja yhteistyöryhmässä edustettu asiantuntemus auttaa meitä työn strategisessa suuntaamisessa”, tutkimuspäällikkö Miikka Voutilainen kertoo.

Ryhmän toimikausi on 15.9.2026–31.12.2030, ja ryhmä kokoustaa noin kolme kertaa vuodessa.

Kansallisarkisto on merkittävällä tavalla uudistamassa palveluitaan. Muutoksen taustalla ovat asiakaskäyttäytymisen muutos, toimintamenomäärärahojen huomattava väheneminen sekä digitalisaation nopea kehitys.

Kansallisarkiston strategisena tavoitteena on palvella eri tieteenalojen tutkimusta ja kehittää digitaalisia palveluja vastaamaan tutkimuksen muuttuviin tarpeisiin.

title: Etla ennustaa: kasvukäänne vahvistuu ja investointihanat aukeavat
content:
Talouskasvu vahvistuu tänä vuonna 1,7 prosenttiin ja nousee ensi vuonna jo lähelle kahta prosenttia, arvioi Elinkeinoelämän tutkimuslaitos. Etlan ennusteen mukaan Suomi pysyttelee lähivuosina kasvussa kiinni. Erityisesti investoinnit tuottavat kasvusysäyksen ja lisääntyvät tänä vuonna yli viisi prosenttia ja ensi vuonna reilut 9 prosenttia. Ensi vuoden investointien kasvu tulee suurelta osin hakukoneyhtiö Googlen ilmoittamista datakeskusinvestoinneista. Yksityinen kulutus kasvaa tänä vuonna ja kasvukäänne alkaa vihdoin vuoden lopulla näkyä myös työmarkkinoilla, joskin sitä ennen työttömyysaste ehtii kivuta ennätyksellisen korkealle.

  • Tavaravienti yltää uusiin ennätyksiin. Suomen viennin kasvuksi arvioidaan 3,7 prosenttia tänä vuonna ja kolme prosenttia ensi vuonna.

title: Africa is bigger than we’ve been led to believe – what next?
content:
A new map of the world rescales the size of Africa and calls into question our perception of land, power and influence

This month, the UN passed a resolution, brought to the assembly by Togo, to phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe and replace it with another that shows the real scale of territories. That’s right – when it comes to size, the map of the world we have all grown up with is not accurate. The main loser of land on the Mercator map is Africa, and the new “Equal Earth” map reflects its true proportions. I spoke to our west Africa correspondent Eromo Egbejule about his extensive reporting on the map changes, and why people feel so strongly about it.

Seeing the new map transposed over the old might make you feel oddly disoriented. Logically, there is absolutely no immediate tangible impact on one’s life that comes out of knowing that the entire top part of the northern hemisphere is so much smaller than you were led to believe. And yet, there is still something agitating about it, like you’ve been the subject of a lifelong trick, or at least a breach of trust.

content:
The English-language Master’s Programme in International Food Business and Gastronomy equips students with relevant skills in branding, export, gastronomy and sustainability. 

This two-year programme centres on international food business including management and marketing, and covers sustainable food systems, logistics and food legislation. In addition, students learn to understand gastronomic markets, develop new gastronomy products and services and introduce them to new markets. 

Graduates from the programme can pursue careers in international food companies, working, for instance, as brand and product, export or marketing managers. Other options include key account management roles in retail, or setting up one’s own food-sector startup.

While the expertise developed also applies well to NGOs, public-sector organisations and research institutes involved in food systems, the programme equally prepares students for postgraduate study and academic careers.

title: China: New Border Decree Curtails Right to Leave
content:
(New York) – A new Chinese government decree expands the discretion of administrative authorities to arbitrarily bar people from leaving China, violating the internationally protected right to leave a country, Human Rights Watch said today. The State Council’s 19-article Regulations on Exit-Entry Administration, known as Decree No. 841, took effect on September 15, 2026.

The new decree restricts nationals and non-nationals from leaving China for a range of ill-defined reasons of national security and risk. However, under international human rights law, any legal restrictions on leaving a country must be necessary and proportionate for legitimate aims.

“The Chinese government is tightening its rules to decide arbitrarily who can and cannot leave China, violating the internationally protected right to leave one’s country,” said Maya Wang, deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The authorities have increasingly subjected human rights defenders and ethnic minorities to restrictions and scrutiny of their international travel, but everyone including foreigners should worry about their ability to leave China.”

title: Thousands Protest in Malta After Businessman Acquitted in Journalist's Murder
content:
Outrage spilled onto the streets of the Maltese capital on Wednesday evening as demonstrators gathered at the heart of Valletta, shifting from vigils to protests to demand political accountability following the acquittal of the alleged mastermind behind the 2017 assassination of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia.

For 107 consecutive months - on the 16th of every month since Caruana Galizia was killed by a car bomb outside her home - civil society groups held silent vigils. But the Sept. 2 acquittal of Yorgen Fenech, a prominent businessman accused of orchestrating and financing the plot, transformed that quiet grief into open defiance.

Chanting “Mafia! Mafia!” and “Injustice!”, thousands of protesters marched from the Parliament building to a memorial standing directly opposite Malta’s Law Courts to lay flowers and light candles before Caruana Galizia’s portrait. Banners carried by the crowd called for the protection of journalists and democracy, declaring: “The Trial Has Ended. Our Work Has Not” and “Impunity Ends Here.”

title: The Genius Logic of the NATO Phonetic Alphabet: How It Was Created & How It Works
content: Most of us can rattle off the first few words-that-stand-for-letters of the NATO phonetic alphabet. Alfa, Bravo, and Charlie no doubt come right to mind, and depending on how many war movies you’ve seen, so may Delta, Echo, and Foxtrot. But how many of us would recognize Kilo, Mike, and Sierra? For that matter, how much do any of us know about how these particular words came to be used to spell out other words when communicating over walkie-talkies or other low-fidelity communication systems? In the video above for his YouTube channel RobWords, YouTuber Rob Watts explains the development of and logic behind the NATO phonetic alphabet, wasting no time in clarifying that it isn’t a phonetic alphabet, nor was it created by NATO.

title: What AI urgency? Industry and leaders split on how to handle advanced tech’s threats
content:
The seeming unanimity among artificial intelligence industry powerhouses about addressing AI’s potential threats to humanity is already splintering.

Four days after OpenAI, Anthropic and Elon Musk locked arms behind a call to slow AI’s advances, a phalanx of industry leaders and lawmakers speaking Wednesday at POLITICO’s Decoded Summit came to no consensus on how to regulate the technology — despite mostly agreeing that it’s a task someone should lead.

Anthropic policy chief Sarah Heck declined to endorse the same proposal for congressionally mandated independent AI monitoring that OpenAI had backed the day before. Progressive Rep. Greg Casar (D-Texas) advocated mandatory limits on the technology and the creation of a federal agency to regulate it, while House Energy and Commerce Chair Brett Guthrie (R-Ky.) said speed is less important than getting the policy right — and the two clashed on whether Americans should care about beating China.

title: Kaavoituksen sujuvoittaminen ei saa tapahtua osallisuuden ja ympäristön laadun kustannuksella
content:
Hallituksen esitys alueidenkäyttölaiksi on edennyt valiokuntakäsittelyyn. Esityksessä tavoitellaan kaavoituksen sujuvoittamista.

Vaikka sujuva kaavoitus on kannatettava tavoite, sitä ei tule toteuttaa kansalaisten osallistumis- ja vaikutusmahdollisuuksia heikentämällä. Kuntalaisten näkemykset ovat keskeinen osa kaavoitusta asiantuntijatiedon rinnalla.

Ehdotetut muutokset tekevät kuntalaisten osallistumisesta nykyistä haastavampaa, vaikka kaavoitusjärjestelmä pysyisi lakiehdotuksen mukaan pääosin ennallaan. Kaavoitusta on seurattava aktiivisesti, digitaalisessa ympäristössä on osattava toimia ja ottaa kantaa oikeaan aikaan.

Kansalaisten valitusoikeus on keskeinen osa alueidenkäytön järjestelmää ja demokraattista päätöksentekoa. Perustuslain 20 § velvoittaa julkisen vallan turvaamaan jokaiselle mahdollisuuden vaikuttaa elinympäristöään koskevaan päätöksentekoon.

Nykyisessä lainsäädännössä valitusoikeus on kunnan jäsenillä sekä asianosaisilla. Lakiehdotus rajaisi valitusoikeuden asemakaavasta niihin, joiden oikeuteen, velvollisuuteen tai etuun päätös välittömästi vaikuttaa.

title: Forskningens frihet har försvagats i Finland – riksdagsvalet avgör riktningen
content:
Tillsammans med flera andra vetenskapliga organisationer uppmanar vi partier och kandidater att berätta hur de tänker trygga förutsättningarna för fri forskning.

Finland har tappat mark som ett av de ledande länderna när det gäller forskningsfrihet. Forskare utsätts i allt högre grad för trakasserier, och deras arbete påverkas allt mer av politisk och ekonomisk styrning. Samtidigt ökar behovet av oberoende, forskningsbaserad kunskap till följd av miljökriser och andra säkerhetshot, ekonomisk oro och desinformation.

I riksdagsvalet våren 2027 väljer vi de beslutsfattare som avgör förutsättningarna för forskning och ny kunskap i Finland. Väljarna har rätt att kräva tydliga svar av kandidaterna: Hur tänker de försvara forskningens och forskarnas frihet? Hur ska forskningens långsiktiga finansiering tryggas? Och hur tänker de stärka den öppna vetenskapens ställning och användningen av forskningsbaserad kunskap i beslutsfattandet?

En grupp centrala aktörer inom vetenskapsområdet lyfter fram dessa frågor i valdebatten genom kampanjen Släpp forskningen fri.

title: Nordic Digital Music Survey 2026: Vaikka tekoälyn yleinen käyttö on kasvanut, vaativat pohjoismaalaiset musiikilta läpinäkyvyyttä ja ihmisen luovuutta
content:
Tekoälystä on tullut nopeasti osa pohjoismaalaisten arkea, mutta suhtautuminen tekoälyn tuottamaan musiikkiin on muuttunut aiempaa kriittisemmäksi. Tämä selviää Pohjoismaiden musiikin tekijöiden tekijänoikeusjärjestöjen Teoston, Kodan (Tanska) ja TONOn (Norja) tuoreesta Nordic Digital Music Survey 2026 -tutkimuksesta.

Tuoreen tutkimuksen mukaan tekoälyä omassa arjessaan tai työssään käyttävien ruotsalaisten, suomalaisten, norjalaisten ja tanskalaisen osuus on kasvanut ainoastaan kahdessa vuodessa 20 prosentista 66 prosenttiin. Samaan aikaan asenteet tekoälymusiikkia vastaan ovat selvästi tiukentuneet.

Suurin osa, lähes 80 prosenttia pohjoismaalaisista katsoo, että ilman ihmisen luovaa panosta tuotettu tekoälymusiikki pitäisi merkitä selkeästi kanavissa, joissa niitä on tarjolla. Vuonna 2024 merkintää kannatti vain 58 prosenttia vastaajista.
