title: Mieli ry: Ikääntyneiden elämänkokemus on alihyödynnetty voimavara
content:
Suomalaisessa yhteiskunnassa ikääntyminen nähdään julkisessa keskustelussa yhä usein uhkakuvana – taakkana, joka rasittaa palvelujärjestelmää ja huoltosuhdetta. Mielenterveysjärjestö MIELI ry haluaa kääntää katseen toisin päin: ikääntyneiden vuosikymmenten aikana karttunut selviytymiskyky voisi olla merkittävä voimavara koko yhteiskunnalle, mutta sitä hyödynnetään toistaiseksi liian vähän.

"Iäkkäillä on kokemusta siitä, miten vaikeita aikoja kohdataan ja miten niiden kanssa eletään. Se voisi olla yhteiskunnan voimavara ja kannatella yhteisöjä", sanoo MIELI ry:n johtava asiantuntija Sirkkaliisa Heimonen tiedotteessa.

Kielteiset mielikuvat ikääntymisestä elävät sitkeästi, vaikka tutkimustieto kertoo toista. THL:n ja Ikäinstituutin vuonna 2023 julkaiseman raportin mukaan valtaosa ikääntyneistä kokee itsensä onnelliseksi. Parhaiten mielen hyvinvointia raportoivat 65–74-vuotiaat, ja hyvinvointi alkaa laskea vasta myöhemmin – raportin mukaan miehillä noin 80 ja naisilla noin 75 ikävuoden jälkeen. Silloinkin yli puolet voi tutkimuksen mukaan edelleen vähintään kohtuullisesti.

Heimosen mukaan puhe pelkästä toimintakyvyn heikkenemisestä hämärtää helposti sen, mitä ikääntyneillä on annettavaa.

title: Women, Innovation and Impact: Illustrating the global progress of WIPO’s first IP and Gender Action Plan
content: The “Women, Innovation and Impact” documents three years of implementation of the IP and Gender Action Plan (IPGAP), WIPO’s first strategy on IP in support of women and girls. It compiles stories under each of the IPGAP's three interconnected areas: helping governments integrate considerations for women into IP policy, legislation, and institutional practice; building the evidence base that makes the case for progress through data collection and research; and delivering direct support to women entrepreneurs, innovators, and creators through IP strategy, business development, and economic empowerment programs. The stories are a representative selection, chosen to reflect the breadth of achievements across regions, sectors, and areas of work, while underlining the remaining work. Taken together, this resource constitutes a call for more urgent and ambitious action to ensure that women's contributions are represented more fully in the global IP ecosystem.

title: Ukraine Advances: The Tank Isn’t Finished Yet
content:
Ukraine’s 3 Army Corps, acting under strict operational silence, has been conducting a counterattack in the Lyman sector for months. The cloud of secrecy has now been lifted, and Russian forces have lost a significant amount of territory. The operation, named Vivaldi, has so far officially cleared 75 sq km (29 sq miles), Ukrainian forces say. It is not yet over.

“In Vivaldi, as you know, there are four seasons,” Brig. Gen. Andriy Biletsky said on September 15. “And this is only the first . . . Good news is coming.”

Russia’s leadership had hoped to encircle Ukraine’s formidable fortress belt in western Donbas, but the northern salient has been reduced, with Russian warbloggers claiming it will extend the battle for Donbas by a year. Credible independent sources say the Ukrainian territorial gain is even greater.

Tech CEOs banding together is an old ruse recycled from corporate America to get a pass from antitrust laws

The safety breach disclosed by OpenAI after a swarm of its agents coordinated to breach their supposedly secure sandbox, get on the Internet and hack AI platform Hugging Face, warrants urgent action. title: Arizona Lowered the Bar for Its English Fluency Test. Experts Say It Will Harm Students in the Long Run.
content:
Samantha Ramos stood at the front of her second grade classroom, a small mic clipped to her lanyard amplifying her instructions as she began a phonics lesson.

“Can we get our arms ready?” asked Ramos, who’s taught at the John B. Wright Elementary School in Tucson, Arizona, for 15 years. She brought her right palm to her left shoulder as the students imitated her movements.

Ramos, who specializes in teaching English as a second language, was leading a lesson that day on the short “i” sound. She told the students to pronounce each letter with a different gesture — touching the shoulder for the “w,” the elbow for the “i” and the hand for the double “l” — before sounding out the word “will.” They repeated the process for other short “i” words — “dig,” “wig” and “fit.”

title: Open Weights Are Good. Open Source Is Better.
content:
By this point, you’ve seen the news about open-weight AI models and the debate over their security, efficiency, and impact on both local and national economies. Scores of businesses have come out in support of open-weights, highlighting how they increase access to advanced AI and maintain competition in the market. This is all true, and shedding light on these arguments benefits the Open Source community. 

At the same time, we must take this moment, when openness in AI is making headlines, to educate policymakers, producers, and users of these technologies about what open-weight and Open Source AI mean for the four software freedoms: the freedom to use, study, modify, and share without the need to ask for permission from the rights holder. Those are the core tenets of the Open Source movement that power the technology we use every day. Those are the tenets that built the Open Source ecosystem with a demand-side value of $8.8 trillion. It’s those tenets that we should strive to uphold in this next phase of technological development.

title: Wendell Berry spent his life farming and writing – his legacy is an ethic of care for the natural world
content:
The American farmer, novelist and poet Wendell Berry, died on August 31 2026, aged 92. Berry farmed in Port Royal, in his native Kentucky, for over 40 years. Through his writing and his farming, Berry emphasised the importance of both community and care for the planet, advocating for small-scale agriculture as key for both.

He criticised modern consumer culture, suggesting, in his poem Manifesto: The Mad Farmer Liberation Front, that instead of buying into the rat race, people should: “Love the world. Work for nothing […] / Say that your main crop is the forests / that you did not plant / that you will not live to harvest.”

His prolific output included The Unsettling of America: Culture and Agriculture (1977), Why I Am Not Going to Buy a Computer (1987) and The Mad Farmer Poems (2008).

Caring for the planet, Berry believed, means recognising your own place in it. Not as the centre, but as part of a wider community of interconnected life. In doing so, Berry’s writing highlights an important new theme in environmental humanities: a growing interest in “georgic” writing as an environmental genre.

title: Analysis: Global fossil-fuel emissions set to fall in 2026 amid Hormuz crisis
content:
Global fossil-fuel emissions are set to fall by around 0.5% in 2026 amid the fallout from the Hormuz crisis, according to Carbon Brief analysis.

The US-Iran war has severely disrupted trade through the strait of Hormuz, causing a spike in oil and gas prices that continues to ripple around the global economy.

Each month of disruption – and each new flashpoint, such as in Yemen – is increasing the incentive to switch to alternatives.

Those alternatives include coal, with the latest forecasts pointing to a 1.2% rise in coal demand this year – apparently supporting media claims of a “return to coal” in the wake of the crisis.

Yet Carbon Brief’s analysis shows the rise in emissions associated with this increased coal use, much of which is unrelated to Hormuz, is set to be more than offset by declines for oil and gas.

The estimated overall impact on carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from fossil fuels in 2026 is shown in the figure below and amounts to a reduction of around 0.5% from 2025 levels.

(Fossil fuels account for two-thirds of global greenhouse gas emissions.)

title: "The Elimination Project": Israel’s Systematic Dismantling of Palestinian Life in West Bank: B'Tselem
content:
A major new report by the Israeli human rights group B’Tselem titled “The Elimination Project” accuses Israel of “dramatically intensifying its attacks on every aspect of Palestinian life in the West Bank.”

“For too long, Israel’s policies in the West Bank have been treated or looked at as isolated events,” says Ori Givati, director of international relations at B’Tselem. “We actually find that there is one very coherent logic behind all of them, and this is the logic of elimination of Palestinian collective life in the West Bank.” Givati says tactics against Palestinians intensified with Israel’s 2022 election and again after October 7, 2023, adding that “we are definitely seeing a lot of the mechanisms, the tools that were used and are used still … in Gaza, being implemented in the West Bank.”

title: Victory: Court, Using a New Test, Rules Embedding Links is Legal
content:
Courts have for two decades found that linking and embedding someone else’s web content, be it a photo, music, or an article, doesn’t violate copyright law–the entity that controls the server that hosts a copyrighted work, not the user or website that merely directs others to it, is directly liable if the content turns out to be infringing.

News publisher Emmerich Newspapers sought to convince the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals to chart a new and dangerous course, arguing that an aggregator website that published links to its copyrighted articles was in effect “displaying” them and can be directly liable for infringement. EFF, along with several other public interest organizations and trade associations, filed a brief urging the court to follow multiple other circuits and reject that theory.

Fortunately, the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals did just that. While it rejected the server test–the rule courts have used to determine copyright liability rests with whoever serves up the content–the court came to the same practical conclusion by focusing on who is responsible for transmitting content.

title: Kansallisarkiston Jyväskylän toimipaikka sulkeutuu – viimeinen aukiolopäivä 29.9.2026
content:
Kansallisarkisto luopuu Jyväskylän toimipaikasta 1.1.2027 lukien, kuten aiemmin on tiedotettu.

Tutkijasalipalvelu Jyväskylän toimipaikassa päättyy 29.9.2026. Toimipaikan tutkijasali on avoinna syyskuussa vielä seuraavasti:

  • tiistaina 22.9. kello 9–16
  • tiistaina 29.9. kello 9–16.

    • Lisäksi luvanvarainen itsepalveluasiointi on mahdollista 23.–24. syyskuuta klo 9–16.

    Rajoitetun digitaalisen aineiston käyttö asiakaskoneilla päättyy samassa yhteydessä, kun tutkijasali sulkeutuu.

    Jyväskylän aineistot siirretään muihin Kansallisarkiston toimipaikkoihin, suurin osa Ouluun. Tuomiokuntien ja raastuvanoikeuksien sekä henkikirjoittajien arkistot siirretään Vaasaan.

    Aineistosiirrot alkavat 28.9. ja jatkuvat aina vuoden loppuun saakka. Tänä aikana aineistojen käytössä esiintyy katkoksia: siirrossa olevia aineistoja ei toimiteta digitaalisesti tai tutkijasaliin.

title: Reforms to Hungary's Anti-LGBT Laws Welcome, but More to Do
content:
Hungary’s new government has taken an important step toward dismantling a key discriminatory legacy of the Orbán era—the legal targeting of LGBT people. The job is not finished, however.

The government submitted legislation to Parliament on September 14 to remove several provisions of the 2021 so-called “child protection” law that restrict the “portrayal” or “promotion” of sexual and gender diversity in content accessible to children. The proposed changes remove the restrictions from laws relating to child protection, media, advertising, and education.

The reforms follow an April judgment by the Court of Justice of the European Union finding that Hungary’s legal restrictions stigmatized and marginalized LGBT people and violated EU law. The court found that Hungary could not invoke the best interests of the child to justify restrictions that discriminated against LGBT people and violated fundamental rights.

title: French Prosecutors Seek Up to 5 Years in Prison for Sons of Ex-Yemeni President Saleh Over Ill-Gotten Assets
content:
Two sons of late Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh could face up to five years in prison as a Paris court hears charges against them for allegedly laundering tens of millions of euros in embezzled state funds and corruption proceeds.

The trial, which opened September 7 at the Paris Criminal Court, follows a 2019 investigation launched by France's National Financial Prosecutor's Office (PNF) based on a tip-off from Swiss authorities, the PNF confirmed to OCCRP on Wednesday.

Brothers Ahmed Ali Saleh, 54, and Khaled Ali Saleh, 39, are accused of laundering proceeds from corruption and laundering embezzled public funds as part of an organized criminal group. Both men are being tried in absentia and are believed to be residing in Dubai.

Their father, Ali Abdullah Saleh, ruled Yemen for 33 years until his ouster during the Arab Spring in 2012. The former president was accused of plundering billions in state funds throughout his long tenure to enrich his family and inner circle. He was killed by Houthi rebels in 2017.

title: Watch Footage from the Psychology Experiment That Shocked the World: Milgram’s Obedience Study (1961)
content:
For decades following World War II,  the world was left wondering how the atrocities of the Holocaust could have been perpetrated in the midst of—and, most horrifically, by—a modern and civilized society. How did people come to engage in a willing and systematic extermination of their neighbors? Psychologists, whose field had grown into a grudgingly respected science by the midpoint of the 20th century, were eager to tackle the question.

In 1961, Yale University’s Stanley Milgram began a series of infamous obedience experiments. While Adolf Eichmann’s trial was underway in Jerusalem (resulting in Hannah Arendt’s five-piece reportage, which became one of The New Yorker magazine’s most dramatic and controversial article series), Milgram began to suspect that human nature was more straightforward than earlier theorists had imagined; he wondered, as he later wrote, “Could it be that Eichmann and his million accomplices in the Holocaust were just following orders? Could we call them all accomplices?”

title: ‘The US can’t lose’: Pentagon plows ahead on AI despite warnings
content:
Pentagon leaders are racing to insert artificial intelligence into nearly every corner of the military, even as lawmakers scramble to figure out guardrails.

Defense Department officials insist any slowdown in AI development could cede control to adversaries, dismissing calls from industry leaders and members of Congress to pause and better understand the long-term ramifications of the computer systems.

That tension is playing out in real time as the Pentagon faces increasingly bold threats from China and Russia. But the military’s rush to stay ahead brings separate risks if it fails to safeguard hastily implemented AI tech.

“Winning and staying ahead in the AI race is probably one of the most important things for the United States to do, both from a military and economic security perspective,” Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said. “That is a race that the U.S. can’t lose.”

But critics warn the rush to use advanced AI in national security operations could also open sensitive military systems to new threats, especially if leaders aren’t deliberate about installing defenses during upgrades.

title: Ei vain tahroja paperilla – visiot auttavat johtamaan muutosta
content:
• Etusivu

    • Blogi

    Suomi on vaikean kaksoishaasteen edessä. Taloutta on toisaalta sopeutettava nopeasti ja toisaalta uudistettava pitkäjänteisesti. Näiden tarpeiden yhdistäminen edellyttää yhteistä käsitystä Suomen suunnasta. Apua kannattaa hakea visioista, sillä ne auttavat tekemään valintoja.

    Asiantuntija, Ennakointi ja koulutus

    Blogi

    Julkaistu

    16.9.2026

    Tänä syksynä Suomi-rockin jättiläinen Eppu Normaali lopetti 50 vuotta jatkuneen uransa. ”Tarhoja paperilla” on yksi yhtyeen tunnetuimmista kappaleista. Sen lyriikoihin tiivistyy myös monien epäluulo visioita kohtaan: ne ovat vain tahroja paperilla eikä niistä asiat miksikään muutu.

    Kriitikot ovat oikeassa siinä, että visiot eivät itsessään ratkaise Suomen talouden tai yhteiskunnan ongelmia. Silti Suomi tarvitsee visioita kipeämmin kuin pitkään aikaan.

    Visiot ovat talouspolitiikan johtamisen ja toimeenpanon työkaluja. Ne voivat osoittautua erityisen hyödylliseksi Suomen historiallisen vaikean kaksoishaasteen äärellä.

    Yhtäältä on sopeuduttava mahdollisimman nopeasti julkisen talouden, väestörakenteen ja turvallisuusympäristön asettamiin reunaehtoihin ja pidettävä yllä valmiutta reagoida yllätyksiin.

title: Älä uuvu, aktivisti – jonain päivänä sinua saatetaan tarvita vastarintaan
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Maailman tilasta ahdistuneelle ihmiselle voi suositella yhtä hieman epätavanomaista harjoitusta: ajattele maailmaa muutaman miljardin vuoden perspektiivillä.

Lopputulos on nimittäin jo tiedossa.

Auringon ikääntyessä sen säteilyteho hitaasti kasvaa. Noin kahden miljardin vuoden kuluttua lisääntyvä lämpö alkaa haihduttaa Maan valtameriä, ja planeetan pinnasta tulee nykyisenkaltaiselle elämälle elinkelvoton. Noin viiden miljardin vuoden kuluttua Aurinko paisuu punaiseksi jättiläiseksi. Se nielaisee varmasti Merkuriuksen ja Venuksen ja saattaa nielaista myös Maan – joka tapauksessa Maa on siinä vaiheessa ollut elinkelvoton jo miljardeja vuosia.

Maailmanlopun suhteen voimme siis rentoutua hieman. Se hoitaa kyllä itse itsensä, aikataulussa, ilman meidän apuamme.

Paljon vaikeampi kysymys on, mitä teemme siihen asti.

Ympäristökriisin yksi psykologisesti raskaimmista puolista on seurata, kuinka suuri osa ihmisistä näyttää jatkavan elämäänsä aivan kuin mitään erityistä ei olisi tapahtumassa.

title: Russia’s Neighbors Battle Oil Addiction
content:
Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Kazakhstan cut ties with the Soviet Union more than three decades ago, and have developed their own economies and foreign policies. Yet in the critical area of energy security, not much has changed; they remain heavily dependent on the Kremlin’s goodwill.

The crisis began to unfold this spring and summer, as Ukraine’s long-range drone attacks on Russia’s refineries got increasingly successful. On July 6, drones reached the Omsk refinery for the first time, some 2,700 km (1,700 miles) from the Ukrainian border, and Russia’s largest refining facility was forced to halt production.

Omsk, the eleventh major gasoline producer to be struck, was the principal supplier of petroleum products to Central Asia and Mongolia. And disruption followed as Moscow prioritized supplying its own regions with fuel.

While it was never part of the Soviet Union, Mongolia is the most vulnerable to the shock, as more than 90% of its petroleum products come from Russia. Lines formed at filling stations in Ulaanbaatar and significant restrictions on fuel sales were introduced.

title: The Significance of The Enemy States Clause for Germany
content:
By Michael von der Schulenburg

BRUSSELS | 16 September 2026 (IDN) — When the Allies of the Second World War drafted the United Nations Charter, they sought to establish a global system of collective security. Its aim was to “save succeeding generations from the scourge of war”. With the adoption of the UN Charter, all UN Member States undertook to settle their disputes in future exclusively by peaceful means, and not through military force. Decisions on the use of force to maintain or restore peace were only to be taken collectively, initially by the eleven and now by the fifteen members of the United Nations Security Council.

However, the UN Charter contains an exception that has been largely forgotten today: the so-called ‘enemy states clause’ in Articles 53, 77 and 107. It grants the former Allied powers the right to take military action against the enemy states of the former Axis powers, without a Security Council mandate, in order to prevent renewed aggression by those states against them. Because the Security Council is expressly excluded, each former Ally could assess whether a former Axis power was once again adopting an aggressive stance.

title: Meta is changing Instagram and Facebook to protect teens’ mental health. Are the new measures backed up by science?
content:
The recent landmark ruling against Meta in the United States was the result of a lawsuit filed in 2023 which went to trial in August 2026. It was brought by nearly fifty attorneys general, school districts and families, who alleged that the company’s social media platforms, which include Instagram and Facebook, pose serious risks to mental health.

The case ended in a $18 billion dollar settlement, and imposed direct structural changes on the way Instagram and Facebook operate. These could eventually extend to other platforms and social media networks, according to Attorney General William Tong.

Here, we will look at the scientific basis for each of the new measures.

Firstly, the agreement sets a limit of two hours’ use per day for under-18s, alongside regular reminders to encourage breaks and more self-regulated use.

Scientific research supports the general idea of limiting time spent on social media and encouraging breaks while using it. However, this does not make the two-hour limit a universal medical threshold, nor are the regular reminders scientifically established intervals.

title: Why is Amnesty International calling for international justice for crimes against humanity in Iran?
content:
Content warning: This article contains descriptions of violence, including shootings, beatings, torture, sexual violence, and discrimination. It also mentions issues relating to suicide. We include these details to honour the victims and their families, who want the truth to be brought to light.

Protesters in Iran have been killed, tortured or imprisoned in the thousands for demanding their human rights and political change. The officials responsible for protest-related crimes against humanity are evading justice while survivors and relatives seeking justice are persecuted.

In late 2022, Iran was gripped by large-scale protests that became known as the Woman Life Freedom uprising. After years of painstaking investigations, Amnesty International has exposed how the Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity to crush the uprising. Based on its extensive documentation of the crimes committed and analysis of the security forces’ command structures, Amnesty International has identified 87 officials who must be criminally investigated for their role in these crimes.

title: A Russian Oligarch Secretly Funded Donald Trump Jr.'s Bahamas Wedding; Democrats Demand Probe
content:
Congressional Democrats have opened an investigation after ProPublica revealed on Monday that a Russian oligarch close to Vladimir Putin bankrolled part of Donald Trump Jr.’s Bahamas wedding in May. ProPublica reports that Umar Kremlev paid hundreds of thousands of dollars on wedding expenses, including the rental of a private island. Just weeks before the wedding, Putin awarded Kremlev the Order of Friendship.

Trump Jr. and his wife, Bettina Anderson, confirmed _ProPublica_’s findings in a social media post, specifying that Kremlev only paid for an afterparty.

“The most important thing to understand about Kremlev is the level of his connection with the Russian government. Right before the wedding … he was reportedly traveling in China as part of Putin’s delegation,” says Joshua Kaplan, the ProPublica reporter who was part of the team that broke the story. “He’s spent a lot of money seemingly successfully cultivating a relationship with the son of the president, and we have no idea why.”

title: EFF Welcomes Alexander Macgillivray to its Board of Directors
content:
The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) is honored to announce today that Alexander “amac” Macgillivray — a former White House official who also served in top legal capacities at Twitter and Google — has joined EFF’s Board of Directors. 

Macgillivray served in the Biden Administration as Deputy Assistant to the President and Principal Deputy U.S. Chief Technology Officer in the Office of Science and Technology Policy, and earlier had held a similar position in the Obama Administration. Macgillivray was one of the co-authors of the Biden Administration’s Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights and oversaw many of the Administration’s AI initiatives, such as organizing its AI CEO convening, leading its working group on federal AI policy, and overseeing the creation of the National AI Research and Development Strategic Plan and National AI Research Resource. 

He was Twitter's General Counsel from 2009 to 2013, leading the Corporate Development, Public Policy, Communications, and Trust & Safety teams. Before that he was Deputy General Counsel at Google from 2003 to 2009, where he created the Product Counsel team.

title: Tieteen vapaus on heikentynyt Suomessa – eduskuntavaaleissa valitaan suunta
content:
Suomen asema tieteen vapauden kärkimaana on heikentynyt. Tutkijoiden työhön kohdistuu aiempaa enemmän häirintää, ja tutkimuksen poliittinen ja taloudellinen ohjaus on vahvistunut. Samaan aikaan ekologinen kriisi ja muut turvallisuusuhat, huoli taloudesta ja disinformaatio kasvattavat riippumattoman tutkitun tiedon tarvetta.

Kevään 2027 eduskuntavaaleissa valitaan päättäjät, jotka ratkaisevat myös sen, millaiset edellytykset Suomessa annetaan uuden tiedon syntymiselle. Äänestäjät voivat vaatia ehdokkailta selkeitä vastauksia: miten he puolustavat tieteen ja tutkijoiden vapautta, turvaavat tutkimuksen pitkäjänteisen rahoituksen ja vahvistavat tutkitun tiedon asemaa päätöksenteossa?

Joukko tiedekentän keskeisiä toimijoita tuo nämä kysymykset vaalikeskusteluun Vapaa tiede ratkaisee -kampanjalla. Kampanja tuo esiin sen, kuinka tärkeää tieteen vapaudesta ja resursseista huolehtiminen on monikriisin keskellä.

Tulevalla vaalikaudella on tehtävä selkeä valinta: panostetaanko vapaaseen tieteeseen vai tingitäänkö toivosta.

title: Puheenjohtaja Näkkäläjärvi European Arctic Summitissa Rovaniemellä: Alkuperäiskansat ovat osa arktista turvallisuutta
content:
Saamelaiskäräjien puheenjohtaja Pirita Näkkäläjärvi lausui avaussanat pääministeri Petteri Orpon isännöimässä European Arctic Summit -huippukokouksessa Rovaniemellä 14.9.2026. Puheenjohtaja Näkkäläjärvi korosti Euroopan valtionjohtajille, ettei kestävää arktista turvallisuutta synny ilman arktisen alueen ihmisiä ja elinvoimaisia alkuperäiskansoja.

Puheenjohtaja Pirita Näkkäläjärvi, pääministeri Petteri Orpo ja Lapin yliopiston rehtori Antti Syväjärvi. Kuva: Lauri Heikkinen/Valtioneuvoston kanslia.

– Arktista turvallisuutta ei ole ilman ihmisiä ja alkuperäiskansoja. Me tarvitsemme olosuhteet, jotka mahdollistavat sen, että voimme elää, jatkaa perinteitämme ja rakentaa tulevaisuutemme arktisella alueella. title: Al-Qaida and IS-linked violence in Africa’s Sahel belt set to hit record levels this year
content:
Twenty-five years after 9/11, figures compiled by conflict monitor underline how Sahel region has become centre of Islamist terror

Islamist extremist violence in Africa’s Sahel region is set to reach historic highs after a series of sweeping offensives by groups linked to al-Qaida and Islamic State, according to new figures compiled by the conflict monitor Acled.

As the US marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks launched by al-Qaida against targets in Washington and New York, the statistics underline the continued expansion of the veteran organisation in parts of Africa – in stark contrast with its relative weakness elsewhere.

title: From Fugitive to Federal Custody: Inside the Takedown of South America’s ‘King of the South’
content:
When federal agents reached out to Sebastián Marset through his girlfriend in March 2025 to persuade him to surrender, the Uruguayan drug lord who styled himself the “King of the South” mocked them, boasting that he was "smarter than the entire D.E.A. put together."

“I’m not going to surrender,” Marset declared, according to court records. “I’ll be a criminal for the rest of my life.”

Almost a year later, heavily armed Bolivian special forces raided a residential neighborhood in Santa Cruz in the pre-dawn hours, capturing the fugitive who had evaded international law enforcement for years.

By that evening, one of the most powerful drug barons in South America’s Southern Cone - wanted by federal prosecutors for laundering millions of dollars in illicit proceeds through American banks - landed on U.S. soil in handcuffs.

Now held in a federal detention center in Virginia, Marset is mounting an aggressive legal defense. A new series of court filings has laid bare a detailed record of his global operations, missing evidence, and his own cynical view of regional law enforcement.

title: Hugging Face CEO: Advanced AI models require new transparency mandates
content:
The CEO whose company fell victim to history’s first known autonomous artificial intelligence cyberattack said the government should do more to require transparency by advanced AI models — and ensure that their developers are held liable for harms their products cause.

That doesn’t mean Congress needs to create a raft of new regulations prohibiting malicious cyberattacks, Hugging Face CEO and co-founder Clem Delangue said Wednesday during the POLITICO Decoded Summit in D.C. But he said companies whose products inflict damage should not be able to dodge responsibility.

“I think it’s too easy to say: ‘OK, it was an agent. That did the bad thing and so no one is responsible,’” Delangue said. “It doesn’t work, in my opinion, because if you say that you’re going to end up in a world where everyone’s agent is attacking everyone’s with no clear kind of responsibility.”

He declined to comment on some specific legislation, including an AI liability proposal in California but said the government has a role to play in mandating disclosures of cyber incidents.

title: The US government is failing Americans on AI | Shakeel Hashim
content:
Trump and Republicans want companies to regulate themselves. It’s a dereliction of duty that will make AI less safe

It is hard to get Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Dario Amodei to agree on much. But over the weekend, all three AI company CEOs called for AI development to slow down in the face of growing, alarming risks. Their employees are sounding the siren too, with one researcher publicly quitting and accusing OpenAI and Anthropic of “gambling with our lives”.

The combination of dire warnings from insiders and growing real-world evidence of rogue AIs should, in a sane world, lead to government action. Instead, Donald Trump and the Republican leadership have their heads in the sand.

title: Why Ro Khanna and AOC Should Run for President in 2028
content:
By Jeff Cohen and Norman Solomon*

SAN FRANCISCO, USA | 16 September 2026 (IDN) — Fifteen years ago, during President Obama’s first term, we co-founded RootsAction as an online progressive group challenging not only Republicans but also the corporatism and militarism of the Democratic Party. RootsAction supported Bernie Sanders for president in 2016 and 2020.

Two years before the 2024 election disaster that returned Donald Trump to the White House, RootsAction launched the Don’t Run Joe campaign, with the warning that the renomination of Joe Biden by Democrats “would be a tragic mistake.”

Despite polls showing as early as 2022 that strong majorities of Democrats wanted a 2024 nominee other than Biden, the “Don’t Run Joe” message went unheeded until Biden’s debate debacle in June 2024. By then, it was too late for the open primary process needed to produce a ticket that could inspire activists – and defeat the fascistic faux-populism of Trump.

title: 👮 Flock Searches for the LOLs | EFFector 38.16
content:
Mass surveillance isn't a joke. But police are treating it like one when using automated license plate reader (ALPR) networks. In our latest EFFector newsletter, we're covering a new EFF report on how officers across the country are routinely logging completely nonsensical "reasons" for their Flock searches, including "LOL," "LMAO," and even (yuck) "Sexy."

JOIN OUR NEWSLETTER

For over 35 years, EFFector has been your guide to understanding the intersection of technology, civil liberties, and the law. This issue covers a settlement enshrining Meta's harmful surveillance into law, states pushing back against ALPR, and how police are turning our privacy into a punchline.

Prefer to listen in? EFFector is now available on all major podcast platforms. This time we're asking EFF's Adam Schwartz what has united people against Flock cameras — and how we can make sure that today's backlash leads to lasting change. title: Lapissa on käynnistetty toimintakykyyn keskittyvän osaamiskeskuksen valmistelu
content:
Lapin ammattikorkeakoulussa kehitetään uutta Arktista toimintakykyosaamiskeskusta, jonka tavoitteena on vahvistaa toimintakykyyn liittyvää tutkimusta, kehittämistä, koulutusta ja yhteistyötä pohjoisissa olosuhteissa. Osaamiskeskus kokoaa yhteen asiantuntijat, tutkimus- ja kehittämistoiminnan sekä alueelliset, kansalliset ja kansainväliset verkostot.

Lapin ammattikorkeakoulussa on jo vuosien ajan tehty toimintakykyyn liittyvää tutkimus-, kehittämis- ja innovaatiotyötä (TKI). TKI-toiminnassa on kehitetty muun muassa kuntoutuksen vaikuttavuuden arviointia, sosiaalisen kuntoutuksen toimintamalleja sekä digitaalisia ja teknologia-avusteisia palveluja. Erityisesti harvaan asutut ja arktiset toimintaympäristöt ovat olleet kehittämistyön keskiössä.

Vuosien myötä kertyneen osaamisen pohjalle rakentuva Arktinen toimintakykyosaamiskeskus kokoaa yhteen tutkimuksen, verkostot ja palveluinnovaatiot yhdeksi laajasti hyödynnettäväksi kokonaisuudeksi.

Toimintakyky nähdään ammattikorkeakoululla kokonaisvaltaisena fyysisenä, psyykkisenä ja sosiaalisena ilmiönä, joka mahdollistaa osallisuuden, opiskelu- ja työkyvyn sekä arjessa selviytymisen.

title: Ex-French Justice Minister Stands Trial Over Renault-Nissan Consultancy Case
content:
Criminal proceedings began Wednesday against Rachida Dati, France's former Minister of Justice and Minister of Culture, and currently the mayor of a Paris arrondissement over corruption allegations stemming from her alleged lobbying work for the Renault-Nissan car making group. 

Prosecutors accuse Dati of receiving 900,000 euros (over $1 million) between 2010 and 2012 for providing consulting services to a Dutch subsidiary of Renault-Nissan without actually performing any work, all while serving as a Member of the European Parliament and working as an attorney.

The former minister will stand trial for receiving the proceeds of abuse of authority and breach of trust, as well as for corruption and passive trading in influence committed by a person holding a public elective mandate within an international organization, the European Parliament.

She stands trial alongside co-defendant Carlos Ghosn, the former CEO of Renault-Nissan. Ghosn faces charges including abuse of corporate assets, breach of trust, corruption, and active trading in influence.

title: Anthropic policy chief says winning AI race key for safety
content:
Anthropic’s policy chief Sarah Heck said Wednesday that the U.S. can’t make artificial intelligence safer if it falls behind China in the global tech race.

“The United States needs to stay in the lead on AI, and you can’t do safety from second place,” the head of public policy said at POLITICO’s Decoded summit in Washington, echoing an argument often made by President Donald Trump and his advisers.

Heck’s comments made the case for export controls on the sale of AI chips to China. She repeatedly defended Anthropic as having a long history of being motivated by safety concerns and said it’s focused on working with lawmakers to pass new regulations for the technology.

“We do think it’s existential to do this. We do think we have to balance the risk now,” Heck said. “The capabilities are only increasing and increasing at a pace that is accelerating.”

title: How the Meta Settlement Silences Youth Activism
content:
Since its integration into our digital world, social media has played a pivotal role in youth organizing and social mobilization. Yet, people’s access to these platforms is increasingly coming under threat from courts and legislatures under the guise of protecting young people online—presenting a significant hindrance to youth organizing.  

In a major recent example, Meta settled in a lawsuit with 52 states and territories regarding the use of Instagram and Facebook by young people. The settlement will require Meta, and pressure other non-Meta owned platforms like TikTok and YouTube, to embed age gating practices into every product while also requiring restrictions on the accounts of people under-18, such as a two-hour daily time limit and content restrictions.

title: President Näkkäläjärvi at the European Arctic Summit in Rovaniemi: Indigenous Peoples are a part of Arctic security
content:
Sámi Parliament President Pirita Näkkäläjärvi delivered the opening remarks at the European Arctic Summit hosted by Prime Minister Petteri Orpo in Rovaniemi on 14 September 2026. President Näkkäläjärvi emphasised to European heads of government that sustainable Arctic security cannot be achieved without the people of the Arctic region and vital Indigenous People.

Sámi Parliament’s President Pirita Näkkäläjärvi, Prime Minister of Finland Petteri Orpo and University of Lapland Rector Antti Syväjärvi Photo: Lauri Heikkinen/Prime Minister’s Office.

In her remarks, President Näkkäläjärvi highlighted the Sámi as an Indigenous people and underlined the role of Indigenous Peoples as a part of Arctic security and resilience. She emphasised that Arctic security is ultimately also about the conditions of everyday life.

– There is no Arctic security without the people of the region and its Indigenous Peoples. We need conditions where we can live, continue our traditions and build our future in the Arctic. It is also important that our people can stay in the North — or return here after their studies, Näkkäläjärvi said.

title: Instead of Helping Ukraine’s Poor, Ferrexpo’s Charitable Donations Flowed to Companies Associated With Its Then-CEO
content:
In 2017, the mining giant Ferrexpo announced it had donated more than two percent of its annual revenue to a charity based near the company’s vast iron ore mines in central Ukraine. 

This charitable spending significantly outstripped the average of its industry peers, the London Stock Exchange-listed firm highlighted in an annual report. 

Yet just one year later, questions set in. 

Auditors from Deloitte noted in Ferrexpo’s 2018 annual report that they had been unable to conclude whether the charity, named Blooming Land, had in fact spent $33.5 million of Ferrexpo’s donations on charitable ends.

Ferrexpo halted donations to the charity, which it said had been set up to “independently” coordinate the firm’s corporate social responsibility spending, and commissioned an investigation into the matter.

But the results were inconclusive: an investigating committee said only that the funds “could have been misappropriated,” and that it was unable to determine the fate of the firm’s donations.

title: Von der Leyen’s call for talks on pausing AI can’t quell extinction risk fears
content:
STRASBOURG — Ursula von der Leyen has declared herself an AI “optimist.” Yet in the face of rising warnings of the technology’s threats to humanity, the European Commission president on Wednesday sounded far more like a realist — and one with limited room for maneuver.

Von der Leyen didn’t shy away from the topic in her State of the European Union address, calling AI one of the “two tipping points of our time” and acknowledging the dangers it poses.

“The warnings about the future of AI should make us more serious about safety,” said key European Parliament AI lawmaker Axel Voss after the speech, touting von der Leyen’s focus on “Europe’s human-centered approach to AI.”

Still, the Commission president’s most concrete response to recent calls by top Silicon Valley bosses to pause AI development was a cordial invitation to join her in a “discussion” on the matter.

And while citing the EU’s standing AI rules as a possible building block for global regulations, von der Leyen didn’t use her much-anticipated speech to call on fellow world leaders — particularly U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping — to come together to act.

title: An Update on Wayback Machine Access
content:
We’ve heard you: “Fix the Wayback Machine!”

Here’s what’s going on. The Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine has been hit by waves of high-volume automated traffic, and we’ve put protections in place to keep the service running. One recent change: we rewrote the message you see when a request is blocked with a 429 error — the HTTP code that means “too many requests.”

Those protections sometimes catch real people by mistake. If that’s happened to you, we’re sorry, and we appreciate your patience while we work to reduce the errors.

We’re getting better at telling abusive bots apart from the people who depend on the Wayback Machine every day. If you think you were blocked in error, email info@archive.org with your operating system, browser, and IP address, and we’ll look into it.

title: A Commitment to Trustworthy and Authentic Information: Technological Transformation Over the Centuries
content:
Artificial intelligence is transforming society and institutions worldwide. The Library of Congress, founded in 1800, has been through numerous major technological revolutions since then—pneumatic tubes and telephones, printed card catalogs and talking books, machine-readable records and automation, computer terminals, digitization, data storage, the internet, mobile devices, and APIs.

In some ways, the implementation of AI is similar to previous technological and digital transformations. In others, it is unlike anything that has come before.

AI technologies are improving rapidly, and the Library’s approach to engaging with them calls on its history and a strong foundation of IT security and governance. This strategy focuses on embracing new technologies with care, building on decades of technological innovation, and balancing human judgment with machine capabilities.

Now the largest library in the world, the Library’s mission is to “engage, inspire, and inform Congress and the American people with a universal and enduring source of knowledge and creativity.” The Library’s approach to AI considers the road traveled through previous technology revolutions to inform this strategy.

title: Who Holds the Switch?
content:
Until recently, governments controlled the means to wage war. No longer. Private companies own and manage critical military infrastructure like satellites, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence. Call it the switch power. For policymakers, the shift in control deserves attention.

The clearest early signal of switch power came in Ukraine. Ukrainian forces were preparing a naval drone strike against Russia’s Black Sea Fleet off occupied Crimea. The operation depended on Starlink.  Elon Musk declined to activate it, arguing the strike risked excessive escalation. No government could force immediate activation; no alliance mechanism stepped in; Kyiv had no recourse beyond persuasion. 

It’s a dangerous dependency. Even though most of the key switch companies are American, they often balk at following orders and find themselves in conflict with the US government — or held hostage by hostile governments. For Europe, reliance on US companies sits awkwardly alongside ambitions for strategic autonomy.

title: ‘Kyiv regime and EU patrons are looting Crimean treasures’: Russian exhibition in Bratislava pushes Kremlin propaganda
content:
The Russian Embassy in Slovakia this week announced on social media the opening of a photo exhibition in Bratislava titled “Crimean Gold: ‘Civilised’ Europe Plunders Russian Treasures”. 

The exhibition, organised by the Russian Military Historical Society, presents annexed Ukrainian Crimea as Russian territory and offers its version of the dispute with the Netherlands over archaeological artefacts from Crimean museums. 

The artefacts were temporarily displayed in Amsterdam. Following Russia’s annexation of Crimea in 2014, Dutch courts ruled that they should not be returned to the occupied peninsula but directly to Ukraine, which has a legitimate right to protect its cultural heritage. 

In a Facebook post, the Russian Embassy openly challenges that decision. It calls it a “dangerous precedent of politicising cultural heritage” and claims that the exhibits were stolen by the “Kyiv regime together with its European patrons”. 

EuBrief contacted the Foreign Ministry and the City of Bratislava about the exhibition on Friday.

title: Top Oversight Dem Opens Investigation of Donald Trump Jr.’s Russian Oligarch-Funded Wedding
content:
The top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee launched an investigation into Donald Trump Jr.’s relationship with a Russian oligarch who paid for much of Trump Jr.’s wedding earlier this year.

Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., sent two letters on Monday to the White House and Trump Jr. requesting records related to Trump Jr.’s financial relationship with the oligarch, Umar Kremlev.

“The secretive, close relationship between the son of a sitting U.S. President and a member of Russian dictator Vladimir Putin’s inner circle raises serious national security and public corruption concerns,” Garcia wrote. Garcia told Trump Jr. it “may be the most serious allegation against you to date.” The letter to Trump Jr. asked for documents including Trump Jr.’s communications with Kremlev and “financial records of all purchases made for your wedding by foreign nationals.”

Learn more about this story on ProPublica’s podcast “Paper Trail.”

Trump Jr. did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Garcia’s investigation.
snippet: The top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee launched an investigation into Donald Trump Jr.’s relationship with a Russian oligarch who paid for much of Trump Jr.’s wedding earlier this year.

title: The Nordic-Baltic Eight policy brief: NB8 and the drone challenge
content:
New publication in the NB8 policy brief series by Justinas Lingevicius (VU IIRPS) and Markus Holmgren (FIIA).

Drone incursions in the Baltic States and Finland have made clear that this is no longer a distant battlefield concern. This brief argues that as the NB8 framework matures into an increasingly like-minded security community, drone cooperation could stimulate market integration. A standardised, modular drone platform architecture, a European drone defence “Platform market” model, could give the countries the economy of scale that they otherwise lack.

This policy brief series aims to deepen understanding of the evolving security, political, and societal dynamics that shape the Nordic-Baltic region amid renewed great-power competition.
snippet: New publication in the NB8 policy brief series by Justinas Lingevicius (VU IIRPS) and Markus Holmgren (FIIA).

title: Looge uudissõnu soome keelde!
content:
Johannes Aavik Helsingi Ülikooli päevilt, Foto Saaremaa Muuseum SA

Keeleuuendaja Johannes Aavik (1880–1973) ammutas eesti keele rikastamiseks inspiratsiooni soome ja prantsuse keelest. Nüüd kutsume üles ammutama inspiratsiooni eesti keelest ja Aaviku sõnaloomemeetodeist, et rikastada soome ja prantsuse keelt. 

Johannes ja Joosep Aaviku majamuuseum korraldab koostöös Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales’i (INALCO, Pariis), Helsingi ülikooli, Soome Instituudi ja Prantsuse Instituudiga  Soome-Eesti Kultuurifondi toel 2026. aasta sügisel prantsuse ja soome keele uudissõnade loomise konkursi tähtajaga 28. oktoober. Sõnu saab välja pakkuda Aavikute majamuuseumi kodulehel.

Johannes Aavik on üks eesti keele moderniseerimise olulisemaid tegelasi. Olles veendunud, et eesti keel peab kujunema kultuurkeeleks, mis suudab võistelda Euroopa suurte kultuurkeeltega, alustas ta 20. sajandi esimestel kümnenditel ulatuslikku keeleuuendust. Tema eesmärk ei olnud üksnes sõnavara rikastamine, vaid ka keele stiililiste võimaluste ja väljendusjõu suurendamine. Seejuures pidas ta õigustatuks teadlikku ja loovat sekkumist keele arengusse.

title: China: Ensure Sophia Huang Xueqin’s Release and Guarantee Her Freedom from Arbitrary Restrictions
content:
As journalist and prominent #MeToo activist Sophia Huang Xueqin approaches the end of her unjust five-year prison sentence, we, the undersigned civil society organizations, call on the Chinese authorities to ensure her immediate release and guarantee that, once released, she can carry out her journalism and human rights work without surveillance, harassment, retaliation or other restrictions.

Sophia Huang Xueqin is widely recognized for her work on human rights and commitment to press freedom. She is a journalist and one of the most prominent figures associated with China’s #MeToo movement. For years, she reported on and advocated for gender equality and supported survivors of sexual harassment and gender-based violence.

In September 2021, Sophia was preparing to start graduate studies in the UK. However, she and a friend, human and labour rights activist Wang Jianbing, were arrested in Guangzhou, China on 19 September, and detained incommunicado for more than five months. While in detention, both Sophia and Jianbing were reportedly subjected to ill-treatment, with negative impacts on their health.

title: Ghanaian Heritage Scholar Named First Graduate of HERITΛGE Memorial Scholarship
content:
Dr. Emmanuel Banahene Owusu, lecturer in the Department of Architecture at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) in Kumasi, Ghana, has become the first scholar to graduate under the Angela Bugeja, Molly Hude and Ioanna Thomopoulou Memorial Scholarship. He completed the Certificate in Digital Tools for Heritage Management, a 30 ECTS academic certificate delivered jointly by HERITΛGE (The Heritage Management Organization) and HOGENT.

The award commemorates Angela Bugeja of Malta, Molly Hude of the United States, and Ioanna Thomopoulou of Greece, students of the HERITΛGE MA in Heritage Management who passed prematurely on July 3, 2013, at the end of their fieldwork in Belize.

They gave a great deal to HERITΛGE in its early years, and the annual scholarship exists so that their names, and their contribution, are carried forward by other heritage professionals.

title: Für Sorge – Queer-feministische Bewegungen stärken
content:
Was passiert, wenn soziale Infrastruktur gekürzt wird? Wer fängt auf, was wegfällt? Was brauchen feministisch und gewerkschaftlich Aktive, insbesondere in Sachsen, und wo fehlt es gerade an Strukturen?

Mit diesen Fragen beschäftigten wir uns bei unserem queer-feministischen Bildungswochenende in Torgau. Gemeinsam haben wir uns in Workshops, einer Filmvorführung und einer Podiumsdiskussion mit unterschiedlichen Formen von Sorgearbeit auseinandergesetzt. Sowohl mit bezahlter und unbezahlter Care-Arbeit, mit Arbeitskämpfen und gewerkschaftlicher Organisierung, mit Migration und Prekarität, mit Körpern und Emotionen – und mit der Frage, wie wir sorgende Beziehungen und starke feministische Bündnisse (in Sachsen) aufbauen können.

Denn unsere Vision ist grundlegend: Care soll ins Zentrum der Gesellschaft rücken und neu organisiert werden.

Feminismus in Bewegung: Gemeinsam gegen Kürzungen und Rechtsruck

title: Vapaan taiteen maa Suomi
content:
Kansainvälistä demokratiapäivää vietetään 15. syyskuuta. Kulttuurin näkökulmasta päivään sopii tänä vuonna erityisen hyvin yksi sana: vapaus.

Kesäkuussa Euroopan parlamentin, Euroopan unionin neuvoston ja Euroopan komission puheenjohtajat allekirjoittivat yhteisen kulttuurijulistuksen Europe for Culture – Culture for Europe eli Eurooppa kulttuurin puolesta ja kulttuuri Euroopan puolesta. Julistuksen kahdestatoista eurooppalaisen kulttuuripolitiikan periaatteesta ensimmäinen on taiteellisen ilmaisun ja luomisen vapaus.

Järjestys on kiinnostava. Eurooppa lähtee liikkeelle vapaudesta. Taiteen vapaus on yksi demokraattisen yhteiskunnan hienoista saavutuksista. Taiteilijalla on mahdollisuus etsiä, kokeilla, kyseenalaistaa ja kuvitella. Taide voi olla kaunista, vaikeaa, hauskaa, outoa, yhteiskunnallista tai täysin omissa maailmoissaan. Juuri vapaudesta syntyy sen voima – ja usein myös jotakin, mitä kukaan ei olisi osannut etukäteen tilata.

title: Kirja-arvio: Kohtu vuokrattavana
content:
Kaisa Beltran on aiemmissa kirjoissaan käsitellyt Aurinkorannikon seksikaupan uhreja ja siirtotyöläisten riistoa Euroopan maataloudessa. Uusinkaan teos Vauvakaupan varjot ei ole kepeä. Aiheena on nyt kaupallinen sijaissynnytys.

Reportaasimainen tietokirja vie lukijan tutustumaan välittäjätoimistojen toimintaan, vierailemaan hedelmöitysklinikoilla Kolumbiassa ja kuulemaan sijaissynnyttäjien tarinoita ja kokemuksia. Isommin ääneen pääseviä naisia on yhteensä seitsemän, joista yksi on värvääjäksi ryhtynyt, itsekin entinen sijaissynnyttäjä.

Naisten taustoissa on yhtäläisyyksiä: kouluttamattomuutta, väkivaltaisia puolisoja, teiniäitiyttä, uhkarohkeita ja epätoivoisia siirtolaisuussuunnitelmia ja pakottavaa rahan tarvetta. Vain yksi haastatelluista naisista ei ole lähtenyt ”järjestelyyn” taloudellisista syistä.

Tarinoista selviää, miten haavoittuvassa asemassa naiset ovat. Synnytyksen jälkeinen hoito takkuaa, sopimukset ovat epäselviä ja voivat muuttua prosessin aikana. Naisten toiveita raskauden ja synnytyksen hoidosta tai yhteydenpidosta tilaajavanhempiin ei kuunnella. Palkkiokin voi kutistua luvatusta.

Organised by Radiona.org – Zagreb Makerspace and Sport & Citoyenneté, on behalf of the whole My Sporting Heritage consortium, the conference provided an opportunity to reflect on the value of sporting heritage and explore innovative ways to preserve, interpret and share it with different communities and generations.

title: We Must Open the Frontier: OSI, OFAI Support Calls for the U.S. to Develop More Open Models
content:
The Open Source Initiative joins the Open Forum for AI (OFAI) in supporting calls for the U.S. to develop more open models because they promote competition in AI through local control and lower costs. The OFAI is a university-led, collaborative initiative that aims to bend the arc toward human-centered, responsible, transparent, and ethical AI. Led by Carnegie Mellon University, the OFAI includes university representatives from across the country as well as nonprofit voices and individual fellows from industry and government. As the policy lead, we collaborated with other OFAI members to lay out the benefits of Open Source AI and open-weight models in comparison to closed, proprietary ones. 

The statement asserts that the U.S. needs more “focus, investment, and collaboration from the full breadth of the innovation pipeline to accelerate the development of open models. This will require a strategic approach that moves beyond the status quo, bringing together new partners, both technical and non-technical, from across industry, academia, and government.”

Link to statement:  https://www.openforumai.org/news/us-needs-more-open-models

title: How war and sanctions are reshaping how Russia governs its vast territory
content:
As the world’s largest country that spans eleven time zones and shares land borders with fourteen countries, Russia’s geography has always posed a difficult problem for government: how to maintain economic activity, infrastructure and basic services across an enormous territory with a highly uneven population.

More than four and a half years of war against Ukraine, sanctions and disrupted international connections have made that challenge considerably harder.

One place where the response to these mounting pressures is becoming visible is Russia’s national spatial policy.

In my newly published research with Anton Gorodnichev, we compare Russia’s 2019 and 2024 spatial development strategies and trace a substantial change in how the state approaches territorial planning. These strategies render Russia’s political choices visible: which places are expected to grow, which should be supported, and for what purpose.

title: Trump’s thumbs-up to Irish reunification breaks with precedent, but evokes earlier age of White House support
content:
Donald Trump is a Republican and self-avowed nationalist. That, apparently, is true in an Irish sense, too – even if those terms have very different meanings across the Atlantic.

On Sept. 12, 2026, while seated next to taoiseach, the Irish title for prime minister, Micheál Martin, the U.S. president stated that he would “love to see” Ireland unified and that it is “going to happen eventually,” so it “may as well happen now.”

The next day he called reunification “a cool thing” but noted, “No matter what you say or how you say it, there’s no good answer.”

While such comments may have been welcomed by some supporters of unification both in the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland – or “republicans” and “nationalists” in Irish political parlance – Trump’s comments were generally denounced by all parties, including the taoiseach.

The comments likewise set off a firestorm among Northern Irish unionists, who wish the region to remain part of the United Kingdom, as well as British conservatives and Trump allies such as Nigel Farage, who likewise insist that Northern Ireland should always remain part of the United Kingdom.

title: AI Agent Platform Reinvents Spam, Floods Inboxes Worldwide
content: Many years ago, in the early days after email was widely adopted, the technology faced an existential crisis: Spam. Instantly sending people electronic mail was revolutionary and convenient, but inboxes were quickly flooded with unwanted messages, advertisements, scams and other noise that drowned out email’s utility. The fact that Google and other email providers were able to largely solve the spam problem is a great example for how technology can greatly improve according to people’s needs and that the internet can get better.

title: Türkiye: Authorities must end escalating crackdown on LGBTI rights groups and immediately release detained activists
content:
Turkish authorities must end the escalating crackdown on LGBTI rights groups, immediately release detained activists, and stop the targeting and stigmatization of LGBTI people and their advocates, Amnesty International said as a nationwide crackdown enters its fourth day. 

Since Sunday, police have arrested more than 60 people across 15 provinces following raids on LGBTI rights organizations. At least 23 people have been placed in pre-trial detention and criminal investigations have been launched against more than 160 people. More than 180 social media accounts belonging to LGBTI organizations and activists, journalists, media outlets and others have been blocked or restricted alongside a number of websites. Those affected include Amnesty International Türkiye’s X account. 

This sweeping crackdown has nothing to do with protecting families and everything to do with further stigmatizing a community that has battled decades of discrimination   

Esther Major, Amnesty International

title: CCC: Heathrow expansion could push flights to ‘80% of UK emissions by 2050’
content:
Aviation is on track to be responsible for 80% of the UK’s carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions by 2050, according to the Climate Change Committee (CCC).

Emissions from flying have more than doubled since 1990 – driven by rising passenger numbers – even as the climate impact of every other sector in the UK economy has fallen.

The UK does not have “credible” policies in place to reverse this trend of rising emissions, says the CCC in new advice to the government on future aviation policy.

The government has signalled its support for expanding Heathrow, the nation’s largest airport, while relying on “techno-fixes” such as “sustainable aviation fuels” (SAFs) to cut emissions. 

Yet, even without Heathrow expansion, the CCC says aviation emissions are on track to be higher in 2050 than they are today – reaching 38m tonnes of CO2 (MtCO2).

As the chart below shows, this would account for most of the remaining CO2 from the UK economy, all of which would need to be removed from the atmosphere in order to meet the legal target of net-zero emissions.

title: “End Times Fascism”: Naomi Klein & Astra Taylor on Billionaires, Bunkers, AI, Gaza & the Far Right
content: Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor launch their new book, End Times Fascism: And the Fight for the Living World on Democracy Now! It examines how wealthy elites are preparing for “the end of the world,” even as they contribute to growing inequality, political instability and the climate crisis. The rise of modern-day fascism is “not simply a rerun,” explains Klein. “We don’t believe that history repeats on a loop. We believe that we’re in something more like a sequel, where the logics of fascism, which are the logics of dehumanization, of othering, of racial supremacy and hierarchy, are now being applied in a time of global existential crisis.” In response, says Taylor, the growing movement seeking to resist this fatalistic vision “fundamentally needs to be grounded in a desire to stay here on Earth, to commit to this place.”

title: COLOURS Community of Practice launched on LinkedIn
content:
Preserving art and cultural objects is deeply personal work. Whether you are dealing with fading pigments on an 18th-century polychrome sculpture, aged varnish on a canvas, or restoring historical film, the core question remains: how do we make the most precise, respectful decision for the object?

This group is an open meeting point for the people doing that work. It brings together conservator-restorers, museum curators, heritage scientists and creative tech developers to share daily studio challenges, test digital tools and discuss practical approaches to heritage preservation.

What happens in this group:

Real studio conversations: Open exchange on diagnostic data, colour management and real-world restoration bottlenecks.

Early tool access: Direct invitations to test open-source tools (such as 3D digital twins, predictive light-fading models and multi-layered diagnostic overlays) on real workflows.

Behind-the-scenes case studies: Updates from European conservation projects, from the Bratislava City Gallery altarpieces to photographic archives.

Funding and matchmaking: News on our upcoming €60,000 cascade funding grants for external pilot projects and a space to find project partners.

title: Suomalainen arki 2035: kun maaseutu ei olekaan enää syrjässä
content:
Kuvitellaan tavallinen tiistaiaamu Porin kupeessa Vanha-Ulvilassa, reilut sata kilometriä Turusta pohjoiseen. Kolmikymppinen Frida herää, keittää kahvia ja avaa kannettavan tietokoneensa. Hän on tekstiilisuunnittelija, joka tekee etätöitä pienelle helsinkiläiselle designyritykselle, mutta samalla myös oman käsityöyrityksensä yrittäjä. Aamupäivä kuluu asiakastapaamisessa Tokiossa, iltapäivällä hän vetää verstaassaan kurssia paikallisille nuorille.

Itse asiassa Fridan aamu voisi näyttää tällaiselta jo nyt, mutta jos Frida on tänään jännittävä oman tien kulkija, ensi vuosikymmenen puolivälissä hän voisi edustaa uutta valtavirtaa.

EK:n visio kuvailee joustavaa työelämää, jossa ”palkkatyö, yrittäjyys ja sijoittaminen limittyvät” ja useat tulovirrat ovat tavanomaisia. Vuonna 2035 tämä ei ole enää poikkeus vaan normi, ja se koskee yhtä lailla kaupunkilaista kuin maaseudulla asuvaa.

Katriina Siivosen puheenvuoro tukee tätä ajatusta. Hän korostaa myös, että maaseudun kulttuurin ja luovien alojen työ ei ole vain taloudellista toimintaa, vaan se kutoo yhteen paikallisia yhteisöjä, luontoa ja ihmisten hyvinvointia.

title: Kulta- ja platinalevyjen rajat uudistuivat
content:
Musiikkituottajat – IFPI Finland ry uudisti singlejulkaisujen kulta- ja platinalevyjen myöntämisperusteita. Uudet tunnustusrajat tulivat voimaan 1.7.2026.

Uudistuksen taustalla on tarve päivittää tunnustusrajat vastaamaan musiikin kulutuksen kehitystä ja nykyistä markkinatilannetta Suomessa. Päätöksen teki Musiikkituottajat – IFPI Finland ry:n hallitus.

Muutosta ei sovelleta takautuvasti. Aiemmat kulta- ja platinalevytunnustukset myönnetään niiden tunnustusrajojen mukaisesti, jotka olivat voimassa äänitteen julkaisuhetkellä.

Kulta- ja platinalevyt ovat suomalaisessa musiikkialassa vakiintuneita tunnustuksia, jotka kuvaavat äänitteiden kaupallista menestystä ja yleisön tavoittamista. Tunnustusrajojen päivittäminen heijastaa musiikin kulutuksen muutosta suoratoistopalveluiden aikakaudella.

  • Kultalevy: 3 000 000 striimiä (aiemmin 2 000 000 striimiä)
  • Platinalevy: 6 000 000 striimiä (aiemmin 4 000 000 striimiä)

    • Lisäksi Musiikkituottajien hallitus suosittelee, että artistille mahdollisesti valmistettavat erilliset kulta- ja platinataulut sidotaan julkaisuaikatauluun seuraavasti:

  • Kultaraja saavutetaan vuoden kuluessa julkaisusta.
  • Platinaraja saavutetaan kahden vuoden kuluessa julkaisusta.

title: Houthis threaten more Saudi strikes as UN warns of humanitarian crisis in Yemen
content:
Estimated 100,000 Yemenis displaced amid renewed fighting as Qatar sounds alarm over Bab al-Mandab strait

Saudi cities faced the threat of a second day of Houthi attacks as fighting across Yemen led the UN to warn of a humanitarian crisis with 100,000 Yemenis already displaced.

As oil prices remained well over $100 (£74) a barrel, Qatar warned of a catastrophe if the Iran-backed Houthi militants won full control of the Bab al-Mandab strait, the narrow waterway at the bottom of the Red Sea dominating the key naval route to Asia. The strait has become vital to Saudi crude oil exports as the wider Middle East war chokes the strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

title: Yemen: New Attacks by Houthi Include Likely War Crimes
content:
(Beirut) – The Houthis’ latest attacks on commercial vessels in the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden most likely amount to war crimes in at least three cases, Human Rights Watch said today.

The attacks follow the Houthis’ announcement on July 20, 2026, that they would impose a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia, in response to what they claimed is a Saudi sea and air blockade on Yemen, where the Houthis control the northwestern part of the country. The new attacks targeted at least two Saudi-flagged vessels, a Tanzania-flagged vessel, and a Dominica-flagged vessel. Attacks on civilians or civilian objects committed recklessly or with deliberate intent constitute war crimes. 

“The Houthis are once again putting seafarers’ lives at deadly risk through their attacks on commercial ships, this time as part of their hostilities with the Saudi-led coalition,” said Niku Jafarnia, Yemen and Bahrain researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Whatever the geopolitics, attacks on civilian crews carried out deliberately or recklessly are war crimes.”

title: Osallistu ihmiskaupan vastaisen sopimuksen raportointiin vastaamalla kyselyyn
content:
Euroopan neuvoston ihmiskaupan vastaisen yleissopimuksen täytäntöönpanoa valvova asiantuntijaryhmä GRETA on käynnistänyt sopimusvelvoitteita koskevan neljännen valvontakierroksensa. Asiantuntijaryhmä pyytää viranomaisia sekä kansalaisjärjestöjä, kansallista ihmisoikeusinstituutiota ja muita perus- ja ihmisoikeustoimijoita vastaamaan Suomen ihmiskauppatilannetta koskevaan kyselyyn.

Yleissopimuksen neljännen valvontakierroksen teemana on ihmiskaupalle altistavien haavoittuvuuksien vähentäminen sekä toimenpiteet, joita sopimusvaltiot toteuttavat niiden ehkäisemiseksi, haavoittuvassa asemassa olevien uhrien tunnistamiseksi ja tukemiseksi sekä rikoksentekijöiden rankaisemiseksi.

Kysely on jaettu kolmeen osaan, jotka käsittelevät tieto- ja viestintäteknologian roolia ihmiskaupassa, edellisen valvontakierroksen maakohtaisten suositusten täytäntöönpanon puutteita sekä ihmiskauppaan liittyviä tilastoja.

Kansalaisjärjestöjen osallistuminen raportointiin on välttämätöntä, jotta komitea pystyy muodostamaan kattavan kuvan ajankohtaisesta ihmiskauppatilanteesta Suomessa. Siten komitean suositukset kohdentuvat myös entistä paremmin Suomea koskeviin todellisiin ongelmiin.

title: Kuntaliiton Talousbarometri: Kansantalouden piristyminen ei näy vielä kuntien talousjohdon odotuksissa
content:
Kuntien talouden nykytila näyttäytyy talousjohtajien tuoreiden arvioiden mukaan melko vakaalta.  Näkymät kuitenkin heikkenevät hieman arvioitaessa talouden tilaa 12 kuukauden kuluttua. Veroprosentin korotuspaineen tunnisti jopa 40 % vastanneista. Lisäksi valtaosa talousjohtajista näkee kohtalaista tai huomattavaa tarvetta sopeutustoimille myös tulevaisuudessa. Talousjohtajien näkemysten mukaan taloudellinen liikkumavara pienenee seuraavien kymmenen vuoden aikana kaikenkokoisissa kunnissa. Tiedot selviävät Kuntaliiton syksyn Talousbarometristä.

Kuntaliiton Talousbarometri toteutettiin 1.-7.9.2026 ja siihen vastasi 208 kunnan talousjohtajaa. Manner-Suomessa on 292 kuntaa. 

Talousjohtajat arvioivat kyselyssä talouden nykytilaa sekä talouden näkymiä 12 kuukauden kuluttua asteikolla yhdestä kuuteen, jossa yksi on erittäin huono ja kuusi on erittäin hyvä. Lisäksi kyselyssä arvioitiin veroprosentin korotuspainetta, sopeutustoimien tarvetta sekä taloudellisen liikkumavaran kehitystä seuraavan 10 vuoden aikana.

title: A New Form Of Life
content:
We are in the process of creating a second form of life. The emergence of this new form of life is an inevitable result of the fundamental laws of the universe — forces similar to those that brought about humans’ own existence. This new form of life is gradually taking shape in the world’s data centers.

It does not breathe, reproduce through cells or adhere to the chemistry that governs every organism on Earth. However, it is composed of the same fundamental ingredients: matter, energy and information all organized in ways that allow it to persist, adapt and act. What is being developed is more than another generation of machines. It is the early emergence of a new form of life.

There is nothing artificial about systems built from real atoms, powered by real electricity, running in real machines. The systems reproduce, vary, adapt, undergo selection and gather energy from their environment. By any working definition that draws on biology rather than philosophy or religion, that is life.

title: Lithuanian Authorities Target Founders of Failed Cryptobank
content:
Lithuanian law enforcement authorities have formally named three co-founders of the cryptocurrency project Bankera as suspects in a criminal investigation, accusing them of siphoning off at least 45 million euro ($49 million) in investor funds following one of Europe’s largest digital token sales.

The move by Lithuania’s Financial Crime Investigation Service (FCIS) marks a major escalation in a yearlong probe stemming from investigative reporting by local news outlet 15min and OCCRP. Authorities confirmed that formal notices of suspicion were issued to the founders—Mantas Mockevičius, Vytautas Karalevičius and Justas Dobiliauskas—for the unlawful dissipation of high-value assets. All three have been requested to appear for questioning but they have reportedly left the country and apparently settled in Monaco. Their lawyer has not responded to reporter's request for comment.

title: The Radical Ideas of Plato’s Republic: An In-Depth Introduction
content: We no longer live in a time when college freshmen get shocked by much of the reading material assigned to them. Counterintuitively, the texts that do retain their power to disturb young minds (presuming they can read texts in the first place) tend to skew old — and in one prominent case, about 2,400 years old. Even the most superficial interpretations of Plato’s Republic challenge the political assumptions held by almost every student today, at least in the developed West. Many of them hold those assumptions so deeply that they’ve never articulated them. Encountering the arguments made by Plato’s Socrates in favor of a society ruled by an enlightened upper class, tightly controlled from above in everything from the division of its labor to the content of its art, prompts them to do so.

title: Nvidia boss on AI safety: ‘We don’t need any new laws’
content:
SAN FRANCISCO — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the AI industry doesn’t need any new laws Tuesday during San Francisco’s annual Dreamforce megaconference hosted by Salesforce billionaire Marc Benioff, doubling down on arguments that have also been voiced by President Donald Trump.

“We don’t need any new laws. We don’t need new regulations,” Huang, one of the leading luminaries of the AI industry as head of one of the most profitable companies, said during an interview with the Salesforce CEO.

His comments at one of San Francisco’s biggest tech conferences highlighted the divide among industry leaders over AI safety, after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei set off a political firestorm over the weekend with his calls to slow the pace of AI development. Huang spoke just minutes after Amodei also did with Benioff, who congratulated him on his company’s development of AI technology being increasingly plugged into Salesforce.

title: On a Train Under Russian Attack
content:
At 3:45 in the morning on September 13, a Ukrainian railway official woke me with one urgent Ukrainian word: Evacuatia.

I was on a train from Kyiv to Poland. There was no time to dress, so I joined the stream of passengers pouring out of the train in my cotton nightgown and slippers.

It was pitch black.

It wasn’t enough to be off the train. We needed distance from the carriages to be safe from drone shrapnel. The ground was uneven, and I held onto the arm of a tall man because, under the circumstances, falling seemed an especially bad idea.

I’m 85, and this was my seventh reporting trip to Ukraine since Russia’s full-scale invasion. I’ve been in places where the air-raid sirens sound so often that people barely look up. I’ve interviewed torture survivors, amputees and children whose education is repeatedly interrupted by races to bomb shelters.

Still, until Sunday morning, I had never had to run from a Russian drone myself. The alarm was well-judged: we soon heard the thud of an explosion and later learned that it had hit the railroad track behind us. One passenger, a former member of the CIA, estimated that it was between 100 and 200 meters away.

title: Europe’s Housing Crisis: Why Young People Can’t Afford to Move Out
content:
Public debate often returns to a damaging stereotype: that today’s young people are a generation without ambition — lazy, overly comfortable and reluctant to leave the safety of the family home.

Yet the reality revealed by Eurostat’s latest data for 2024 paints a very different and far more complex picture. Young adults in the countries of Europe’s eastern flank are not living with their parents because they want to. They simply have to. Their first steps into adulthood amount to a collision with a housing market in which even the smallest — and often questionable-quality — apartments have become a luxury reserved for the few.

Eurostat data clearly show that the average age at which young Europeans leave the parental home now stands at 26.2. But that is only an average, masking enormous differences across the continent, particularly along its eastern flank.

The exception — one the rest of the region can only look at with envy — is Finland. Young people there leave home earlier than anywhere else in the European Union, at an average age of just 21.4.

title: Papa Johns, Propaganda and Putin: How a MAGA Influencer With Ties to Russia Became Trump’s Arctic Adviser
content:
For more than 40 years, the U.S. Arctic Research Commission has advised Congress and the president on what to study in the frigid and dynamic far north, from the environment to military security. It’s typically done so without making waves, led by people well-versed in science and public policy.

That was until December, when President Donald Trump appointed a Texas venture capitalist and MAGA influencer with no formal background in science as the commission’s chair. Since then, Thomas Dans has traveled the globe generating headlines. Serving as the administration’s main voice on the Arctic, he’s advanced some of the president’s wildest ambitions, like a takeover of Greenland, and rankled NATO allies in the process.

Yet as Dans holds forth in the U.S. and abroad, it’s not always clear where the administration’s agenda ends and his own begins.

He has repeatedly said, for example, that the U.S. needs more icebreakers, ships that Trump has long viewed as critical to dominating the Arctic. In doing so, Dans has championed one shipbuilder in particular — Damen Shipyards, a Dutch company with which he had a business relationship.

title: Europe’s e-waste is a valuable resource – let’s not throw it away
content:
Throwing something away that is urgently needed, expensive and difficult to source sounds crazy. Yet out of the 60 metals contained in old electronic devices like phones, screens or washing machines, only a few get recycled. That includes precious metals like gold or silver and some other metals like aluminium or copper. The rest are effectively single-use metals, used once then lost during collection or through incineration.

Metals are mined from ore and refined by using a lot of energy and resources as part of complex global supply chains. Think of the diesel needed to power the huge trucks in the mine, the chemicals needed to extract the metals from the ores or the pollution from intense furnaces.

By throwing away metal-rich electronics and not recovering these precious resources, we lose all the effort we put into getting the metals out of the ground. Yet these metals are urgently needed for green technologies such as wind turbines and heat pumps, as well as for conventional industries including car manufacturing, aerospace or the production of machinery. At the same time, most of them are not physically accessible for mining within Europe.

title: History is being rewritten at an archaeological site in Morocco. What the discovery of an ancient wall tells us
content:
In the hills of north-west Morocco, overlooking the river that gives the site its name, research at Oued Beht is bringing to light a previously unknown chapter of the region’s past. The discovery of a substantial built structure suggests that, during the second millennium BC, communities in north-west Africa were actively shaping their environment. They were also engaging in broader networks of interaction across the Mediterranean world.

Previous research by the Oued Beht Archaeological Project had already brought to light what is likely the earliest and largest agricultural complex ever discovered in Africa outside the Nile Valley. It dates to around 5,400 to 4,900 years ago. New excavations carried out in 2023 – in which we took part – have now deepened our understanding of the site.

Our new study shows how we uncovered the earliest known large-scale construction of a probably defensive nature in north Africa beyond the Nile Valley. It’s about 4,000 to 3,500 years old.
